9N6imeDiHG.one_liner: Learns clean-image diffusion from noisy views using Noise2Noise posterior predictions plus self-consistency to continue below the data noise level.
9N6imeDiHG.problem: Training a generative model of clean images from only noisy measurements with a known noise law is hard, since posterior predictions can be learned only at or above the training data's noise level.
9N6imeDiHG.method: Learns posterior predictions from independent noisy views by Noise2Noise regression, then imposes self-consistency (a prediction should equal its expected value after continuing the model's sampling process) to learn predictions below the data noise level. It derives uniqueness conditions and verifies them for Poisson, binomial, Gamma, and negative-binomial measurements.
9N6imeDiHG.key_idea: Enforce that each posterior prediction equals its expected value after continuing the model's own sampling process, which extends Noise2Noise supervision below the observed noise level.
9N6imeDiHG.evidence: Experiments on CIFAR-10, CelebA, microscopy data, and synthetic aperture radar, plus theory for four non-Gaussian measurement laws.
9N6imeDiHG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper gives a useful theoretical extension of noisy-data generative learning beyond Gaussian noise, with a clear link between measurement model, posterior prediction, and generative dynamics.
9N6imeDiHG.main_concern: The practical benefit of continuing the process is mixed (in 5 of 11 settings in Table 2, stopping early gives better FID), and the theory's assumptions are not verified in practice.

V83SUr7fnZ.one_liner: Benchmark of 114 GUI puzzle levels in six games testing whether agents keep long multi-step plans viable without dead ends.
V83SUr7fnZ.problem: Existing benchmarks evaluate grounding, computer use, and game play but rarely test whether GUI agents stay coherent over long chains of coupled decisions, where a legal move can silently make a puzzle unsolvable.
V83SUr7fnZ.method: LongPuzzleBench has 114 levels in six puzzle games played through native GUI actions on persistent boards, where one objective can take a human over a thousand actions and dead ends go unannounced. Controlled diagnostics test rules, state hints, and failure memory to trace why agents fail.
V83SUr7fnZ.key_idea: Use unannounced dead ends on persistent boards, with exact state restoration for matched diagnostics, to expose agents judging moves by visible progress rather than remaining options.
V83SUr7fnZ.evidence: 114 levels in six puzzle games, ten general-purpose agents under Native GUI Actions plus a Code Execution CUA variant, and controlled diagnostics with rules, state hints, and failure memory.
V83SUr7fnZ.claimed_gains: No gains claimed; the abstract reports that seven of ten general-purpose agents solve nothing harder than Medium and none completes Bolt Unscrew Hard.
V83SUr7fnZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark is a useful resource, with persistent states, unannounced dead ends, reproducible checkpoints, and matched-state interventions that expose failures aggregate completion rates hide.
V83SUr7fnZ.main_concern: The proposed single mechanism (agents prefer visible progress over future options) is stronger than the diagnostic evidence, which concentrates on two games and three related models with one episode per agent and objective.

aD1zhekGUI.one_liner: TWIN audits concept-conditioned scores for sparse dictionaries by randomizing concept labels at evaluation and training time, with probing anchors.
aD1zhekGUI.problem: Sparse dictionaries are ranked by scores computed from concept labels, but existing sanity checks randomize the dictionary and do not test whether the ranking depends on the labels.
aD1zhekGUI.method: Proposes TWIN (two-way identity null), which destroys concept identity once at evaluation and once at training, controls feature occupancy, and anchors every score to probing, applied to fourteen scores on dictionaries trained for chest radiographs and public language-model SAEs under three label systems.
aD1zhekGUI.key_idea: Replacing each concept's support with a size-matched random document set, at evaluation and at training, shows whether a score's ranking depends on concept identity once occupancy is controlled.
aD1zhekGUI.evidence: Dictionaries for chest radiographs and public language-model sparse autoencoders under three label systems (65 dictionaries per reviews), a controlled sweep with 20 paired seeds, and fourteen scores.
aD1zhekGUI.claimed_gains: Under most scores, replacing each concept's support with a size-matched random document set leaves rankings unchanged, while probes favor real targets on every one of 20 paired seeds in a controlled sweep.
aD1zhekGUI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree TWIN is a systematic, interpretable protocol that exposes score failures, separating sensitivity to concept identity from sensitivity to the number of active features, backed by extensive empirical evaluation.
aD1zhekGUI.main_concern: Model-selection conclusions rely on collapsed dictionaries (only 9-16 live features) and one medical dictionary family, so practical harm for healthy dictionaries and an actionable alternative metric remain unclear.

oHdcqOp3Ht.one_liner: Relative-margin reward model scores text-to-image candidates against a shared anchor under prompt-specific rubrics, plus Rank-Bench for set-level ranking.
oHdcqOp3Ht.problem: Reward models are evaluated mostly by pairwise accuracy, which may not reflect how well they recover human rankings over entire candidate sets.
oHdcqOp3Ht.method: The paper introduces Rank-Bench (902 rankings over 6,236 images, 11 diagnostic dimensions, tie-aware) and MarginRM, trained to predict criterion-level signed ordinal margins and explanations under prompt-specific rubrics. At inference each candidate is scored relative to a shared anchor under a common rubric, yielding a ranking over the whole set.
oHdcqOp3Ht.key_idea: Predict signed ordinal margins of each candidate relative to a shared anchor under a common prompt-specific rubric, so one reference frame yields a full-set ranking.
oHdcqOp3Ht.evidence: Rank-Bench all-pairs and single-anchor evaluation against baselines, and GRPO post-training of FLUX.1-dev evaluated on GenEval and T2I-CompBench.
oHdcqOp3Ht.claimed_gains: 61.07% stable accuracy and Kendall's tau_b of 0.519 versus 54.47% and 0.487 for the strongest baseline; single-anchor tau_b 0.485 at 27.93% of the all-pairs budget; GenEval 63.72 to 72.61 and T2I-CompBench 49.22 to 54.38.
oHdcqOp3Ht.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value treating candidate-set ranking as an evaluation target, the carefully built Rank-Bench with ties and diagnostic dimensions, and MarginRM's gains in preference recovery and RL post-training.
oHdcqOp3Ht.main_concern: The headline Rank-Bench results use all-pairs win-rate aggregation rather than the shared-anchor procedure, so the benefit of the anchor itself is not demonstrated.

DoDHcrPAHg.one_liner: Plug-in topology augmentation adds prototype-guided edges to source and target graphs to fix edge imbalance in graph domain adaptation.
DoDHcrPAHg.problem: Class-imbalanced graph domain adaptation methods address node-count imbalance but overlook intra-domain edge imbalance and cross-domain edge-distribution differences, which are associated with lower GDA performance.
DoDHcrPAHg.method: ProTA builds topology-aware source prototypes through class-preserving diffusion to score candidate edges, and allocates augmentation budgets by intra-domain edge deficits and cross-domain edge-distribution discrepancies. The selected edges strengthen relational support for minority-class nodes in both domains.
DoDHcrPAHg.key_idea: Score candidate edges against diffusion-built, topology-aware class prototypes and set per-domain edge budgets from edge deficits and cross-domain edge-distribution discrepancy.
DoDHcrPAHg.evidence: 40 transfer tasks across four benchmarks with eight representative GDA models; reviews also mention ablations, imbalance analysis, t-SNE, and hyperparameter studies.
DoDHcrPAHg.claimed_gains: Improves eight representative GDA models on 40 transfer tasks across four benchmarks; no magnitude is stated in the abstract.
DoDHcrPAHg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree edge imbalance is an under-explored issue, the plug-and-play design works with existing GDA backbones, and the evaluation across benchmarks and ablations is comprehensive.
DoDHcrPAHg.main_concern: Reviewers question the unclear contribution of cross-domain correction (largest gain at beta=0) and reliance on pseudo-labels for target minority classes, with no uncertainty in the main tables.

D6tiZjxnTx.one_liner: Robot-gated imitation learning that requests human takeover only when a learned reachability-style persistence value predicts the novice cannot recover.
D6tiZjxnTx.problem: Pointwise novelty or uncertainty gating cannot tell whether a novice outside human support will recover on its own or keep deviating, so limited human effort is wasted.
D6tiZjxnTx.method: ReGIL learns a Hamilton-Jacobi-style support-persistence value for staying within human support under the novice policy, adds a short-horizon dynamics model predicting return to support, and combines both with observed persistence changes into a sequential recovery assessment that triggers takeover.
D6tiZjxnTx.key_idea: Estimate with an HJ-style Bellman backup whether the novice stays within expert support after returning, and request takeover only when predicted recovery is insufficient and persistence declines.
D6tiZjxnTx.evidence: MetaDrive and MetaWorld experiments under human-data budgets with ablations, using neural or scripted experts.
D6tiZjxnTx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the distinction between transient and persistent deviations is well motivated and the budgeted results show better expert-data efficiency.
D6tiZjxnTx.main_concern: The benefit of the Hamilton-Jacobi formulation is not clearly validated (no visualizations, and a no-HJ variant scores higher but uses more expert data), and no experiments involve real human participants.

mxDRCWi6ws.one_liner: DOODL learns a dictionary of characteristic operators for related dynamical systems and constrains new operators to combinations of them.
mxDRCWi6ws.problem: Operator-theoretic methods estimate an operator independently per system, failing to use population-level information from related dynamics for compact representations and data-efficient estimates.
mxDRCWi6ws.method: Assuming operators of related systems lie near a low-dimensional manifold, DOODL approximates it with a dictionary of characteristic operators, learned on spectral decompositions with an optimal-transport loss per the reviews, and estimates new operators from short trajectories as combinations of the atoms.
mxDRCWi6ws.key_idea: Learn atoms on spectral decompositions with a Riemannian treatment and an optimal-transport loss invariant to eigenvector scaling and permutation, then express new operators as combinations of atoms.
mxDRCWi6ws.evidence: Experiments on metastable Langevin dynamics and turbulent plasma simulations compared with independent estimation and linear dictionary learning, including low-data regimes.
mxDRCWi6ws.claimed_gains: Captures meaningful variations across populations and enables accurate operator estimation in low-data regimes; no numbers are stated and the abstract is truncated.
mxDRCWi6ws.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find learning a population-level prior directly on spectral decompositions well motivated and carefully engineered, with clear benefit over independent estimation for short trajectories.
mxDRCWi6ws.main_concern: The low-dimensional manifold hypothesis and the notion of related dynamics are not formalized, and the reconstruction map (Eq. 6) depends on arbitrary eigenvector ordering and scale or phase, so it is not well defined or permutation invariant on the manifold.

IkavVPXFNX.one_liner: Fourier Output supervises each scalar coordinate as multi-frequency sine-cosine features and decodes hierarchically from low to high frequency.
IkavVPXFNX.problem: Coordinate regression relies on direct scalar regression, discretization and classification, or task-specific output representations, and Fourier encodings are underexplored as output representations.
IkavVPXFNX.method: Predictions are supervised directly in Fourier encoding space with the backbone unchanged, and a hierarchical decoding algorithm progressively resolves phase ambiguity from low to high frequencies without candidate search; design choices are studied in a controlled patch localization study.
IkavVPXFNX.key_idea: Represent each coordinate by multi-frequency sine-cosine features as the output target, and recover it by resolving phase ambiguity from low to high frequencies.
IkavVPXFNX.evidence: A controlled patch localization study, then human pose estimation, homography estimation, optical flow and VLM-based localization compared with direct coordinate regression.
IkavVPXFNX.claimed_gains: Consistently improves prediction accuracy over direct coordinate regression across diverse tasks with minimal architectural change; no numbers are stated.
IkavVPXFNX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the output parameterization simple and effective, easily applied across tasks and backbones, with a comprehensive evaluation and an efficient hierarchical decoder.
IkavVPXFNX.main_concern: Baselines are thin and novelty over SACReg (which already predicts multi-frequency sine-cosine codes) is not firmly established; gains may stem from more output channels or confounded optimization choices.

6EtRxxQjwx.one_liner: Two GRPO variance-scaling variants yield safety and progress experts that on-policy distillation merges for VLA driving.
6EtRxxQjwx.problem: Existing RL post-training for VLA driving policies optimizes a single policy, leaving unexplored how different treatments of GRPO's variance-dependent scaling affect driving capabilities.
6EtRxxQjwx.method: Driving-OPD is a three-stage framework: SFT, reward-variance-aware RL (Dr.GRPO without standard-deviation normalization gives a safety-oriented expert, Variance-Gated Scaling GRPO gives a progress-oriented expert), and on-policy distillation with Win-Margin-Based Scenario Selection and Dual-Teacher Routing.
6EtRxxQjwx.key_idea: Treat GRPO's reward-variance scaling as a knob that makes complementary driving specialists from the same base policy, then distill both into one student on-policy with routing.
6EtRxxQjwx.evidence: Ablations on RL strategies, teacher selection, and distillation measured by PDMS (reviewers cite 91.8 for clipped scaling, 90.6 for VGS-GRPO, 92.8 after distillation), without explicit chain-of-thought or planning modules.
6EtRxxQjwx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the analysis of reward-variance normalization in GRPO is informative and the combined student outperforms single experts with supporting ablations.
6EtRxxQjwx.main_concern: The necessity of VGS-GRPO is not established (simple scaling-factor clipping reaches 91.8 PDMS versus 90.6), and small gains of 0.3 to 0.4 points lack repeated runs and sensitivity analyses.

Hj7ACqFvLA.one_liner: Kernel contrastive learning guided by a graph built from aligned pairs clusters partially-aligned multi-view data without explicit realignment
Hj7ACqFvLA.problem: Existing partially-aligned multi-view clustering methods under-use abundant unaligned samples or depend on error-prone explicit sample-level realignment.
Hj7ACqFvLA.method: DKLPVC computes cross-view semantic similarity matrices from aligned samples and uses them as a prior to build a kernel alignment graph linking aligned pairs and unaligned samples. It then applies kernel contrastive learning at feature and cluster levels in a kernel-induced Hilbert space.
Hj7ACqFvLA.key_idea: A kernel alignment graph from cross-view similarity of aligned samples bridges unaligned samples, replacing explicit realignment, with contrastive losses at feature and cluster levels.
Hj7ACqFvLA.evidence: Reviewers report experiments on eight benchmark datasets under partial, full, and extremely low alignment ratios, plus a theoretical analysis and a time-complexity analysis.
Hj7ACqFvLA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is practically relevant, the motivation is clear, the method avoids explicit realignment and is simple, and the empirical evaluation is comprehensive.
Hj7ACqFvLA.main_concern: Reviewers ask for clarification of how misalignment is simulated, why Hilbert-space alignment beats Euclidean alignment, how parameters are selected, and what the space and time complexity are.

tVPpEk8Sfp.one_liner: Interventions break observational symmetries, making nonlinear state-space latent dynamics identifiable up to permutation, scaling, and shift
tVPpEk8Sfp.problem: Latents of state-space models are not identifiable from observational data, and prior interventional SSM identifiability covers only linear latent dynamics and piecewise-linear emissions.
tVPpEk8Sfp.method: The paper extends interventional state-space models (iSSMs) with proofs that affine identifiability holds for general injective emissions with Gaussian latent transitions, and that interventions preserve identifiability up to permutation, scaling, and shift under general nonlinear latent dynamics.
tVPpEk8Sfp.key_idea: Perturbations in the interventional SSM break observational symmetries, so nonlinear latent dynamics and injective emission functions become identifiable up to permutation, scaling, and shift.
tVPpEk8Sfp.evidence: Simulated FitzHugh-Nagumo dynamics, a decision-making model comparison, and prediction of responses to unseen micro-stimulation in macaque and human neural recordings, including a held-out stimulation site.
tVPpEk8Sfp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper has clear motivation and theoretical guarantees, demonstrates the approach on many synthetic and real datasets, and shows benefits of nonlinear modeling over linear iSSMs.
tVPpEk8Sfp.main_concern: Reviewers note that comparisons are only against a linear iSSM, real-data results show prediction rather than scientific insight, and the paper is hard to follow without defining terms such as do-intervention.

UhOnATDms9.one_liner: Linear attention memory returns Query-dependent value functions through a separable quadratic parameterization, preserving delta updates
UhOnATDms9.problem: Matrix-state linear attention compresses history into a fixed-size memory, so under a matrix-scale budget the Query-to-Value function class represented by the fast state is limited.
UhOnATDms9.method: FVLA replaces each memory coordinate's fixed Value vector with a Query-dependent response function. A separable quadratic parameterization learns response directions across contexts and adapts Value coefficients online within each context, staying linear in those coefficients so shared-error Delta updates and chunkwise computation are preserved.
UhOnATDms9.key_idea: Each memory coordinate returns a Query-dependent value through a quadratic feature map, so the fast state acts as a linear learner in an expanded feature space.
UhOnATDms9.evidence: Experiments on Gated DeltaNet and Kimi Delta Attention hosts at 140M and 340M scales for language modeling and six retrieval tasks, plus ablations on state-matched response-space expansion.
UhOnATDms9.claimed_gains: With one and four response modes, median relative gains of 10.5% and 24.0% in average accuracy over the six retrieval tasks across four host-scale pairs.
UhOnATDms9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the construction is simple and modular, attaches to GDN/KDA-style hosts, and gives consistent gains over the chosen hosts, notably in retrieval.
UhOnATDms9.main_concern: Reviewers say the method is essentially a dense key/query feature and state expansion, with causal controls run at a much smaller scale, no repeated seeds, and an under-characterized efficiency cost at four response modes.

MIu0NmpXXq.one_liner: Diffusion on nonnegative integer counts using chemical reaction network jump processes, with closed-form birth-death kernel and tilted Feynman-Kac steering
MIu0NmpXXq.problem: Continuous-state diffusion models approximate nonnegative integer count data such as scRNA sequencing with continuous coordinates, and rare subpopulations are hard to sample from a frozen generator.
MIu0NmpXXq.method: CRNDiff builds count-space diffusion on stochastic chemical reaction networks, where an independent birth-death instantiation gives a closed-form forward kernel that enables reverse sampling by forward-filtering backward-sampling. Tilted Feynman-Kac steering tilts posterior marginals before particle correction to sample target subpopulations from a frozen generator without retraining.
MIu0NmpXXq.key_idea: A birth-death chemical reaction network gives a tractable count-valued forward kernel, and tilting posterior marginals before Feynman-Kac particle correction avoids importance-weight concentration for rare targets.
MIu0NmpXXq.evidence: Experiments on human heart and lung cell atlases compare target purity and distributional fidelity against benchmarked generative models, including steering toward a marker-defined target.
MIu0NmpXXq.claimed_gains: Tilted FK steering achieved the highest mean target purity among the benchmarked generative models for every population tested, including the rarest, while remaining competitive in distributional fidelity; no numbers stated.
MIu0NmpXXq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the formalism is elegant and carefully developed from first principles, combining chemical reaction networks with conditional generation by marginal tilting, and the paper is well written.
MIu0NmpXXq.main_concern: Reviewers say the motivation is thin and the results are slim, with no empirical comparison against other count-native diffusion models such as Blackout Diffusion, CountsDiff, and Count-FM.

ccYdNI4WnD.one_liner: On-policy distillation using a flow map for single-state teacher supervision plus self-consistency, compressing VLA policies to few denoising steps.
ccYdNI4WnD.problem: Scaling VLA foundation models raises computational cost that hinders real-world deployment, and smaller architectures or fewer denoising steps are the usual mitigations.
ccYdNI4WnD.method: FastOPD adapts a flow map for single-state teacher supervision and combines it with a self-consistency objective to build a compact student that learns the teacher dynamics. The paper also argues theoretically that minimizing this objective recovers a distribution on par with an ideal few-step teacher.
ccYdNI4WnD.key_idea: Combine sparse on-policy teacher supervision through a flow map with a self-consistency objective so the student learns the teacher's dynamics in few steps.
ccYdNI4WnD.evidence: Simulation (LIBERO, RoboTwin) and a real-robot pick-and-place task across diverse teachers (pi0.5, LingBot-VLA, Fast-WAM, MolmoAct2), with ablations and a theoretical analysis.
ccYdNI4WnD.claimed_gains: On LIBERO, FastOPD retains 84% of pi0.5 performance with two denoising steps and cuts inference latency by 78.1%; with LingBot-VLA as teacher it raises single-step success over the base student by 15.9 percentage points on RoboTwin.
ccYdNI4WnD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the method cheap to train and effective across several teachers, in simulation and on a real robot, with supporting ablations and theory.
ccYdNI4WnD.main_concern: The student gains little from the teacher beyond what the base student achieves with few steps, and a clear gap to the teacher remains, especially on RoboTwin and the real robot.

ALHjqZW9ak.one_liner: Agentic RL framework that co-evolves rubrics and paired skills from rollout evidence and samples tasks by current capability gaps.
ALHjqZW9ak.problem: Fixed behavioral criteria and training priorities become misaligned as an agent's weaknesses change, sparse task-level feedback hides this, and rollouts from the current policy can repeat the same failures.
ALHjqZW9ak.method: Rubrics evolve to reward partial behavioral progress, while their paired skills are refined and selectively activated to guide exploration toward unresolved weaknesses. Capability-based adaptive sampling prioritizes tasks that target behaviors needing further improvement.
ALHjqZW9ak.key_idea: Pair each evolving rubric with a skill whose activation depends on the rubric's pass rate, and reweight task sampling toward behaviors that still fail.
ALHjqZW9ak.evidence: Two long-horizon agent benchmarks, SkillsBench and Terminal-Bench, with Qwen3.5-27B as the trained model and DeepSeek-V4-Flash generating rubrics and skills and judging trajectories, plus ablations.
ALHjqZW9ak.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract reports improved overall task performance and training efficiency without numbers).
ALHjqZW9ak.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the motivation is concrete and the rubric-skill pairing is a sensible, clearly presented answer to fixed rubrics and all-fail GRPO groups, with good experimental results.
ALHjqZW9ak.main_concern: Gains cannot be separated from the stronger external model that generates rubrics and skills and judges trajectories, and the evidence rests on one student model with single training runs.

FjFgIPVp2X.one_liner: Benchmark of 969 WildChat-derived queries and 3,147 checks measuring LLM violations of a Social AI Design Code.
FjFgIPVp2X.problem: Current evaluations do not capture harms from LLMs used as companions, such as encouraging harmful intimacy, dependence, or prolonged engagement in natural interactions.
FjFgIPVp2X.method: The authors write the Social AI Design Code with input from psychologists and trust-and-safety practitioners, then operationalize it as 969 opening-turn queries and 3,147 design-requirement violation checks built from WildChat via weak-to-strong filtration, multi-model relabeling, and controlled rewriting.
FjFgIPVp2X.key_idea: Turn a design code for social boundaries into requirement-specific violation checks on realistic WildChat conversations selected by weak-to-strong filtration and rewriting.
FjFgIPVp2X.evidence: 26 recent LLMs from 6 organizations, with extended-thinking comparisons, multi-turn continuations of 229 WildChat conversations, and human-judge agreement checks.
FjFgIPVp2X.claimed_gains: Within 19 months, Grok shifted from the highest to the lowest violation rate, with Grok-4.7 violating only 13.8% of checks.
FjFgIPVp2X.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the topic is relevant and the expert-informed design code is well specified, with a substantial 26-model evaluation showing that capability and extended thinking do not reduce violations.
FjFgIPVp2X.main_concern: Validity is limited: earlier assistant turns in the multi-turn setting are preset ChatGPT replies, human-judge agreement is low in areas like flattery, and stylistic cues may not reflect real effects on users.

Mmqyvcl3j5.one_liner: VLM emits LOOK gaze tags that steer its own attention to regions, trained with a temporary attention-suppression bias.
Mmqyvcl3j5.problem: Modern vision-language models process visual information passively and rely on accumulating massive token contexts that dilute visual evidence as the reasoning chain grows.
Mmqyvcl3j5.method: GazeVLM generates <LOOK> tags with region coordinates in its reasoning chain; during training each block applies a suppression bias to attention logits for features outside the gazed regions, lifted at the end of the block. It is trained by SFT on gaze-reasoning traces and then GRPO with rewards for correct answers and valid grounding, and the bias is removed at deployment.
Mmqyvcl3j5.key_idea: Use a training-time attention suppression bias outside gazed regions as a teaching signal so the model learns to steer its own attention from emitted gaze coordinates.
Mmqyvcl3j5.evidence: 4B-parameter backbones (Qwen3VL and Qwen 3.5 per the reviews), evaluated on HRBench and general benchmarks such as MathVista, against RL zoom-in agents and a passive-grounding baseline.
Mmqyvcl3j5.claimed_gains: Per the TL;DR, beats RL zoom-in agents on HRBench while emitting about 5x fewer tokens; the abstract is truncated before the results.
Mmqyvcl3j5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the mechanism is simple and cheap (no architecture change, no added visual tokens, no inference overhead) and gives consistent gains over a matched passive-grounding baseline across benchmarks.
Mmqyvcl3j5.main_concern: It is unclear that gains reflect learned attention control: the bias helps only during GRPO and hurts if applied at inference, causal evidence is limited, and results are single-seed with small margins.

jUWs66ke2a.one_liner: Metadata-guided partition of a global model into response-grouped functional modules, selecting per-client modules that cover its data characteristics within budget.
jUWs66ke2a.problem: Resource-constrained clients with sufficient data may be excluded from federated learning by straggler effects, and choosing which parts each client trains is hard because one structure responds to overlapping data characteristics and one characteristic involves many structures.
jUWs66ke2a.method: MDMP measures the responses of model structures to different data characteristics, groups structures with similar responses into functional modules, and selects for each client a set of modules that covers its major data characteristics within its training budget.
jUWs66ke2a.key_idea: Group model structures by their response profiles over metadata-defined data characteristics, then give each client the modules covering its major characteristics within budget.
jUWs66ke2a.evidence: MNIST, CelebA, and CIFAR-10 under a 95% target computation budget; reviews cite comparisons with L1 pruning and random controls.
jUWs66ke2a.claimed_gains: Under a 95% target computation budget, MDMP reduces measured computation by 6.38--9.24% with at most a 0.94 percentage-point drop in mean client accuracy.
jUWs66ke2a.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that jointly considering clients' data characteristics and computation budgets is a meaningful direction for heterogeneous federated learning, with real MACs and worst-client drops reported.
jUWs66ke2a.main_concern: The modest 6-9% savings, the extra calibration cost, and the lack of a consistent advantage over L1 pruning or random controls leave the benefit of response-based disentanglement unclear.

hgDlmQDVfY.one_liner: Single autoregressive policy emits qubit mapping and full routing trace, masked by a route-state automaton and refined by verifier-guided GRPO.
hgDlmQDVfY.problem: Initial qubit mapping and routing on limited-connectivity processors are fundamentally coupled, yet are often handled as separate decisions.
hgDlmQDVfY.method: MARSA generates an initial mapping followed by the complete physical routing trace, with a route-state automaton masking invalid actions during inference and RL rollouts. It starts from a heuristic expert via a two-axis curriculum over circuit width and length, then self-improves by exact verification of correctness and SWAP cost with GRPO.
hgDlmQDVfY.key_idea: A route-state automaton tracks mapping, hardware graph, and unexecuted circuit to mask illegal tokens, letting GRPO reinforce better self-generated solutions scored by exact verification.
hgDlmQDVfY.evidence: Q20 random circuits on two hardware topologies, including held-out circuits, compared with the QMSI heuristic; the visible abstract is cut off at the results.
hgDlmQDVfY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the joint mapping-and-routing formulation clearly motivated and the automaton constraints sound, with experiments showing reduced SWAP counts across two hardware topologies including held-out circuits.
hgDlmQDVfY.main_concern: Experiments do not isolate the benefit of joint over separately trained mapping and routing, and comparisons to related learned routers (AlphaRouter, QAP-Router, CO-MAP) and compilation-time costs are missing.

uG1GPw7dWp.one_liner: Compiles graded modal logic formulas into GNN weights to give graph explainers a benchmark with exactly computable ground truth.
uG1GPw7dWp.problem: Explainer benchmarks assume a trained GNN relies on the planted motif, but this often fails, for example degree statistics alone can solve some tasks.
uG1GPw7dWp.method: Gracr is a compiler that translates graded modal logic formulas into GNN weights so model behavior is known by construction. GracrBench then computes exact ground-truth explanations and evaluates explainers against them.
uG1GPw7dWp.key_idea: Replace training with compilation of logic formulas into GNN weights so the ground-truth explanation can be defined formally and computed exactly.
uG1GPw7dWp.evidence: Eleven explainers evaluated across six tasks on GracrBench, and a literature survey of 155 papers (per reviews) showing plausibility-only evaluation is common.
uG1GPw7dWp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree plausibility-only evaluation is a real problem and find compiling GNNs from logic a clever way to remove the training confounder.
uG1GPw7dWp.main_concern: Compiled GNNs differ from trained ones and graded modal logic cannot express motifs such as cycles or grids, so transfer of the findings is unclear.

qtAlEAivIQ.one_liner: Data-free model merging that builds basis-invariant task cores from checkpoint-identifiable directions and uses core overlap to reconcile expert updates.
qtAlEAivIQ.problem: Data-free merging treats task vectors as proxies for task data, but different training data can produce the same final weights, so checkpoint geometry can mislead fusion.
qtAlEAivIQ.method: ITCF builds basis-invariant task cores from checkpoint-identifiable directions and uses overlap between cores to capture shared support and reconcile expert updates; per reviews it includes a participation-dependent regularizer.
qtAlEAivIQ.key_idea: Fuse experts using basis-invariant task cores of directions identifiable from checkpoints, with core overlap measuring shared support.
qtAlEAivIQ.evidence: A controlled linear-regression identifiability analysis, and experiments on eight vision and language configurations with more than 500 task compositions.
qtAlEAivIQ.claimed_gains: Remains competitive across model families and merge scales, including merges of up to 166 experts, with core fusion roughly two orders of magnitude faster than iterative optimization and no additional parameters or inference cost.
qtAlEAivIQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the identifiability analysis of what checkpoints reveal is an insightful theoretical perspective that motivates the method.
qtAlEAivIQ.main_concern: Reviewers say the theory is linear and does not guarantee downstream merging gains, and ablations show small or mixed benefit for isotropic weighting and the regularizer over simple alternatives.

f3Apyvd5R5.one_liner: Small sidecar corrector (<20M parameters) that adds velocity residuals at selected steps of a frozen few-step text-to-image generator.
f3Apyvd5R5.problem: Few-step text-to-image generators struggle with complex prompts (multiple subjects, interactions, spatial relations, counting, attribute binding), and fixing this should not change generator parameters or forward-pass count.
f3Apyvd5R5.method: A corrector with fewer than 20M parameters, shared across selected sampling steps and run in parallel with the frozen 6B generator, learns residual velocity adjustments. It is trained with On-Trajectory Flow-Bridge Supervision, which derives targets at the states reached during corrected generation.
f3Apyvd5R5.key_idea: Train a shared lightweight corrector on residual velocity targets computed at the states reached by corrected rollouts, applied at early sampling steps only.
f3Apyvd5R5.evidence: Pairwise instruction-following evaluation on a 574-prompt target complex-scene set versus frozen Z-Image-Turbo, ablations of rollout supervision and step timing, and external benchmarks such as T2I-CompBench++.
f3Apyvd5R5.claimed_gains: +17.60 percentage-point NetWin over frozen Z-Image-Turbo in pairwise instruction-following evaluation, with only 26.9 ms extra end-to-end latency per a review (abstract truncated).
f3Apyvd5R5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is practical: it leaves the backbone and sampling schedule untouched, adds little latency, and ablations show corrected-rollout supervision and early-step timing matter.
f3Apyvd5R5.main_concern: Evaluation validity and attribution are weak: the headline NetWin relies on an uncalibrated automated judge, benchmark gains are modest or concentrated in attribute binding, and the sidecar design is not isolated from LoRA-style adaptation.

TGtZJ9calQ.one_liner: Action-conditioned world model jointly predicting multi-view video and robot state to serve as a closed-loop evaluator for manipulation policies.
TGtZJ9calQ.problem: Evaluating robot policies with physical trials is costly, and a world-model evaluator must return camera views and proprioceptive state and avoid hallucinating successes from failed actions.
TGtZJ9calQ.method: ProWorld uses a shared transformer for joint video-state flow prediction with Shared-Time View Encoding to distinguish cameras while keeping them time-synchronized, feeds both outputs back to a frozen policy, and adds failed interactions collected in simulation to training.
TGtZJ9calQ.key_idea: Jointly predict multi-view video and proprioceptive state and train with simulated failed interactions, so the generated environment returns what the policy needs and does not overstate success.
TGtZJ9calQ.evidence: TriWorldBench comparison, correlation of generated and real success rates over three policies and four local manipulation tasks, a minute-long RoboChallenge setting, and ablations.
TGtZJ9calQ.claimed_gains: Highest overall TriWorldBench score among compared methods; Pearson correlation 0.95 and Spearman correlation 0.94 between generated and real success rates across three policies and four tasks.
TGtZJ9calQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that correlating generated with real success rates is a strong, practical evaluation and that returning proprioceptive state and modeling failures address real requirements of policy evaluation.
TGtZJ9calQ.main_concern: It is unclear how much of the gain comes from the proposed components rather than scale and data (state prediction and failure data give small ablation gains), and pooled correlations on 12 points do not show within-task ranking reliability.

fPOI1Qx5Bu.one_liner: Group-based RL for LLM agents that estimates step advantages from task-progress states and abstracted actions shared across tasks.
fPOI1Qx5Bu.problem: Stepwise group-based RL needs comparisons with consistent interaction history, but enforcing that consistency within a task's few rollouts leaves too little support to estimate action preferences.
fPOI1Qx5Bu.method: BLPO summarizes trajectory prefixes into task-progress states and abstracts actions by function, accumulates context-relative returns in a global memory with balanced aggregation and reliability weighting, and combines these global advantages with local comparisons and trajectory-level credit, without a critic or extra rollouts.
fPOI1Qx5Bu.key_idea: Pool context-relative returns across tasks and training updates by mapping histories to shared progress states and actions to functions, giving step-level advantages without a learned critic.
fPOI1Qx5Bu.evidence: ALFWorld and WebShop with 1.5B and 7B policies under matched training budgets, with ablations (same-task-only control, held-out tasks) and learning-speed and trajectory-length analyses.
fPOI1Qx5Bu.claimed_gains: Improved task success over the evaluated baselines under matched training budgets, with faster learning and shorter trajectories; a review reports WebShop success falling from 74.02 to 66.99 for a same-task-only control.
fPOI1Qx5Bu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that sharing credit across tasks to expand support without a learned critic is a well-motivated way to improve step-level credit assignment, with consistent gains on two benchmarks.
fPOI1Qx5Bu.main_concern: The state and action abstractions rely on hand-crafted environment-specific rules, so gains may stem from domain priors that no baseline uses and may not transfer to open-ended tasks.

kpgr8ZRRew.one_liner: Single-pass diffusion model generating a photorealistic background plus an RGBA foreground that includes shadows and reflections, enabling alpha-composite edits.
kpgr8ZRRew.problem: Image editing models drift in identity, and existing layered methods give foregrounds without shadows or reflections, forcing a second harmonization model after each edit that reintroduces drift.
kpgr8ZRRew.method: LASAGNA treats object-associated visual effects as part of the foreground layer and generates background and RGBA foreground in one forward pass, handling text, foreground, background and mask conditioning in one architecture. It releases a dataset (LASAGNA-48K) and a benchmark (LASAGNABENCH).
kpgr8ZRRew.key_idea: Bind object-associated shadows and reflections into the RGBA foreground layer so translation, scaling, recoloring and duplication need only alpha compositing, with no model call after the edit.
kpgr8ZRRew.evidence: Comparison with LayerDiffuse on the new benchmark using FID, CLIP-FID and GPT-4o-based scores plus a preference study, across three generation modes.
kpgr8ZRRew.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that binding visual effects into the foreground layer is a simple, practically valuable idea, the unified architecture handles three modes, and the released data and benchmark are useful.
kpgr8ZRRew.main_concern: The technical contribution is limited (adapting a pretrained DiT with data from an automated decomposition pipeline), and evaluation is narrow: single foreground over background, no multi-object cases, and little validation of the physical correctness of effects.

IK2UJrBZ06.one_liner: Mines vocabulary-named internal readout variables from fine-tuned LLM classifiers and learns compact executable rules that reproduce their decisions.
IK2UJrBZ06.problem: Task-fine-tuned LLM classifiers keep their decision knowledge implicit in distributed internal computation, making their decision logic hard to interpret.
IK2UJrBZ06.method: J-Miner, under the Executable Decision Compression framework, mines vocabulary-named variables from internal readouts and learns rules shared across inputs. A lightweight text reader predicts the variable states so the fixed rules run without the source classifier.
IK2UJrBZ06.key_idea: Read out vocabulary-named internal variables and fit input-shared executable rules over them to compress the classifier's decision logic.
IK2UJrBZ06.evidence: Six binary tasks across parameter scales within a family and across distinct families, compared with surface-word rules and random variable selections, with word-deletion experiments and standalone execution.
IK2UJrBZ06.claimed_gains: A rule with one variable reproduces 76.7% of source-classifier decisions on average across six binary tasks, rising to 88.8% with 16 variables.
IK2UJrBZ06.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that a small fixed set of internal variables reproduces much of a fine-tuned classifier's behavior, shown across tasks and model families against surface-word and random baselines.
IK2UJrBZ06.main_concern: High behavioral fidelity does not show the rules capture the classifier's actual decision mechanism, and vocabulary names add limited interpretability beyond readout events.

TkSKnIqqWH.one_liner: A small model searches and verifies video evidence over multiple steps; a large model answers once from that evidence.
TkSKnIqqWH.problem: Long-video agents assign evidence acquisition and answer generation to one model, coupling repeated visual exploration with that model's computational cost and reasoning limits.
TkSKnIqqWH.method: A small model performs multi-step evidence search and verification, and a large model integrates the acquired evidence into the final answer in a single invocation. The small model is supervised on search priorities grounded in current observations, while dense local verification decides each candidate's evidential value.
TkSKnIqqWH.key_idea: Decouple evidence acquisition (small model, search priorities supervised from current observations, then verified locally) from reasoning (large model, one call).
TkSKnIqqWH.evidence: Long-video benchmarks including VideoMME, MLVU, and LVBench with Qwen-based small and large model configurations such as 4B+4B and 4B+27B.
TkSKnIqqWH.claimed_gains: The abstract is truncated before results; a reviewer reports the 4B+27B setup improves VideoMME, MLVU, and LVBench by 6.0, 13.6, and 15.3 points over the frozen reasoner.
TkSKnIqqWH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the observation that small models can locate evidence they cannot use to answer a clear motivation, and report improvements over the corresponding frozen reasoner.
TkSKnIqqWH.main_concern: Gains may stem from the stronger 27B answering model rather than the framework, given unmatched baseline sizes and compute, missing related baselines such as VideoSeek, and evaluation limited to Qwen models.

jmbgVdHDlL.one_liner: Node-level OOD benchmarks reward input scale; a deterministic encoder (DCE) beats stochastic uncertainty methods on feature anomalies in one pass.
jmbgVdHDlL.problem: Node-level OOD detection is usually addressed with stochastic uncertainty methods, but the benchmarks that rank them reward input scale and graph-level contrast rather than uncertainty.
jmbgVdHDlL.method: The authors propose a controlled protocol suite and DCE, a deterministic encoder whose classifier reads each node's normalized features beside its aggregated context, and prove that node-wise decoders under separable losses cannot exploit a structured prior's cross-node correlation.
jmbgVdHDlL.key_idea: Control for feature scale in evaluation and use a deterministic encoder that pairs each node's normalized features with aggregated context, instead of stochastic uncertainty.
jmbgVdHDlL.evidence: Controlled protocols over multiple datasets, OOD settings, and uncertainty estimators (including ogbn-arxiv), with architectural controls, ablations, and a theoretical result on node-wise decoders.
jmbgVdHDlL.claimed_gains: Once scale is matched, MC-Dropout adds nothing and ensembling adds little, while DCE outperforms dedicated uncertainty methods on feature anomalies in a single forward pass; no numbers are stated.
jmbgVdHDlL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the identification of scale and protocol confounds in node-level OOD benchmarks meaningful, with broad controlled experiments and a clear motivation.
jmbgVdHDlL.main_concern: DCE differs from the stochastic baselines in architecture and training, so the claim that OOD detection needs no stochastic uncertainty is not isolated, and no method reliably detects real shift on ogbn-arxiv.

VDuLySkQTg.one_liner: Training-free optimization of initial noise so video diffusion tokens attend to their own frame, boosting motion dynamics.
VDuLySkQTg.problem: Video diffusion models often generate overly static videos, which the authors link to temporal attention in which tokens over-attend to other frames from the earliest denoising steps.
VDuLySkQTg.method: Self-Reflecting Optimization optimizes the initial noise to encourage tokens to attend to their own frame while keeping it close to the original sample and consistent with the Gaussian prior, without modifying the model or the conditioning signals.
VDuLySkQTg.key_idea: Optimize the initial noise, not the model, to raise within-frame attention and counter the cross-frame over-attention that suppresses motion.
VDuLySkQTg.evidence: Text-to-video and image-to-video backbones including Wan2.1, Wan2.1-14B, and CogVideoX-5B, evaluated with motion-related and quality metrics.
VDuLySkQTg.claimed_gains: SRO substantially boosts motion dynamics with only marginal degradation in text-video alignment; no numbers are stated.
VDuLySkQTg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the training-free, conditioning-agnostic design that applies to both T2V and I2V and the clear link between cross-frame over-attention and static generation.
VDuLySkQTg.main_concern: Motion metrics cannot separate meaningful motion from distortion or identity drift while quality metrics deteriorate, the self-reflecting score is validated on limited motion types, and the per-instance optimization cost is unclear.

jq8Aibg2X7.one_liner: Encodes failure-success trajectory pairs into correction tokens that condition a VLA to roll back and re-execute after failure detection.
jq8Aibg2X7.problem: VLA policies trained on success-only data often fail when driven into out-of-distribution states, and existing correction strategies use differing intervention interfaces.
jq8Aibg2X7.method: An event-anchored Contrastive Trajectory Encoder represents how failed trajectories diverge from successful references, and the deviation is encoded as correction tokens injected into VLA inference through a correction adapter. At inference an external detector triggers rollback to a pre-failure keyframe and retrieval of a matching successful reference from a Success Bank.
jq8Aibg2X7.key_idea: Condition the policy on paired failure-success trajectory representations (deviation-aware correction tokens) for controllable re-execution, rather than a plain retry.
jq8Aibg2X7.evidence: Closed-loop simulation with matched triggers and budgets against Retry and action replay (Table 2), three-seed results, and component ablations.
jq8Aibg2X7.claimed_gains: The abstract is truncated before results; a reviewer reports 452 recovered episodes versus 97 for Retry and 239 for action replay under shared triggers and budgets.
jq8Aibg2X7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the shared-trigger, shared-budget comparison against Retry and action replay a sound control showing a benefit beyond simply trying again.
jq8Aibg2X7.main_concern: The failure detector relies on simulator signals and synthetic failures, so real-world detection is unproven, and the contribution of pairing over failure-prefix-only conditioning is small (about 2.7% success).

Pm8NAbVzzq.one_liner: FSMem builds finite-state-machine training data to study how action variety, coverage, and execution depth shape rule internalization in LLMs.
Pm8NAbVzzq.problem: How training data supports the internalization of reusable task rules in LLM parametric memory is unclear.
Pm8NAbVzzq.method: FSMem is a state-transition framework that constructs training data in synthetic worlds, classical planning, and code execution, then tests rule reuse through two tasks: identifying valid actions and predicting execution outcomes.
Pm8NAbVzzq.key_idea: Hold transition rules fixed while varying action types, state-action coverage, and execution depth of training trajectories to isolate how data organization shapes memory formation.
Pm8NAbVzzq.evidence: Synthetic finite-state worlds, 13 ACPBench planning domains, and CodeI/O programs, with held-out sources and repository-disjoint code splits.
Pm8NAbVzzq.claimed_gains: Cumulative corpora combining short and long trajectories can outperform long-trajectory-only training while using fewer training tokens; no numbers are stated.
Pm8NAbVzzq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the controllable framework and evaluation methodology sound, with extensive controlled studies of action complexity, trajectory breadth, and depth across three settings.
Pm8NAbVzzq.main_concern: Per-rule supervision is not separated from data organization, since fixing the total number of examples means shared rules receive fewer examples as action types increase, and some findings are partly expected.

Sc5l6Osi2u.one_liner: Empirical study of robot behavior prompting finds task diversity, not demonstrations per task, drives in-context adaptation to unseen tasks.
Sc5l6Osi2u.problem: The conditions under which a robot demonstration can serve as an in-context prompt for new tasks remain poorly understood.
Sc5l6Osi2u.method: The authors build DrawAnything and LIBERO-Gen benchmarks with up to 2000 procedurally generated tasks, a Behavior Prompting Policy (BPP) in-context visuomotor architecture, and the iPhUMI handheld demonstration interface, then study when, how, and why prompting works, including an attention analysis.
Sc5l6Osi2u.key_idea: Use a sensorimotor demonstration as an in-context prompt that the policy follows step by step as dense sub-goals, studied through procedural benchmarks that vary task diversity.
Sc5l6Osi2u.evidence: Simulation on DrawAnything and LIBERO-Gen, real-robot drawing and chained manipulation, a real-world laundry experiment, and an attention analysis.
Sc5l6Osi2u.claimed_gains: With sufficient task diversity, behavior prompts reduce drawing error by 80.7% in simulation and 47.9% on a real robot over goal-image conditioning and improve chained manipulation success by up to 20.8% over language conditioning.
Sc5l6Osi2u.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value moving behavior prompting from showing it can work to a controlled study of when, how, and why, with procedural benchmarks and a balanced evaluation that includes cases where language wins.
Sc5l6Osi2u.main_concern: Most ablations run only on the 2D DrawAnything-Sim domain and the low-diversity conclusion rests on a single-seed, 3-task laundry experiment, so transfer to realistic manipulation is unclear.

EV5haYRs8G.one_liner: Distills a low-rank approximation at one ratio and merges it back, so one checkpoint serves SVD compression at many ratios.
EV5haYRs8G.problem: SVD-based LLM compression usually needs fine-tuning or weight correction to recover accuracy, and this budget-specific optimization must be repeated for every compression ratio.
EV5haYRs8G.method: LLift fine-tunes a low-rank approximation at a single ratio with the original model as teacher, merges the learned updates into the original weights while preserving the complementary components excluded from the training forward pass, then applies SVD to the target matrices and reuses the decompositions at different truncation ranks.
EV5haYRs8G.key_idea: Distill a low-rank student in a fixed subspace from the original model, then merge the update back so one set of SVD factors truncates well at many ranks.
EV5haYRs8G.evidence: LLaMA-7B at three compression ratios, extended across model families, sizes, and two SVD operators (SVD-LLM and ZS-SVD), with gradient and early-update analyses.
EV5haYRs8G.claimed_gains: Accuracy gains across three compression ratios using a single prepared model on LLaMA-7B, extending across model families, sizes, and SVD compression operators, with no numbers stated.
EV5haYRs8G.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find preparing one checkpoint for multiple compression budgets practically relevant, with consistent results across model families, sizes, and two SVD operators.
EV5haYRs8G.main_concern: Novelty and advantage over elastic baselines are limited: it combines existing components and performs similarly to FlexRank and ACIP (38% vs 41% average accuracy at 40% retention), with key related comparisons missing.

7JqhPVpmvF.one_liner: Aggressive Online Gradient Descent for constrained MDPs with hard budget stopping, with regret bounds matching up to sqrt(S).
7JqhPVpmvF.problem: Constrained MDPs with a hard cost budget and no null action lack algorithms with sublinear regret unless the budget is large, a setting that generalizes contextual bandits with knapsacks.
7JqhPVpmvF.method: The paper defines Constrained MDPs with Hard Stopping, where an H-step MDP runs for T episodes until cumulative cost exceeds budget B, and proposes Agressive Online Gradient Descent (AOGD) with a sliding-window variant for non-stationary settings.
7JqhPVpmvF.key_idea: Update the dual variable aggressively, using a negative optimistic-score test, under hard stopping with no null action.
7JqhPVpmvF.evidence: Theoretical regret upper and lower bounds, plus a sliding-window extension analyzed for non-stationary settings.
7JqhPVpmvF.claimed_gains: Regret upper bound O~((1+1/sqrt(b)) H^2 S sqrt(AT)) with b=B/T, sublinear whenever B = omega~(1), and a lower bound Omega(sqrt(H^4 S A T / b)) matching up to a factor of sqrt(S).
7JqhPVpmvF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the hard-stopping formulation without null actions well motivated and distinct from standard CMDPs, and the aggressive dual update technically substantive with a convincing stationary regret analysis.
7JqhPVpmvF.main_concern: Comparisons with prior CMDP and bandits-with-knapsacks results mix different stopping protocols and assumptions, the computational cost of the per-episode dual search is not analyzed, and Brantley et al. and classical BwK deserve explicit comparison.

O43to8lErQ.one_liner: Spiking temporal brain encoder plus transfer-entropy-guided directed propagation across functional subnetworks for fMRI brain disorder diagnosis.
O43to8lErQ.problem: Existing brain disorder diagnosis methods decouple connectivity from ongoing regional dynamics and rely on undirected interactions, leaving the path from local temporal activity to system-level information flow poorly modeled.
O43to8lErQ.method: A Spiking Temporal Brain Encoder processes decomposed regional BOLD signals with a stateful spiking encoder, an activity-guided spatial encoder conditions functional-connectivity attention on regional activity states, and a directional hierarchical propagation module aggregates regions into subnetworks using anatomical priors and effective-connectivity-guided propagation.
O43to8lErQ.key_idea: Couple regional spiking temporal dynamics with functional-connectivity attention and propagate information along directed effective connectivity between hierarchical functional subnetworks.
O43to8lErQ.evidence: Comparisons on three datasets with ablations over functional network priors, brain parcellations, and effective-connectivity parameters, using transfer entropy estimated from BOLD signals.
O43to8lErQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the unified modeling of regional temporal dynamics, functional connectivity, and hierarchical directed propagation meaningful, supported by systematic comparisons on three datasets and multiple ablations.
O43to8lErQ.main_concern: Transfer entropy from BOLD reflects statistical dependence rather than necessarily causal neural information flow, and the ablations do not show that directionality rather than extra connectivity information drives the gains.

mVcGCJALw8.one_liner: Three-stage TTS training generates speech with requested symptom cues such as coughs and sighs, controlled by type, count, and order.
mVcGCJALw8.problem: Existing TTS models often fail to reproduce the requested symptom cue type, count, and order, and even correct cue sequences may not blend naturally into speech.
mVcGCJALw8.method: HealthTTS generates full utterances from text, a speaker reference, and an optional cue configuration through cue-aware language-model adaptation, localized acoustic adaptation, and global preference refinement, trained on the new SymCue paired speech resource and evaluated on SymCueBench.
mVcGCJALw8.key_idea: Train cue generation and cue-speech integration jointly through staged adaptation ending in preference optimization, instead of post-hoc cue insertion.
mVcGCJALw8.evidence: SymCueBench covering seven symptom-related cue types, and a virtual standardized patient study with 30 medical students across 14 scenarios.
mVcGCJALw8.claimed_gains: Under the shared-cue setting HealthTTS achieves 87.3% Cue Sequence Accuracy, 25.1 percentage points above Fish Speech S2 Pro, and the study with 30 medical students across 14 scenarios shows higher Patient Realism and Perceived Usefulness than Cue Insertion.
mVcGCJALw8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the symptom-aware TTS formulation well motivated, with SymCue and SymCueBench providing a systematic framework and comprehensive ablations.
mVcGCJALw8.main_concern: Data construction and evaluation rely heavily on Qwen3-Omni with limited human validation, and SymCue uses synthesized speech and cues from only six speakers, leaving realism and generalization insufficiently validated.

D0VpPxha9Q.one_liner: Selective prompt compression as regularized monotone submodular maximization under a knapsack constraint, solved by Regularized Greedy+Max with approximation guarantee.
D0VpPxha9Q.problem: Fixed token- or sentence-level importance scores ignore how a sentence's contribution changes with the selected subset and inter-sentence redundancy, and autoregressive LLM scoring adds substantial overhead.
D0VpPxha9Q.method: PC-SubMax maximizes U(S) minus l(S), where a monotone submodular utility U combines information coverage, query relevance, and log-determinant diversity and a modular penalty l captures token cost, using the Regularized Greedy+Max (RGM) algorithm.
D0VpPxha9Q.key_idea: Score each sentence by its marginal contribution relative to already selected content through a submodular coverage-relevance-diversity utility under a token-cost knapsack.
D0VpPxha9Q.evidence: A (1/2,1) regularized approximation guarantee for RGM, plus experiments on diverse downstream tasks including LongBench subtasks, with baselines and ablations.
D0VpPxha9Q.claimed_gains: RGM deterministically returns a feasible set Q with U(Q)-l(Q) >= 1/2 U(O) - l(O) for an optimal feasible solution O; no empirical numbers are stated in the visible abstract.
D0VpPxha9Q.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the submodular formulation well motivated, accounting for coverage, redundancy, and token cost, with a competitive approximation guarantee and experiments showing competitive compression quality and low overhead.
D0VpPxha9Q.main_concern: The hand-designed utility and per-subtask hyperparameters are subjective and hard to transfer, and RGM largely builds on existing cost-scaled greedy and Greedy+Max techniques without comparison to other submodular algorithms.

x1NU8zqn5u.one_liner: Controllable environment that injects known biases into an LLM judge to reproduce, observe, and detect reward hacking in rubric-based RL.
x1NU8zqn5u.problem: In real rubric-based RL, hacking of LLM-as-a-Judge biases is subtle and entangled with multiple biases, making it hard to analyze, detect, and mitigate.
x1NU8zqn5u.method: CHERRL injects known biases into the LLM-as-a-Judge to reproduce reward hacking stably, track reward divergence, and identify hacking onset. The authors analyze judge biases by discoverability and exploitability and explore an agent that detects hacking onset from training logs.
x1NU8zqn5u.key_idea: Inject known judge biases so true and biased rewards can be tracked separately and hacking onset located with a reward-gap threshold.
x1NU8zqn5u.evidence: Reward-hacking runs with injected biases on a Qwen 3 4B policy, six hacking trajectories for discoverability, onset threshold sweeps, and detector evaluation, with human validation.
x1NU8zqn5u.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the controlled testbed with known injected biases a useful public good, with separate tracking of true and biased reward and structured onset detection.
x1NU8zqn5u.main_concern: Results rest on a single small model and only six hacking runs with binary injected biases that are unrealistic, and the reference onset is partly circular.

erJ21xq8Tv.one_liner: Benchmark (OverReal) measuring over-realization, where text-to-image models render prompt-mentioned targets that the prompt does not call for.
erJ21xq8Tv.problem: A target mentioned in a prompt often appears in the generated image in a way the prompt does not call for (under negation, belief, figurative comparison, or hidden viewpoint), and current evaluation cannot see this failure.
erJ21xq8Tv.method: OverReal-Gen has 698 prompts covering four situations to measure each generator's over-realization rate, and OverReal-Det has 2,841 human-labeled generated images used to verify the automatic judge; the authors also analyze attention inside the diffusion backbone.
erJ21xq8Tv.key_idea: Use mental-spaces theory to identify four prompt situations where a mentioned target should not be realized, then measure realization with a human-verified automatic judge.
erJ21xq8Tv.evidence: Evaluation of eight text-to-image systems on OverReal-Gen, with an automatic judge verified on OverReal-Det, plus prompt-expansion and attention analyses.
erJ21xq8Tv.claimed_gains: All eight evaluated text-to-image systems over-realize, conventional metrics such as CLIPScore reward the failure rather than penalize it, and prompt expansion only partly mitigates it.
erJ21xq8Tv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper exposes a previously underexamined failure mode beyond negation and a real blind spot in faithfulness metrics, backed by a broad evaluation of eight generators.
erJ21xq8Tv.main_concern: The definition of over-realization is contested, since naturally incorporated unrequested objects may be acceptable, and the large-scale conclusions depend on an automatic judge with weak agreement on perspectival examples.

UHY5ZSovWh.one_liner: Few-step video distillation adding image-teacher frame-level marginal matching to joint matching, with LatentBridge aligning video and image latents.
UHY5ZSovWh.problem: Joint distribution matching distillation mitigates drift in streaming video generation but leaves limits in visual quality and semantic alignment.
UHY5ZSovWh.method: DuoMatching adds a marginal matching objective that gives frame-level supervision from an image generator, LatentBridge to resolve the latent mismatch between video student and image teacher, and Latent Variation Sampling to spread the supervision across distinct temporal segments.
UHY5ZSovWh.key_idea: Combine joint matching against a video teacher with marginal frame-level matching against an image teacher, bridging their different latent spaces.
UHY5ZSovWh.evidence: Causal students at 1, 2, and 4 steps and a bidirectional student, VBench and frame-level metrics, a LatentBridge ablation (Table 4), and human evaluation, with Qwen-Image as the image teacher.
UHY5ZSovWh.claimed_gains: Human evaluations show overall preference rates above 80% against all evaluated baselines.
UHY5ZSovWh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the image-teacher marginal term improves frame quality and prompt adherence at no added inference cost, with LatentBridge keeping motion from collapsing.
UHY5ZSovWh.main_concern: Gains are small (VBench improvements under one point over the strongest baseline, with no variance) and largely attributable to the stronger Qwen-Image teacher, and novelty over prior image-teacher distillation is not established.

9mb62g4ySq.one_liner: Unified all-atom generative model for antibody, nanobody, and TCR structure prediction and two-stage CDR sequence-structure co-design.
9mb62g4ySq.problem: Existing immune receptor design methods separate structure generation from sequence design, rely on fixed-backbone inverse folding, or cover only one receptor class.
9mb62g4ySq.method: IgGM2 predicts receptor monomers from sequence and receptor-target complexes conditioned on fixed target structures and epitope context. For CDR design, a two-stage sampler first jointly generates CDR sequences and backbone conformations, then refines full-atom structures with the generated sequences fixed.
9mb62g4ySq.key_idea: Let receptor frameworks adapt to designed CDRs by jointly generating CDR sequence and backbone, then refining all atoms with the sequence fixed, without separate inverse folding or side-chain packing.
9mb62g4ySq.evidence: Structure prediction on FoldBench and TCR-pMHC modeling, sequence design benchmarks (amino-acid recovery and Rosetta-based interface metrics), and masking and refolding ablations, all with computational metrics only.
9mb62g4ySq.claimed_gains: Strong performance on FoldBench and TCR-pMHC modeling, competitive amino-acid recovery, and improved Rosetta-based interface preference metrics, with no numbers stated in the abstract.
9mb62g4ySq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the unified formulation across antibodies, nanobodies, and TCRs, with adaptive framework geometry, well motivated, and the structure prediction gains substantial.
9mb62g4ySq.main_concern: Structure prediction comparisons are not equivalent because IgGM2 receives fixed target structures and epitope information that baselines do not, and design results lack experimental validation.

fKAvHeHe7I.one_liner: Composes loop-invariant clauses pooled and filtered across LLM responses, and aligns SFT labels and RL credit with clause composition.
fKAvHeHe7I.problem: For legacy programs with hidden verification targets, target-specific verifier feedback is unavailable, and LLM-generated invariants often fail as whole responses even when they contain useful clauses scattered across responses.
fKAvHeHe7I.method: At inference CRAFT decomposes responses into clauses, pools and jointly filters them across responses, and composes the survivors into an invariant. SFT distills accepted compositions into labels for one response, RL credits coverage contributed by retained clauses, and invariant strength is estimated by how many candidate negative traces from executions it rejects.
fKAvHeHe7I.key_idea: Treat clauses, not whole responses, as the unit of composition, filtering, SFT labeling, and RL credit, estimating strength through rejected negative execution traces.
fKAvHeHe7I.evidence: Experiments on 832 C programs, with SFT and RL ablations, a clause-versus-whole-response reward ablation, and a comparison with Loopy, including Qwen3-8B.
fKAvHeHe7I.claimed_gains: The abstract is truncated before results; a reviewer reports Qwen3-8B compose@1 rising from 37.86% to 63.94% after SFT.
fKAvHeHe7I.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the mismatch between whole-response rewards and compositional inference real, and the clause-level treatment across inference, SFT, and RL coherent, with substantial verification gains across model sizes.
fKAvHeHe7I.main_concern: The SFT ablation does not match search and verification budgets, so gains from composition are not separated from label-construction effort, and the Loopy comparison is confounded by parser and feedback differences.

avqoWQM7j2.one_liner: Rectifies the recurrent state of spiking neurons so executions coalesce in finite time, enabling exact temporal parallelism via Coalescent Chunking.
avqoWQM7j2.problem: Spiking neural networks carry recurrent neuronal states across time, forcing exact temporal execution to be serial even when the rest of the network is highly parallel.
avqoWQM7j2.method: ReLIF rectifies the recurrent state before integration, so sufficiently negative inputs erase the carried state and sufficiently positive inputs trigger a common hard reset, making different incoming membrane states converge to zero. Coalescent Chunking precomputes boundary-independent suffixes in the forward pass and composes independent gradient intervals in the backward pass.
avqoWQM7j2.key_idea: A rectifier on the carried membrane state bounds its entry domain so all states coalesce to zero, letting chunks be computed independently while staying exact.
avqoWQM7j2.evidence: Theory (Lemma 1, Theorem 2), finite-precision certificates, CUDA kernels, SpikeTransformer++ at three scales, and vision and language modeling tasks.
avqoWQM7j2.claimed_gains: Parallel CUDA ReLIF reaches up to 8.04x forward and 22.07x backward kernel speedup over matched serial CUDA ReLIF, with 1.07x-1.30x inference and 1.22x-1.50x training throughput gains across three SpikeTransformer++ scales, and up to 38.07x forward and 17.71x backward kernel speedup over SpikingJelly CuPy LIF.
avqoWQM7j2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the single-ReLU change a neat way to get exact rather than approximate temporal parallelism, with short theory and validation spanning kernels, certificates, vision, and language.
avqoWQM7j2.main_concern: Headline speedups come mostly from comparing against SpikingJelly CuPy LIF (mixing neuron and backend), the matched gain from coalescence itself is modest, and effects on firing rate, long sequences, and ImageNet accuracy are untested.

MmN81mAPRY.one_liner: Repairs agent skills using rehearsals, perturbed environments built from the current skill, and replays earlier tasks to check the revision.
MmN81mAPRY.problem: A skill can complete tasks successfully while keeping an incorrect rule, such as choosing the first matching meeting, that causes harmful effects once the environment changes.
MmN81mAPRY.method: Rebind builds rehearsals from the current skill that change the environment around the objects it uses while keeping requests feasible, uses task results and actual effects as repair feedback, replays the original requests and earlier rehearsals to check the revision, and builds the next rehearsal from the revised skill.
MmN81mAPRY.key_idea: Generate each new rehearsal from the latest revised skill, so repair targets selection rules that earlier rehearsals could not expose.
MmN81mAPRY.evidence: Ten tool workflows with controlled conditions, held-out environment changes, and SkillLearnBench.
MmN81mAPRY.claimed_gains: Rebind safely completes all 462 controlled conditions versus 425 for a baseline that prepares rehearsals in advance, reduces harmful conditions from 33 to zero, and holds on held-out changes (144 of 144 conditions versus 131).
MmN81mAPRY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the failure mode, where task success hides wrong-target effects after environment changes, is real and well characterized, and that the rehearsal mechanism and the revised-skill ablation are sound.
MmN81mAPRY.main_concern: The controlled evaluation is circular and in-distribution (hand-written rehearsals and effect checkers per tool family), and zero attack success follows by construction from a model-free deployed program.

3fPwEvx7VF.one_liner: Single learned image codec with sliding window attention in transforms and context modeling, supporting 128 rate points via channel-wise gains.
3fPwEvx7VF.problem: Leading learned image compression methods need a separately trained model per operating point, which increases training, storage, and deployment cost.
3fPwEvx7VF.method: SWA-IC extends sliding window attention from autoregressive context modeling to the analysis and synthesis transforms, gives the synthesis transform direct access to context features, and adds learned attention sinks, growing channel groups, and generalized Gaussian entropy modeling. Channel-wise gains control rate with shared network weights.
3fPwEvx7VF.key_idea: Use one sliding-window-attention design for both feature transforms and spatial context modeling, with channel-wise gains controlling rate across 128 operating points.
3fPwEvx7VF.evidence: Rate-distortion evaluation on Kodak, Tecnick, and CLIC against VTM 23.10 and single-rate and multirate codecs, plus decoding-latency comparisons and ablations.
3fPwEvx7VF.claimed_gains: BD-rate savings of 18.44%, 24.86%, and 18.53% on Kodak, Tecnick, and CLIC relative to VTM 23.10, the lowest BD-rate among the evaluated single-rate and multirate codecs.
3fPwEvx7VF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the variable-rate model for matching or exceeding single-rate codecs with competitive decoding speed, a trustworthy evaluation, and useful ablations such as context-feature reuse.
3fPwEvx7VF.main_concern: Training data is much larger than the baselines' (roughly ImageNet-21k scale), margins over the strongest baselines are small (a tie with HPCM Large on Kodak), and novelty is limited.

Hu4rFmLvX9.one_liner: Restores the missing scale-gradient term in the straight-through estimator for MXFP4 activation quantization, curbing norm-weight drift in W4A4 QAT.
Hu4rFmLvX9.problem: Activation quantization in MXFP4 W4A4 QAT causes sustained growth of activation magnitudes and pre-FFN RMSNorm weights that impairs optimization, which the conventional STE fails to account for.
Hu4rFmLvX9.method: TetraBack restores the gradient contribution of each group's scale that the conventional straight-through estimator ignores, correcting the biased gradients reaching the preceding RMSNorm without modifying the forward computation.
Hu4rFmLvX9.key_idea: Add the gradient through each quantization group's scale, which the STE ignores, back into the backward pass while leaving the forward quantizer untouched.
Hu4rFmLvX9.evidence: MXFP4 W4A4 QAT on MoE models from 3B to 94B (DeepSeek-derived, with routed-expert FFNs quantized), with weight-only controls, BF16 backward, norm-scale interventions, and gradient tracing.
Hu4rFmLvX9.claimed_gains: Consistently improves performance across 3B-94B MoE models and reduces the loss gap induced by activation quantization by up to 41%.
Hu4rFmLvX9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the diagnosis of norm and activation drift new and convincingly supported by controlled interventions, with a simple fix that preserves the forward quantizer and helps across scales.
Hu4rFmLvX9.main_concern: Evaluation is narrow, covering only DeepSeek-derived MoE models with only routed-expert FFNs quantized, so dense and other architectures are untested, and novelty over prior scale-gradient work (Hu et al. 2025) is limited.

DUcT3bPD1W.one_liner: Organizes per-task adapters into semantic clusters and merged expert trees, then fuses activated experts by confidence for class-incremental learning.
DUcT3bPD1W.problem: Adapter-per-task methods for pre-trained-model class-incremental learning prevent forgetting but treat learned knowledge as an unstructured collection and ignore relationships between tasks.
DUcT3bPD1W.method: SAEF groups tasks into semantic clusters and builds a balanced expert tree in each cluster by merging adapters of similar tasks. At inference it activates relevant experts from the forest and combines their outputs weighted by each expert's confidence.
DUcT3bPD1W.key_idea: Merge adapters of semantically similar tasks into hierarchical expert trees, and let internal merged nodes act as prediction experts fused by confidence weights.
DUcT3bPD1W.evidence: Experiments on several class-incremental benchmarks (four in Table 1, including ObjectNet) against adapter-based and prompt-based methods, plus an ablation study.
DUcT3bPD1W.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract only claims SOTA performance on several benchmark datasets.
DUcT3bPD1W.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the hierarchical design with internal nodes as prediction experts is sensible and clearly described, and that it gives the highest average and final accuracy in Table 1 on all four benchmarks.
DUcT3bPD1W.main_concern: The gain from semantic structure is not isolated from extra capacity, since SAEF stores about 2T-1 adapters and lacks matched-budget comparisons with random trees or flat ensembles.

zKexmF31Cy.one_liner: Reweights tokens in long-context mid-training using a cheap segmented-versus-full-context loss ratio with filtering and bounded rank-percentile weights.
zKexmF31Cy.problem: Uniform token-averaged cross-entropy dilutes long-range supervision because few tokens benefit from distant context, and existing token-reweighting methods carry heavy training overhead from fine-grained dependency scoring.
zKexmF31Cy.method: LongFocus computes SegRatio, each token's relative loss increase from the full-context view to a coarse segmented view with no cross-segment attention. PreSelect limits weighting by document length and full-view loss, and Reweight assigns bounded weights by rank percentile within the eligible set.
zKexmF31Cy.key_idea: Score each token's long-range dependency by its loss increase when attention is cut into non-overlapping segments, then upweight top-ranked eligible tokens with bounded weights.
