zKexmF31Cy.evidence: Llama-3-8B-Instruct, MoE-16B-A3B, and MoE-125B-A10B with a two-stage 64K-to-512K mid-training recipe, evaluated before and after SFT.
zKexmF31Cy.claimed_gains: not stated; the visible abstract says only that LongFocus improves Long-Avg before the text is cut off.
zKexmF31Cy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is lighter than prior token-weighting such as LongCE (faster training, lower peak memory) while matching or slightly improving performance, and that it is tested on dense and MoE models.
zKexmF31Cy.main_concern: Most comparisons are against vanilla cross-entropy, LongCE is compared only on Llama-3-8B-Instruct, and the many hyperparameters with uninformative ablations leave unclear why it beats LongCE.

m7GM5nzGsr.one_liner: Agent framework on ComfyUI that explores multiple editing plans, backtracks to the earliest failed step, and evolves rules from experience.
m7GM5nzGsr.problem: Existing image editing models and agents are fragile on complex chain-dependent edits because of poor planning, step-by-step verification, and no learning from accumulated interaction history.
m7GM5nzGsr.method: EvoEdit combines Multi-Path Exploration of concurrent execution trajectories, Recursive Verification that backtracks through execution history to find the earliest fault, and a Dual-Dimensional Self-Evolving mechanism that synthesizes planning rules and refines step execution from experience.
m7GM5nzGsr.key_idea: Backtrack through execution history to locate the earliest failing step, and accumulate planning rules and step-level refinements from past runs without updating model parameters.
m7GM5nzGsr.evidence: Two-chain and Three-chain dependent editing settings scored by a VLM-based 0-5 score and a multiplicative chain metric, compared with Nano Banana, with ablations removing evolution, multi-path exploration, or recursive verification.
m7GM5nzGsr.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract is cut off before any results are given.
m7GM5nzGsr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it targets a real weakness of treating dependent edit chains as independent steps, that multi-path planning and earliest-fault verification are sensible, and that ablations show drops when any component is removed.
m7GM5nzGsr.main_concern: The evaluation rests on an unvalidated VLM/GPT-4o judge with no human checks, confidence intervals, or compute-matched baselines, and the experience library's separation from test tasks is unclear.

DdqE0KEDcp.one_liner: Distills a multimodal LLM's generative label recognition into a fast image-only discriminative classifier via cross-paradigm and cross-token distillation.
DdqE0KEDcp.problem: MLLM-based annotation-free multi-label recognition generates labels autoregressively, which incurs high inference overhead from task-prompt encoding and token-by-token decoding.
DdqE0KEDcp.method: Cross-Paradigm Distillation converts generative recognition into prompt-aware discriminative prediction while preserving the generative learning signal. Cross-Token Distillation then transfers this prompt-aware capability to an image-only pathway for efficient inference.
DdqE0KEDcp.key_idea: Two-stage progressive distillation: first turn generative outputs into prompt-aware discriminative predictions, then distill them into an image-only branch that needs no task prompt.
DdqE0KEDcp.evidence: Experiments on multiple multi-label benchmarks and backbones against existing annotation-free methods, with a frozen teacher MLLM supplying labels.
DdqE0KEDcp.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract is cut off before any numbers are given.
DdqE0KEDcp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it addresses a practical inference-cost problem of MLLM-based multi-label recognition with a coherent progressive design, extensive experiments across datasets and backbones, and clear writing.
DdqE0KEDcp.main_concern: Training depends on a frozen teacher MLLM's pseudo-labels, whose errors (especially missing positives) are not analysed, and the need for the progressive design over simpler distillation is not shown.

Ng4xBeeWus.one_liner: Large-scale linear-probing study over layers and modules of vision and language transformers, yielding fixed probing locations (Act@100, LN2@60).
Ng4xBeeWus.problem: Probing the final layer is often suboptimal, and prior work varies only depth, treating each transformer block as one unit and ignoring which module within it to probe.
Ng4xBeeWus.method: They run more than 144,000 linear-probing evaluations of vision foundation models and LLMs across layer-module pairs. They then test fixed strategies: the final-layer feedforward activation (Act@100) for vision and the second normalization layer at 60% depth (LN2@60) for language.
Ng4xBeeWus.key_idea: Choose the probing location jointly over layer depth and module within each transformer block, then derive fixed per-domain locations from the large sweep.
Ng4xBeeWus.evidence: More than 144,000 linear-probing evaluations on vision foundation models and LLMs, with supplementary analyses of distribution shift, pre- and post-finetuning representations, and feature dimensionality.
Ng4xBeeWus.claimed_gains: Act@100 and LN2@60 improve over the probing baseline in a majority of evaluations and recover on average 42% and 86% of the gains from the best layer-module pair for vision and language.
Ng4xBeeWus.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the joint layer-and-module analysis is useful and relevant, and that the sweep covers a broad range of vision and language models and benchmarks.
Ng4xBeeWus.main_concern: The study is purely empirical with little explanation of why particular positions work, covers only classification probing (a small multilingual text task for LLMs), and reports no multi-seed results for small differences.

Y0HPxl9NOC.one_liner: Post-training LLM compression that splits weight rows into groups, low-rank factorizes each, and repeats on residuals hierarchically.
Y0HPxl9NOC.problem: Global low-rank compression fits a whole weight matrix in one shared subspace, limiting its ability to preserve distinct local low-rank structures in pretrained weights.
Y0HPxl9NOC.method: HMC partitions weight rows into groups approximated by separate low-rank factorizations, then repartitions and approximates successive residuals. It adaptively allocates ranks and jointly fits the local factors across groups.
Y0HPxl9NOC.key_idea: Approximate each group of weight rows with its own low-rank subspace, jointly fit the group factors, and recursively factor residuals to capture local structure beyond one partition.
Y0HPxl9NOC.evidence: Seven LLMs (reviewers mention five) measured by WikiText-2 and C4 perplexity and six downstream tasks against ASVD, SVD-LLM, and Swift-SVD, with controlled ablations and an analysis under subspace and partition assumptions.
Y0HPxl9NOC.claimed_gains: HMC generally lowers WikiText-2 and C4 perplexity and improves accuracy on six downstream tasks over low-rank baselines across seven LLMs; magnitudes are not stated.
Y0HPxl9NOC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree global low-rank approximation is a meaningful limitation, the local-similarity motivation is concrete, and the ablations help attribute gains to the proposed components.
Y0HPxl9NOC.main_concern: Row-partitioned low-rank approximation is said to have been explored before, and the baselines omit stronger rank-allocation and cross-layer sharing methods such as SVD-LLM V2, Dobi-SVD, and Basis Sharing.

7FhlvtOHnZ.one_liner: Benchmark that checks MLLM-stated visual evidence against ground-truth remote sensing annotations using per-question evidence contracts.
7FhlvtOHnZ.problem: Benchmarks grade only the final answer and tacitly assume a correct answer comes with trustworthy visual evidence, an assumption left untested for MLLMs.
7FhlvtOHnZ.method: Evidence contracts specify, for each question, the visual facts its answer depends on. RSFaith-Bench has 13,511 human-validated questions over 16,288 images, and model claims are checked against ground-truth annotation rather than judged by another model.
7FhlvtOHnZ.key_idea: Define per-question evidence contracts listing the facts an answer depends on, and verify the model's stated claims against structured annotation instead of an LLM judge.
7FhlvtOHnZ.evidence: 22 MLLMs (proprietary, open-source, and remote-sensing models) evaluated under an evidence-first prompt, with the check agreeing with human raters on 89.4% of responses (the TLDR says 18 models).
7FhlvtOHnZ.claimed_gains: Across 18 models, average answer accuracy is 51.3% while faithful accuracy is only 25.8%, and the abstract says more than half of accuracy-correct answers would fail a check of their own evidence.
7FhlvtOHnZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark usefully separates answer correctness from evidence faithfulness, verifies against annotation rather than an LLM judge, and splits failures into contradicted versus missing-support evidence across many models.
7FhlvtOHnZ.main_concern: Prior work already shows correct answers can come with unfaithful evidence (for example faithfulness of visual thinking, CLEVR-X, VISTAQA), and the paper does not clearly distinguish evidence contracts from it.

lwbcoGD9rJ.one_liner: Adaptive test that learns a selector to choose chess positions and an estimator to update player strength from responses.
lwbcoGD9rJ.problem: Estimating a player's strength typically needs about 20-30 games, which is slow, and classical adaptive testing needs calibrated item banks that do not exist for chess positions.
lwbcoGD9rJ.method: CASE, inspired by computerized adaptive testing, uses an estimator that updates strength from the question-response history and a selector that picks the next board position from the history and current estimate. The selector is supervised by the rank-posterior confidence gain a hypothesized response would produce.
lwbcoGD9rJ.key_idea: Learn a selector, supervised by the confidence gain in the rank posterior that a hypothesized response would produce, to pick informative positions without a calibrated item bank.
lwbcoGD9rJ.evidence: Chess experiments with simulated players (Maia-style networks trained on Lichess rank bands, plus ALLIE) compared against baselines and a prior game-based strength estimation method.
lwbcoGD9rJ.claimed_gains: CASE reaches over 80% rank accuracy with 34 questions where no baseline does after 200, 95% within-one-rank accuracy after five questions and 100% after 22, and needs about 27 times fewer player responses than the prior game-based method.
lwbcoGD9rJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is useful and the formulation clean, and that learning the selector removes the need for a calibrated item bank while adapting position choices to the current strength estimate.
lwbcoGD9rJ.main_concern: All test-takers are simulated players, so the results do not show that CASE estimates human strength, and the abstract and introduction do not state this limit.

e7s283zt6q.one_liner: Predicts per-point-pair NOCS coordinates with flow matching and aligns them via RANSAC N-hop Kabsch-Umeyama for category-agnostic 9D pose.
e7s283zt6q.problem: Object pose estimation generalizes poorly to novel categories and unseen scenes, and existing approaches often depend on category labels, CAD models, mean-shape priors, or reference views.
e7s283zt6q.method: Given an instance mask or ROI and RGB-D (or RGB with predicted depth), it samples point pairs, predicts NOCS coordinates per pair from DINOv2 and PointNet features, and uses flow matching for symmetric ambiguities. A point-pair RANSAC N-hop Kabsch-Umeyama algorithm with adaptive threshold recovers rotation, translation, and metric size.
e7s283zt6q.key_idea: Predict NOCS coordinates for sampled point pairs with a flow-matching head to handle symmetry, then recover rotation, translation, and size by robust geometric alignment.
e7s283zt6q.evidence: Experiments across eight datasets with a single unified model trained on a curated mix of public pose annotations, covering unseen objects, unseen categories, and in-the-wild scenes, with ablations and baselines retrained on a four-dataset mixture.
e7s283zt6q.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract only claims competitive performance on standard benchmarks and generalization to unseen objects, categories, and in-the-wild scenes.
e7s283zt6q.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree a single shared category-agnostic model evaluated across many datasets is a practical baseline, with useful ablations and in-domain gains over retrained baselines.
e7s283zt6q.main_concern: Limited novelty, since the point-pair parameterization, probabilistic canonical coordinates, scale calibration, and flow matching adapt CPPF/CPPF++ and standard components, and the unseen-category comparison is not rigorously matched.

ZIBdUe2hGK.one_liner: Audit protocol that perturbs the skill bank after training to measure fragility of skill-policy co-evolved agents.
ZIBdUe2hGK.problem: Skill-policy co-evolution is evaluated only on the final delivered skill bank, yet deployed banks are rewritten, extended, or pruned more often than the policy is retrained, leaving the resulting fragility unmeasured.
ZIBdUe2hGK.method: Theory and experiments show that the shared cooperative acceptance rule ties a policy's competence to the bank it co-evolved with. CODA simulates skill drift and measures worst-case success rate, consistency under meaning-preserving edits, and resistance to corrupted skills.
ZIBdUe2hGK.key_idea: Cooperative acceptance couples a policy's competence to the specific skill bank it co-evolved with; CODA exposes this by evaluating under simulated skill-bank drift.
ZIBdUe2hGK.evidence: Four co-evolution methods across five benchmarks (six settings), with Qwen2.5-7B and Qwen3-4B models, plus a theoretical proposition.
ZIBdUe2hGK.claimed_gains: Worst-case success rates fall 5-13 points below the peaks of the corresponding delivered pairs (the abstract is cut off after this).
ZIBdUe2hGK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it identifies an important evaluation blind spot, with evidence across multiple methods and benchmarks that degradation under skill drift is substantial.
ZIBdUe2hGK.main_concern: The theoretical analysis (Proposition 1) rests on strong idealized assumptions and does not establish that co-evolution itself causes the fragility, and the paper proposes no remedy.

LfKYZHX5GT.one_liner: Generates artisan meshes by flow matching in compact latents, producing vertex positions and edge connectivity separately via vertex-anchored VAEs.
LfKYZHX5GT.problem: Autoregressive face-token mesh generators are slow, and VAE-latent flow matching loses reconstruction quality when geometry and topology are encoded jointly and more so when the latent space is compressed.
LfKYZHX5GT.method: MeshCarve generates vertex positions and edge connections separately with VertexVAE and EdgeVAE on a hierarchical sparse transformer anchored on discrete vertices, using spatial-aware compression and a vertex-link encoding that turns arbitrary connectivity into fixed-length per-vertex embeddings. An anchor generator and flow matching then operate on the shortened token sequences.
LfKYZHX5GT.key_idea: Anchor latents on discrete vertices and encode connectivity as fixed-length per-vertex link embeddings, so flow matching runs over short token sequences with separate vertex and edge latents.
LfKYZHX5GT.evidence: Comparisons with autoregressive and flow matching baselines on Objaverse and Toys4K (the abstract text is cut off), plus an ablation of the vertex-link encoding on EdgeVAE reconstruction F1.
LfKYZHX5GT.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract only claims advantages over autoregressive and flow matching methods on Objaverse and other benchmarks before it is cut off.
LfKYZHX5GT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the vertex-anchored, higher-compression latent design is a concrete response to long token sequences, and the vertex-link encoding ablation shows a large effect on edge reconstruction.
LfKYZHX5GT.main_concern: End-to-end topology is far from artist meshes, with 27.7% of edges non-manifold on Objaverse and 17.5% on Toys4K, which the main-text surface metrics cannot reveal.

DcbeMm0FUa.one_liner: Trains a VLM on calibrated stereo pairs with hierarchical supervision from correspondence and disparity to metric depth and spatial reasoning.
DcbeMm0FUa.problem: VLMs infer 3D structure from uncalibrated images without cross-view geometric constraints, which makes metric 3D inference ambiguous and leaves unclear whether predictions are grounded in visual evidence.
DcbeMm0FUa.method: StereoVLM learns from calibrated binocular observations in a hierarchy from cross-view correspondence and disparity estimation to calibration-conditioned metric depth and semantic spatial reasoning. They also introduce Stereo3D-Bench, a three-level benchmark from point-level geometry upward.
DcbeMm0FUa.key_idea: Train in a hierarchy from cross-view correspondence and disparity to calibration-conditioned metric depth, supervising disparity rather than depth directly on binocular input.
DcbeMm0FUa.evidence: A controlled comparison of three supervision types on the same 234K image pairs, a right-view intervention suite on one checkpoint, Stereo3D-Bench, and transfer to five external benchmarks and RoboCasa control.
DcbeMm0FUa.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract says only that disparity supervision generalizes substantially better than direct binocular depth supervision on unseen environments.
DcbeMm0FUa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the controlled supervision comparison and the right-view intervention show the model really uses the second view and that disparity supervision generalizes better than direct depth supervision.
DcbeMm0FUa.main_concern: The external transfer gains are not isolated from added spatial-task data, since the control removes stereo data together with its metric-depth and 3D box labels and no left-only arm uses the same labels.

U1tntSQaWC.one_liner: Splits encoder features into invertible main and complementary parts and updates the complementary part from main-state differences for all-in-one restoration.
U1tntSQaWC.problem: In hierarchical restoration networks, downsampling can discard information needed for reconstruction, and standard skip connections pass encoder features to the decoder without updating them from the restored main state.
U1tntSQaWC.method: RFD decomposes encoder features into main and complementary representations and reconstructs them at the matching decoder stage with an inverse transform. SCU applies a shared mapping to the encoder and decoder main states and uses the difference of the two outputs to update the complementary representation without explicit degradation identification.
U1tntSQaWC.key_idea: Decompose features with a learnable orthogonal transform whose inverse restores them at the decoder, and update the complementary part using the difference between shared-mapped encoder and decoder main states.
U1tntSQaWC.evidence: Experiments on multiple datasets (four benchmark settings including CDD11 and WeatherBench per reviewers) with component ablations, using a 10M-parameter model.
U1tntSQaWC.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract only says extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the method and its components.
U1tntSQaWC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the decomposition and update form a coherent, well-motivated design for information preservation, with gains across benchmarks, notably on CDD11 and WeatherBench.
U1tntSQaWC.main_concern: Architectural novelty is modest given prior wavelet and lifting-based invertible restoration methods, and SCU's ablation gains are small (0.02 to 0.08 dB in Table 5) without seed variability.

ikf7ZIpFrs.one_liner: Feeds geospatial vector geometry into a VLM as element-level reference-point and path tokens with learnable object, role and relation states.
ikf7ZIpFrs.problem: VLMs get spatial information mainly from language and vision, and at larger geographic scales limited visual observations make it hard to establish accurate spatial references and recover precise spatial relations.
ikf7ZIpFrs.method: GeoVec-VLM builds a structured geometry representation that preserves the spatial structure and arrangement of vector objects, and a geometry interaction strategy that lets it interact with visual content and language references according to the queried spatial relation. Per reviewers, polygon boundaries are split into alternating reference-point and path elements that stay unpooled inside the VLM.
ikf7ZIpFrs.key_idea: Keep polygon boundaries as unpooled element-level reference-point and path tokens, and read them through learnable object, role and relation states inside the VLM.
ikf7ZIpFrs.evidence: Five spatial reasoning tasks, a deterministic geospatial benchmark with six task families, ablations of pooled versus element-level representations and spatial states, held-out region transfer, and a geometric consistency analysis.
ikf7ZIpFrs.claimed_gains: Across five spatial reasoning tasks, GeoVec-VLM improves mean accuracy by about 11% relative to the strongest baseline and maintains its gains under geographic transfer.
ikf7ZIpFrs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the element-level vector representation is well designed and that ablations, geographic transfer tests, and the geometric consistency analysis give useful supporting evidence.
ikf7ZIpFrs.main_concern: The Table 2 baselines (serialized GeoJSON, Geo2Vec, Poly2Vec) lack the components core to GeoVec-VLM, so the comparison is not controlled and does not isolate the benefit of element-level structure.

30dDhGwSc8.one_liner: Aligns instruction tokens with behavior segments bidirectionally to condition a 3D diffusion policy on fine-grained, unseen specifications.
30dDhGwSc8.problem: Text-to-3D policies fail to follow unseen fine-grained behavioral specifications such as target position, displacement, or articulated state, because pretrained language representations and global alignment blur nearby specifications.
30dDhGwSc8.method: T3DP preserves local structure in instructions and demonstrations instead of compressing each into one global embedding, and builds bidirectional token-level correspondence between linguistic elements and behavioral segments. The resulting specification-sensitive language representation conditions a point-cloud-based 3D diffusion policy.
30dDhGwSc8.key_idea: Replace global instruction-behavior embeddings with bidirectional token-level alignment between words and behavior segments, so close specifications stay distinct in representation space.
30dDhGwSc8.evidence: Multiple benchmarks and real robots, with a controlled comparison against global alignment (T2DA) sharing the behavior encoder, alignment data, downstream policy, and training budget, plus ablations of alignment methods.
30dDhGwSc8.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract is cut off before any results are given.
30dDhGwSc8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is relevant and that the controlled comparison with global alignment shows consistent improvements across benchmarks and real robots.
30dDhGwSc8.main_concern: The behavior encoder's reward-prediction objective requires reward-annotated expert demonstrations, which limits use on robot datasets that contain only state-action sequences.

JB4vGJP9Dk.one_liner: Regularizes sparse-view Gaussian Splatting by building twin dropout subfields and enforcing error-guided low-frequency consistency between them.
JB4vGJP9Dk.problem: Dropout-based sparse-view 3D Gaussian Splatting optimizes only one stochastic Gaussian subfield per iteration, leaving the discrepancy across dropout realizations unobserved and unconstrained.
JB4vGJP9Dk.method: TwinDropGS builds twin Gaussian subfields from a shared field with complete joint coverage and aligns their low-frequency luminance responses, emphasizing regions with larger reconstruction error. A progressive complementary consistency schedule gradually increases subfield complementarity and consistency strength during training.
JB4vGJP9Dk.key_idea: Make dropout-induced discrepancy observable by rendering two complementary Gaussian subfields from one field and aligning their low-frequency luminance, weighted toward high-error regions.
JB4vGJP9Dk.evidence: Three sparse-view benchmarks and view settings against DropGaussian and other sparse-view 3DGS methods, including plug-in use on those methods and a training-time comparison.
JB4vGJP9Dk.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract is cut off before any results are given.
JB4vGJP9Dk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the idea is simple and well motivated, needs no external priors or auxiliary networks, and improves results consistently across benchmarks and when added to other methods.
JB4vGJP9Dk.main_concern: The main DropGaussian baseline is reported below its published numbers, which may inflate the gains (about 0.1 dB on some settings), and the method roughly doubles training time.

q9cbLNF7Lc.one_liner: Training-free optimization of the flow-matching sampling schedule by minimizing energy distance between generated and demonstrated action-chunk differences.
q9cbLNF7Lc.problem: Under a fixed budget of neural function evaluations, a flow matching robot policy's output depends on the sampling schedule, and a uniform grid does not bring generated actions close to the demonstrations.
q9cbLNF7Lc.method: GYS applies truncated fractional differencing along each arm joint's action sequence and compares generated-versus-demonstration differences with generated-versus-generated differences at each observation. It minimizes the energy distance between these distributions to pick a schedule per task and NFE budget.
q9cbLNF7Lc.key_idea: After fractional differencing, generated-versus-demonstration and generated-versus-generated pairwise differences coincide exactly when distributions match, so minimizing their energy distance selects the sampling schedule.
q9cbLNF7Lc.evidence: RoboTwin 2.0 benchmarks and real-world robots with different base VLA models, plus an ablation on observation conditioning.
q9cbLNF7Lc.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract is cut off after 'improves success rates at nearly every' on RoboTwin 2.0.
q9cbLNF7Lc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is principled and training-free and gives consistent improvements in simulation and real-world manipulation across base VLA models.
q9cbLNF7Lc.main_concern: Success-rate gains are small (generally 2 to 5 points), are not averaged over multiple runs with standard deviations, and the ablations are thin.

Um2XKwBR60.one_liner: Diagnoses why visual chain-of-thought aids fail in geometry and trains GeoWeave-8B with reinforcement learning for interleaved visual-text reasoning.
Um2XKwBR60.problem: Models struggle to benefit from self-constructed auxiliary lines in visual chain-of-thought geometry solving, and it is unclear whether the failure lies in the aids' value or in the model's ability to build and use them.
Um2XKwBR60.method: They evaluate models under No-Aux, Auto-Aux, and GT-Aux setups plus a five-dimensional trajectory diagnosis on GeoVAD-Bench, then introduce a targeted post-training paradigm and a reinforcement learning algorithm for interleaved visual-textual reasoning. Reviewers add that credit assignment uses a step-level process verifier.
Um2XKwBR60.key_idea: Separate the value of auxiliary diagrams from the model's ability to build and use them via No-Aux, Auto-Aux, and GT-Aux, then train with step-level credit RL.
Um2XKwBR60.evidence: Controlled No-Aux, Auto-Aux, and GT-Aux evaluations of several systems on GeoVAD-Bench, and GeoWeave-8B trained from a single base model and compared with it.
Um2XKwBR60.claimed_gains: GeoWeave-8B outperforms the base model by 25.3 percentage points in final geometric accuracy and 30.4 (the abstract is cut off after this figure).
Um2XKwBR60.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the No-Aux, Auto-Aux, and GT-Aux decomposition and the autonomy-gap framing are valuable, since ground-truth diagrams help while autonomous drawing can underperform reasoning without aids.
Um2XKwBR60.main_concern: The central claim of narrowing the autonomy gap is never measured for GeoWeave, which is reported only under Auto-Aux without No-Aux or GT-Aux results.

3pDj9eGvKf.one_liner: Solves inverse problems with in-context image generators using a measurement-derived reference, scheduled guidance, and early-step suppression of generation-to-text attention.
3pDj9eGvKf.problem: A reference image alone is not enough when in-context image generation models are used for inverse problems, because generations that depart from the observed layout respond less to the reference and the degree of prior trust is left unspecified.
3pDj9eGvKf.method: RefReg is a posterior sampler that regulates reference influence at three levels: constructing a measurement-derived reference, scheduling reference guidance to emphasize structure early and detail later, and suppressing generation-to-text attention during early structure formation. They also derive an upper bound on the average posterior approximation error of a conditional prior under data-consistency updates.
3pDj9eGvKf.key_idea: Treat the model as a measurement-dependent prior and regulate how strongly the reference steers each stage, favoring structure early and detail late, while blocking text attention early.
3pDj9eGvKf.evidence: A posterior error bound plus experiments over 16 dataset-task combinations, additional backbones, a distilled model, and few NFEs, with ablations on the timing of attention blocking.
3pDj9eGvKf.claimed_gains: not stated; the TLDR only claims it beats text-only priors and flow-based solvers.
3pDj9eGvKf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the empirical results are strong, with best LPIPS in most settings and gains across backbones, and that the early-timing intervention has direct experimental support.
3pDj9eGvKf.main_concern: The contribution is mainly a particular combination of established components (reference conditioning, two-scale guidance, attention control, clean-estimate correction), and the posterior-error theory is seen as overselling what it shows.

n9urR0xk8V.one_liner: Homotopy path for LoRA fine-tuning that strengthens the task objective while relaxing a KL retention budget from a quadratic-anchored start.
n9urR0xk8V.problem: Low rank alone does not ensure capability retention in LoRA, and how the optimization path shapes specialization under a fixed behavioral allowance and finite computation is unclear.
n9urR0xk8V.method: RBC-LoRA constrains forward sequence KL divergence from the original model on reference prompts. A temporary quadratic factor anchor gives a unique starting solution, and continuation strengthens the task objective, removes the anchor, and expands the retention allowance, guided by primal-dual correction and acceptance checks while preserving adapter rank.
n9urR0xk8V.key_idea: Reach the same KL-constrained LoRA problem by continuation from an anchored easy solution, with primal-dual correction and acceptance checks, instead of solving the constrained problem directly.
n9urR0xk8V.evidence: Four backbones from 3B to 9B on mathematical reasoning, code generation, and instruction following, plus a path-tracking analysis under local regularity assumptions (reviewers describe the main runs as two 3B models on GSM8K and MBPP).
n9urR0xk8V.claimed_gains: RBC-LoRA achieves higher target-task performance than direct constrained training while reducing audit divergence on math and code and better preserving held-out capabilities across four backbones from 3B to 9B; magnitudes are not stated.
n9urR0xk8V.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that studying the optimization path rather than adding another regularizer is a novel and practically relevant angle, with a careful protocol and reasonable ablations.
n9urR0xk8V.main_concern: Evidence is narrow (two 3B models, math and code tasks, three seeds) and the path-tracking theory rests on assumptions not verified for the actual training procedure.

6lDsDQnFPa.one_liner: Reuses a block-diffusion drafter for multi-pass prefix-conditioned refinement, certifying a common prefix before linear target verification in speculative decoding.
6lDsDQnFPa.problem: Block-diffusion drafters predict token blocks in parallel, so later predictions cannot condition on tokens selected earlier in the same pass.
6lDsDQnFPa.method: Branch-Jacobi reuses one DFlash-style drafter over several passes, each packing prefix-MASK branches into one forward call, and consecutive first-MASK checks identify the proposal's common prefix with a drafter-autoregressive path. One complete branch is selected to extend certification before linear target verification, and moving-anchor training with causal prefix supervision aligns the drafter with variable-prefix queries.
6lDsDQnFPa.key_idea: Pack several prefix-MASK branches in one drafter call and use first-MASK consistency checks to certify the prefix that matches the drafter's autoregressive path.
6lDsDQnFPa.evidence: Seven math, code, and chat benchmarks on Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B at temperatures 0 and 1 with a three-layer drafter using three passes per cycle, plus a proof of sound prefix certification for deterministic greedy drafting.
6lDsDQnFPa.claimed_gains: A three-layer drafter with three passes per cycle achieves 4.93-6.40x geometric-mean decode-stage speedups over target autoregressive decoding, exceeding DFlash by 25.3-29.2% while increasing average acceptance length.
6lDsDQnFPa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it gives substantial, consistent speedups over DFlash across seven benchmarks on Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B, and that refinement passes improve target acceptance without extra verification passes.
6lDsDQnFPa.main_concern: Conceptual novelty is limited relative to concurrent drafters (DSpark, xPress, DFlash 2), which are not compared directly, and the evaluation covers only Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B.

WMZ6jD8edI.one_liner: Approximates GELU-like activations under FHE by keeping the exact odd part x/2 and fitting only the even residual polynomially.
WMZ6jD8edI.problem: Nonlinear activations bottleneck neural inference under FHE, which lacks native exponentials, reciprocals, and selection, and high-degree polynomial approximations incur substantial multiplicative depth and latency.
WMZ6jD8edI.method: For activations of the form A(x)=x g(x) with g(-x)=1-g(x), such as GELU, SiLU, fixed-parameter Swish, and the scalar branches of GEGLU/SwiGLU, SPA retains the exact odd component x/2 and approximates only the even residual as a polynomial in x^2. This gives a comparison-free arithmetic kernel.
WMZ6jD8edI.key_idea: Exploit the shared form A(x)=x g(x) with g(-x)=1-g(x) to keep the odd part exact and spend polynomial degree only on the even residual in x^2.
WMZ6jD8edI.evidence: Plaintext experiments with Gemma-4-E2B and Llama-3.2-3B without weight updates, and fixed-interval CKKS benchmarks against MOAI and other baselines.
WMZ6jD8edI.claimed_gains: On [-5,5], SPA-balanced achieves a 3.25x speedup over MOAI (ICLR'26) for erf-GELU with comparable (the abstract is cut off), and plaintext tests show downstream performance is largely preserved without weight updates.
WMZ6jD8edI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the construction is simple and drop-in with a clear theoretical foundation, reports results transparently (confidence intervals, failed cases, operation counts), and uses fewer multiplications and levels than most baselines.
WMZ6jD8edI.main_concern: No ablation isolates the structure's benefit from fitting and evaluator effects, since an unstructured fit reaches the same best error, and novelty over BOLT-style x/2 plus polynomial approximations is limited.

0I9lZG51qk.one_liner: Adds global decay and write-aligned erasure to hyper-connections so stream state retention is controlled separately from residual mixing.
0I9lZG51qk.problem: Under mHC's doubly stochastic constraint the stream-average component is left unattenuated as layers add outputs, so mixing alone does not control how much carried state is retained.
0I9lZG51qk.method: GDHC adds explicit retention control alongside the existing read/write maps by combining global decay, which regulates overall retention, with write-aligned erasure, which attenuates old content along the incoming write direction independently of write strength.
0I9lZG51qk.key_idea: Combine a global decay with erasure of old stream content along the incoming write direction, so retention is controlled independently of mixing and write strength.
0I9lZG51qk.evidence: Experiments with mHC and identity-mixer iHC on 4B- and 7B-parameter mixture-of-experts models (0.55B and 0.91B active), plus component ablations and analyses of activation profiles and write-gate mass.
0I9lZG51qk.claimed_gains: GDHC gives lower training loss at both the 4B- and 7B-parameter MoE models (0.55B and 0.91B active parameters) and higher average downstream scores at the larger scale; magnitudes are not stated in the abstract.
0I9lZG51qk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the retention mechanism is well motivated and simple, preserves the hyper-connection read/write interface, and comes with a clearly scoped analysis.
0I9lZG51qk.main_concern: Each variant is trained once and the gains are small (0.13 to 0.25 points downstream on mHC, about 0.004 PPL for combining controls), so without independent-seed uncertainty their reliability is unclear.

uc82ky05qA.one_liner: Training-free guidance for next-scale visual autoregressive models that contrasts predictions under generated versus corrupted prefixes.
uc82ky05qA.problem: Autoregressive image and video generators trained on teacher-forced histories sample from their own prefixes at inference, creating exposure bias, while existing remedies change training and sampling-time guidance mainly strengthens external conditions.
uc82ky05qA.method: VPG contrasts predictions under the generated and corrupted prefixes and favors candidates that are both sensitive to and positively supported by the generated prefix. This encourages continuations consistent with the realized visual history and reduces prefix drift at inference.
uc82ky05qA.key_idea: Contrast next-scale predictions under the generated prefix and a corrupted prefix, and favor candidates that are sensitive to and supported by the generated prefix.
uc82ky05qA.evidence: Class-conditional generation with VAR, text-to-image with Infinity, and text-to-video with InfinityStar, with five-seed statistics on VAR and ablations of the corruption design and alternative references.
uc82ky05qA.claimed_gains: VPG reduces FID on VAR by 0.40 on average, raises DPG-Bench on Infinity, and improves VBench Overall on InfinityStar in all four seeds (by 0.22 on average).
uc82ky05qA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it is a simple, training-free method that applies directly to released checkpoints, with consistent gains across VAR sizes and conditioning types and informative ablations.
uc82ky05qA.main_concern: Video evidence is thin, with VBench gains of the order of seed variance and a schedule apparently chosen on the benchmark, and the headline VAR numbers cost about twice the Transformer FLOPs without a matched-compute comparison.

AiTVmLVnt1.one_liner: Jointly trains acting and memory editing in one RL update, rewarding each memory edit by its transfer to other tasks.
AiTVmLVnt1.problem: Agentic RL delivers each episode to the policy only as a scalar outcome reward, and a memory that helps its source episode may not help other tasks or improve the agent when used for training.
AiTVmLVnt1.method: MECA trains a single policy to solve tasks and to maintain procedural memory by adding, revising, and removing memories. Each edit is rewarded by its transfer, the change in success on tasks it was not written from, and the same signal decides whether a memory stays external or is consolidated into the parameters through self-distillation.
AiTVmLVnt1.key_idea: Reward each memory edit by its success change on other tasks, and use that transfer signal to choose which memories are self-distilled into parameters.
AiTVmLVnt1.evidence: ALFWorld, WebShop, and Search-QA with three backbones against controlled agentic RL and memory-based baselines, plus ablations and memory-removed evaluations.
AiTVmLVnt1.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract only claims MECA outperforms controlled agentic RL and memory-based baselines, including GiGPO trained on as many trajectories, before it is cut off.
AiTVmLVnt1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree memory editing and consolidation is a timely problem and that the many ablations, diagnostic studies, and controlled comparisons give useful evidence.
AiTVmLVnt1.main_concern: Gains look modest relative to MECA's extra rollout overhead (64 intervention rollouts per iteration), RL results come from single training runs, and the comparability of published baseline numbers is unclear.

ynKL4DgTp7.one_liner: Replaces clipping in LLM policy optimization with a per-position projection onto a chi-squared ball around the old policy.
ynKL4DgTp7.problem: The error of one RL update on data written by the model's previous version splits into a bias term, from scoring the new policy on old-policy states, and a variance term, from finite-batch estimation.
ynKL4DgTp7.method: CHIP is a projection layer that replaces the actor's proposed next-token distribution at every sampled position with the closest distribution inside the chi-squared ball around the old policy. The solution has a normalized weighted harmonic form governed by one scalar, with closed-form gradients by implicit differentiation, and it takes the place of clipping.
ynKL4DgTp7.key_idea: One chi-squared budget bounds both the variance of importance weights and the total-variation term in the bias bound, enforced by projecting each next-token distribution onto the chi-squared ball.
ynKL4DgTp7.evidence: Five estimator families and a six-scale Qwen3 ladder with five policy-optimization algorithms, supported by a lemma and propositions on the chi-squared bounds.
ynKL4DgTp7.claimed_gains: Replacing clipping with CHIP raises validation accuracy in all five estimator families by +0.7 to +10.7 points, leads in seventeen of eighteen cells of a six-scale Qwen3 ladder, and adds less than 1% to each training step.
ynKL4DgTp7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the chi-squared view is theoretically principled and clearly framed, that the layer is cheap and easy to integrate into existing recipes, and that experiments span several Qwen3 scales and estimators.
ynKL4DgTp7.main_concern: Theorem 1 assumes a discount below 1 while episodic LLM RL is typically undiscounted, and results come from single runs without independent-seed variance or a comparison with the closest prior work, TROLL.

cHzpqBAuPv.one_liner: Values clients by sampled Owen values and edges by exactly solving the small edge game over composable class feature summaries.
cHzpqBAuPv.problem: In hierarchical federated learning, summing sampled client values within each edge conserves the total exactly yet can misallocate individual edges without any visible signal.
cHzpqBAuPv.method: FedCCE has clients upload per-class feature summaries whose counts, means, and variances compose exactly under union, so coalition utility follows from cached summaries without retraining. It samples client Owen values under a fixed budget and solves the much smaller edge quotient game exactly.
cHzpqBAuPv.key_idea: Give each hierarchy level its own estimator: sample the large client game, enumerate the small edge game exactly, and use composable summaries to evaluate any coalition without retraining.
cHzpqBAuPv.evidence: Four image benchmarks with 232 runs at 50 or 100 clients, summary-based and model-based utilities, and a proof that the extra utility calls depend on the number of edges but not clients.
cHzpqBAuPv.claimed_gains: Summing budgeted client values identifies the most valuable edge in only 46% of 232 runs with 50 or 100 clients even at the largest budget, whereas FedCCE identifies it in every run (the abstract is cut off after 'needs roughly').
cHzpqBAuPv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it identifies a real pitfall, that exact conservation of the total does not ensure correct edge-level allocation, and that the resolution-matched design with composable summaries is intuitive and efficient.
cHzpqBAuPv.main_concern: The summary-based utility is a surrogate whose agreement with model-based attribution is only moderate (average edge correlation 0.550), so exact computation of this game may not reflect the deployed model.

rtwwv7iOPS.one_liner: Erases a sensitive concept with a conditional autoencoder trained on reconstruction plus independence, which also enables concept steering at inference.
rtwwv7iOPS.problem: Linear erasure guarantees hold only against linear probes, while nonlinear methods erase more strongly but lack formal guarantees and often sacrifice utility.
rtwwv7iOPS.method: A conditional autoencoder framework with reconstruction and independence terms, for which perfect reconstruction plus population-level independence is shown sufficient for perfect nonlinear guardedness under stated assumptions, with preservation guarantees when reconstruction is imperfect. Changing only the concept at inference yields concept conversion as a by-product.
rtwwv7iOPS.key_idea: Train a conditional autoencoder whose latent is independent of the sensitive attribute while the decoder, given the attribute, reconstructs the input, so erasure removes only that attribute.
rtwwv7iOPS.evidence: Multiple datasets, sensitive attributes, and language models (including Bias in Bios with BERT and Dial tasks per reviewers), compared with linear and nonlinear erasure baselines including supervised variants.
rtwwv7iOPS.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract claims a superior utility-erasure trade-off, surpassing supervised variants of competing methods without target-task labels, and substantially faster convergence, without numbers.
rtwwv7iOPS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the objective is simple (reconstruction and independence terms only), avoids adversarial or iterative eigen-solver training, trains faster, and gives favorable utility-erasure trade-offs.
rtwwv7iOPS.main_concern: The theory is seen as thin and rests on an independence assumption that may fail in real text, and the method is not compared with earlier conditional-autoencoder fair-representation approaches.

sfHA6sXTuv.one_liner: Learns which VLA tokens to reuse via learnable-query importance scores and a recurrent visual memory, with linear-warmup training.
sfHA6sXTuv.problem: VLA caching decisions rely on hand-crafted proxy signals misaligned with control policy demands and use only adjacent frames, without longer-term temporal context.
sfHA6sXTuv.method: MemCache uses learnable query banks to generate token-level importance scores optimized with the control objective, and a recurrent visual memory state to capture long-range dependencies and give history-aware corrections to caching decisions. A linear-warmup training strategy is also developed (the abstract is cut off).
sfHA6sXTuv.key_idea: Learn token caching end-to-end from the action loss with learnable query banks, and correct caching decisions using a recurrent visual memory of past frames.
sfHA6sXTuv.evidence: Three VLA architectures on LIBERO and SIMPLER against eight caching and pruning baselines, with latency measured on a single RTX 4090.
sfHA6sXTuv.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract is cut off before any results are given.
sfHA6sXTuv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that learning caching decisions end-to-end under the action objective is sensible and that the evaluation spans three VLA architectures and two benchmarks with measured latency.
sfHA6sXTuv.main_concern: Evidence for the central long-term memory contribution is weak, since adding memory improves average success by only 0.2 to 0.3 points in the ablations, without memory-reset or history-length controls.

psiJhbg3N3.one_liner: Learns class-dependent, quality-conditioned feature displacements from canonical high-quality class references for LiDAR out-of-distribution detection.
psiJhbg3N3.problem: Quality-induced feature shifts of in-distribution LiDAR observations can be mistaken for anomalies or absorbed as uncontrolled intra-class variation, making legitimate shifts hard to separate from genuine OOD deviations.
psiJhbg3N3.method: QuaD builds canonical class references from reliable high-quality observations and predicts class-dependent, quality-conditioned feature displacements. The displacements are constrained during training so quality shifts are accommodated while displacement-corrected representations stay consistent with the canonical class structure, and inference combines semantic, contrastive, and displacement evidence.
psiJhbg3N3.key_idea: Model sensing-induced representation shift as a learned displacement from a canonical class anchor conditioned on observation quality, and constrain displacement-corrected features to match that anchor.
psiJhbg3N3.evidence: Four LiDAR OOD benchmarks including synthetic and real-world sets (nuScenes-OoD, STU) compared with LIDO, with component ablations run on nuScenes-OoD.
psiJhbg3N3.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract is cut off before any results are given.
psiJhbg3N3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it addresses a real LiDAR-specific confound (range- and density-induced shift) and improves OOD detection across LiDAR benchmarks, particularly AP and FPR@95, with extensive ablations.
psiJhbg3N3.main_concern: Novelty is questioned because range- and density-induced feature variation was addressed by prior work (DDFE, DOODLE), and stronger published STU results (NDP-EE) make the broad state-of-the-art claim too strong.

Ul650mx1in.one_liner: Aligns few-step generators to black-box rewards by training a flow policy over initial noise while keeping the generator frozen.
Ul650mx1in.problem: Few-step generative models are hard to steer with black-box rewards, since direct RL fine-tuning suffers severe reward over-optimization and test-time scaling sacrifices the efficiency advantage of few-step generation.
Ul650mx1in.method: NPO learns an amortized flow policy over the generator's initial noise space that transports Gaussian noise to a reward-tilted noise distribution, whose pushforward through the frozen generator is the reward-tilted output distribution. ELBO-based likelihood estimation improves sample efficiency during training.
Ul650mx1in.key_idea: Learn a flow policy that maps Gaussian noise to a reward-tilted noise distribution, so the frozen generator's pushforward equals the reward-tilted output distribution.
Ul650mx1in.evidence: Three modalities and four generators across 1, 4, and 5 steps, compared with direct generator fine-tuning, test-time noise optimisation, and noise-policy baselines, including a baseline differing only in the likelihood estimator and cost tables.
Ul650mx1in.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract claims a better reward-quality trade-off than direct fine-tuning and inference that adds only a lightweight noise-sampling step, without numbers.
Ul650mx1in.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is clearly written and evaluated broadly across modalities and alignment-method categories, and that keeping the generator frozen gives stability and a better reward-quality trade-off than fine-tuning.
Ul650mx1in.main_concern: Learning only a tilted initial-noise distribution for deterministic generators is already known in prior work, leaving the ELBO-based policy-gradient objective, whose design is loosely grounded in theory, as the main novelty.

fuXZocOUBF.one_liner: Detects audio-visual deepfakes via first-order acoustic responses to mouth queries, with generator sync-objective directions projected out.
fuXZocOUBF.problem: A generator optimized for an audio-visual synchronization objective can match that objective at an observed sample while keeping a different local articulatory response, which weakens detectors that rely on synchronization cues.
fuXZocOUBF.method: OtO is an authentic-only test of how acoustic features inferred by a visual-to-acoustic predictor change under local mouth-tangent queries. It maps declared generator objectives into the acoustic response space and tests the complementary response conditioned on the observed audio, using one consistent residual for learning, projection, and probe selection.
fuXZocOUBF.key_idea: Project declared generator-objective directions out of the predictor's local acoustic response to mouth-tangent queries and test the remaining complementary response, trained only on authentic videos.
fuXZocOUBF.evidence: A controlled synchronization-weight sweep and a common cross-domain protocol on MMDF and HiFi-AVDF, with ablations over matched, mismatched, and random directions.
fuXZocOUBF.claimed_gains: In a synchronization-weight sweep the zero-order cosine detector falls from 88.9 to 66.9 AUROC while the projected first-order test stays between 90.2 and 90.7, and OtO reaches 92.0% AUROC on MMDF and 84.1% on HiFi-AVDF, with 3.6 and 4.8 points attributable to objective-direction removal beyond audio conditioning.
fuXZocOUBF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that testing first-order responses outside the generator objective is an interesting idea that trains on real videos only and beats the selected baselines, with solid ablations.
fuXZocOUBF.main_concern: Key implementation details are missing (the mouth-mesh model, the controlled generators' architectures and exact sync losses, tracker settings), which makes the controlled experiments hard to follow or reproduce.

zleftuH21d.one_liner: Adapts pretrained LLMs with LoRA in hyperbolic space and radial regularization to predict future lab values from treatment sequences.
zleftuH21d.problem: LLMs typically use Euclidean representation spaces that poorly capture the hierarchical structure of medical concepts and the rapidly expanding state space of severe patients.
zleftuH21d.method: TheraWorld predicts future lab values and patient-state trends from historical records and observed treatment sequences, adapting pretrained LLMs with LoRA in hyperbolic space. It adds hyperbolic consistency and severity-aware radial regularization, and is trained on a newly built treatment-round-based EHR dataset.
zleftuH21d.key_idea: Adapt the LLM in hyperbolic space and regularize the radius to track patient severity, so representation geometry reflects the hierarchy and severity of clinical states.
zleftuH21d.evidence: A treatment-round EHR dataset (MIMIC-IV per reviewers) evaluated across multiple model scales against 18 baselines including medical LLMs, with LoRA and SFT comparisons and ablations.
zleftuH21d.claimed_gains: TheraWorld achieves the best average score of 72.10, outperforming MedGemma-27B (67.30) and GLM-5.1 (69.06).
zleftuH21d.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the task is well motivated by treatment-round, intervention-conditioned prediction, the paper is clear with a helpful appendix, and TheraWorld beats the compared LLMs, including medical ones, on the reported scores.
zleftuH21d.main_concern: The benefit of hyperbolic geometry is not isolated, since HypLoRA alone is worse than Euclidean LoRA at 8B and the LoRA and SFT baselines may be under-tuned, and calling a single-institution MIMIC-IV model a world model is seen as overclaiming.

0gOR2H6hgi.one_liner: Constructs two learning problems with near-identical statistical profiles but separated streaming memory requirements, refuting a robust-SQ characterization conjecture.
0gOR2H6hgi.problem: It is unclear whether learning problems with almost interchangeable examples must need the same memory, which bears on the conjecture of Gonen, Lovett and Moshkovitz (NeurIPS 2020) that bounded robust-SQ profiles characterize bounded-memory learning.
0gOR2H6hgi.method: For every fixed B they build explicit finite realizable problems with N concepts on N uniformly sampled points (R = log2 N) whose labeled-sample experiments have Le Cam distance at most R^-B, with identical base Gram matrices and robust-SQ profiles up to radius Theta(sqrt(R/log R)). The construction replaces rare binary parity observations by field equations.
0gOR2H6hgi.key_idea: Swap rare binary parity observations for field equations: pairwise correlations and statistical experiments match, but one problem is learnable in small memory and the other is not.
0gOR2H6hgi.evidence: Theoretical constructions and proofs (with proof sketches); no experiments are described.
0gOR2H6hgi.claimed_gains: One problem admits exact one-pass learning with R^O_B(1) samples and O(R^2/log R) bits, while the other requires Omega_p(R^2) bits or N^Omega_p(1) samples for every fixed pass count p, even for improper learners with error 1/64.
0gOR2H6hgi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the construction is technically elegant and a substantial theoretical contribution, simultaneously matching Gram matrices, achieving vanishing Le Cam distance, and separating streaming-memory complexity.
0gOR2H6hgi.main_concern: The presentation is technically dense, especially the introduction, and one reviewer questions the motivation and significance of refuting the Gonen et al. conjecture.

W5b35T1QeN.one_liner: Learns a graph surrogate over diffusion residuals whose posterior response operator drives both reconstruction refinement and measurement selection.
W5b35T1QeN.problem: Active grounding of a frozen diffusion prior must decide where to measure next and how to use measurements to refine the reconstruction, and posterior-ensemble methods need repeated ensemble generation and capture posterior geometry only through empirical statistics.
W5b35T1QeN.method: GPARA learns a context-dependent graph surrogate over diffusion prediction residuals, giving a reusable posterior response operator that propagates measurement innovations to unobserved variables and ranks candidate measurements by weighted posterior-risk reduction. A bounded learned residual calibrates the analytic utility, and a small prior ensemble is generated once and reconditioned.
W5b35T1QeN.key_idea: One learned graph-based posterior response operator both propagates new measurements to unobserved variables and scores candidate measurements, tying refinement to acquisition.
W5b35T1QeN.evidence: Two reconstruction tasks spanning wireless sensing and computer vision against baselines such as AdaSense, with ablations, and a proposition showing alignment of the analytic utility under a matched graph-Gaussian surrogate.
W5b35T1QeN.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract only claims consistent improvements in refinement and active acquisition over the evaluated baselines on two reconstruction tasks.
W5b35T1QeN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the shared graph-posterior response that couples refinement and acquisition is principled and that the experiments separate measurement selection from reconstruction quality.
W5b35T1QeN.main_concern: Learning the graph adds little, since learned edge weights improve RMSE over a uniform graph by only about 2% in Table 4(a) and the comparison is not made in the full active-acquisition pipeline.

soYGewplLf.one_liner: Adds explicit negative supervision on in-context distractor labels to meta-trained multimodal in-context learning for fine-grained categorization.
soYGewplLf.problem: Cross-entropy meta-training supervises the correct label but does not explicitly penalize incorrect continuations, and it raises both target and distractor scores, partly offsetting gains in the discriminative margin.
soYGewplLf.method: CLOUD (Contrastive Likelihood Only Upon Divergence) complements target-label learning with explicit negative supervision on in-context distractor labels. Reviewers note a bounded penalty, a shared prefix gating mechanism, and CLIP-derived centroids used in training.
soYGewplLf.key_idea: Add a bounded contrastive likelihood penalty on distractor labels applied only once generation diverges from the target label, alongside cross-entropy.
soYGewplLf.evidence: Three backbone configurations on six held-out natural fine-grained benchmarks and three specialized benchmarks, with ablations and training on a small set of datasets (Oxford Pets and DTD per a reviewer).
soYGewplLf.claimed_gains: CLOUD improves accuracy over CE-based Meta-ICL by 1.74-2.21% on six held-out natural fine-grained benchmarks and 2.14-6.11% on three specialized benchmarks, and Qwen3-VL-2B with CLOUD outperforms Qwen3-VL-32B with vanilla ICL by 4.63% on average across all nine benchmarks.
soYGewplLf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree explicit negative supervision on close classes gives consistent gains over CE-based Meta-ICL across backbones and datasets, supported by detailed ablations.
soYGewplLf.main_concern: Novelty is limited because the negative supervision resembles unlikelihood training, direct competitors (CIRCLES, ContextNav, DARA, Fine-R1) are not compared under identical settings, and the main results are single runs.

zYP7dMwvwB.one_liner: Extrapolates RL progress seen in sparse-autoencoder feature changes through a brief activation-matching update outside the RL reward channel.
zYP7dMwvwB.problem: RL for LLMs relies on costly on-policy sampling, and the representational trajectory traversed during RL is not exploited to improve training efficiency.
zYP7dMwvwB.method: The token-aligned change in SAE feature activations from the pre-RL to the current model forms a Delta-SAE signal. On a fixed set of guidance texts, PUSH resolves it into dynamic features, extends their per-token targets along established directions, and fits them in a minute-scale activation-matching update, after which standard RL resumes under its original objective.
zYP7dMwvwB.key_idea: Take the low-dimensional direction along which SAE feature activations drift during RL and extrapolate it as per-token activation-matching targets in a short auxiliary update.
zYP7dMwvwB.evidence: Code generation (Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct on AceCode with MBPP transfer checks) and math (Qwen2.5-Math-7B and DeepSeekMath-Instruct-7B on GSM8K, one seed each) against SFT, dense and PCA activation extrapolation, and weight extrapolation, with ablations.
zYP7dMwvwB.claimed_gains: not stated for PUSH itself; the abstract reports that five final-layer features account for 96.83% of the aggregate squared norm of the Delta-SAE signal in code generation, and the TLDR says PUSH reaches matched performance with fewer rollouts.
zYP7dMwvwB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the idea of reusing historical representation changes is clear and testable, beats extrapolation and SFT baselines at most starting points, with ablations showing the SAE structure matters, and is pluggable.
zYP7dMwvwB.main_concern: Final-performance gains are modest and the multi-seed evidence is confined to one code model and dataset, with single-seed math runs and negative gains when PUSH is applied late in training.

wcwqo27HIQ.one_liner: Shows pre-existing intent-understanding attention heads causally shape emergent misalignment, and mitigates it by temporarily ablating them early in fine-tuning.
wcwqo27HIQ.problem: It is unclear why narrow fine-tuning induces broadly generalized harmful behavior (emergent misalignment), beyond links to global malicious personas, which limits understanding and proactive prevention.
wcwqo27HIQ.method: They ablate and restore attention heads responsible for intent understanding during fine-tuning to test their causal role. They then propose Restored Intent Head Ablation (RIHA), which temporarily ablates intent heads during early fine-tuning.
wcwqo27HIQ.key_idea: Ablate intent-understanding attention heads during early fine-tuning and restore them later, which leaves a persistent effect on the optimization trajectory and attenuates misaligned persona features.
wcwqo27HIQ.evidence: Ablation-and-restoration runs during fine-tuning, extended training, representation-level analysis of persona features, random-head controls, and MMLU checks (1000 questions), plus RIHA combined with other mitigations.
wcwqo27HIQ.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract says RIHA suppresses emergent misalignment and can complement and amplify existing mitigation methods, without numbers.
wcwqo27HIQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the intervention study linking pre-existing heads to fine-tuning dynamics is interesting, with persistent effects after the heads are restored, and that RIHA is simple and combinable with other mitigations.
wcwqo27HIQ.main_concern: Evidence for an intent-specific mechanism is weak, since random-head ablation also substantially reduces misalignment in some settings and the random controls are not matched, and side effects of RIHA are barely tested.

hvO7ZzQiqG.one_liner: Plug-in gates for kernel-generating agents that reject candidates failing static dependency analysis or dynamic bitwise batch-invariance checks.
hvO7ZzQiqG.problem: LLM serving batches requests dynamically, so kernels lacking batch invariance can change numerical outputs for unchanged inputs, and existing kernel generation agents focus on correctness and efficiency and overlook this.
hvO7ZzQiqG.method: BIEvolve combines contract-guided static dependency analysis with dynamic validation of bitwise consistency across batch contexts. It is integrated as successive acceptance gates in the agent's optimization loop that reject risky or non-invariant candidates before performance benchmarking and return feedback to the agent.
hvO7ZzQiqG.key_idea: Insert static dependency-contract and dynamic bitwise-consistency gates before performance benchmarking, returning failure feedback to the kernel-optimizing agent.
hvO7ZzQiqG.evidence: An audit of 83 batch-applicable released kernel artifacts and experiments with three agent frameworks under baseline and BI-aware generation on real-world LLM serving tasks.
hvO7ZzQiqG.claimed_gains: The audit finds 19 confirmed BI violations among 83 batch-applicable released artifacts, and BIEvolve improves the BI pass rate from 67.6% to 91.9% while retaining 91.8% of the baseline geometric mean speedup.
hvO7ZzQiqG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it identifies a concrete, practical failure mode that tolerance-based correctness misses, and that the gates plug into several agent frameworks and improve BI pass rates.
hvO7ZzQiqG.main_concern: The final batch-invariance audit is under-specified: the contexts used to confirm violations are not enumerated, residual failures below a 100% pass rate are unexplained, and evaluation may reuse the gates' contexts.

PRYh1k0Fce.one_liner: Learns nested sensor layouts across budgets in one training run using ordered queries and a frozen reconstructor.
PRYh1k0Fce.problem: Existing sensor placement methods optimize layouts for a single sensor budget, so any budget change requires reoptimizing all sensor locations.
PRYh1k0Fce.method: BASP encodes the physical field prior into spatial features, and ordered sensor queries sequentially generate continuous coordinates through cross attention to these features with spatial suppression, forming nested layouts. A pretrained frozen reconstructor supervises reconstruction at a randomly sampled budget and at the maximum budget during training.
PRYh1k0Fce.key_idea: Generate sensor coordinates sequentially from ordered queries so every prefix is a valid layout, and train with random-budget plus maximum-budget reconstruction loss so early sensors stay informative.
PRYh1k0Fce.evidence: Four datasets with four reconstructors against independent coordinate optimization, random and uniform sampling, D-, A-, and E-optimal placement, and nested baselines such as greedy fixed-coordinates and nested pivot QR.
PRYh1k0Fce.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract only claims lower reconstruction errors than the listed placement baselines in most settings, with multiple budgets supported in one training run.
PRYh1k0Fce.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it is a practical reconstruction-aware approach that avoids reoptimizing or relocating sensors when budgets change, with an evaluation over four datasets and four reconstructors showing advantages in most settings.
PRYh1k0Fce.main_concern: Simpler nested baselines (a reconstruction-aware greedy method, fixed-budget PlaceNet) are missing, novelty over sequential sensor placement is not established, and some differences are tiny (0.2003 versus 0.2004).

FiUKddN4Jq.one_liner: Proves an explicit threshold separating polynomial-time approximation from PPAD-completeness for the regularized best-response gap in entropy-regularized binary games.
FiUKddN4Jq.problem: Entropy regularization gives smooth, unique best responses, yet equilibrium computation can remain hard, and this limitation had not been quantified for binary games.
FiUKddN4Jq.method: For binary games they give an explicit threshold on the largest unilateral improvement in regularized payoff. On every fixed bounded interval of interaction strength, tolerances above it admit polynomial-time algorithms and finding solutions below it is PPAD-complete with inverse-polynomial margins.
FiUKddN4Jq.key_idea: A single scalar identity links a contraction-based algorithm and a hardness reduction, so the same threshold gives both the polynomial-time upper bound and the PPAD-hardness lower bound.
FiUKddN4Jq.evidence: Theoretical results only, with hardness shown to persist under fixed regularization, bounded payoffs, and sparse interactions (a constant number of neighbors per player).
FiUKddN4Jq.claimed_gains: not stated; the results are theoretical and the abstract gives no numerical gains.
FiUKddN4Jq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is well motivated and that sharp algorithms with matching hardness results are interesting, with hardness holding under fixed regularization, bounded payoffs, and constant neighbors.
FiUKddN4Jq.main_concern: The presentation is hard to follow and not self-contained, with heavy notation, an entropy term never introduced explicitly, and an unclear reduction, and some parameter regimes remain open.

ba5rWVXYJe.one_liner: Separates acoustic arrival estimation from navigation direction in audio-visual navigation with a target-conditioned DOA module and depth-conditioned affordance model.
ba5rWVXYJe.problem: Prior audio-visual navigation methods derive guidance from the geometric source direction, which struggles indoors where multi-source interference hides target cues and reverberation makes the perceived acoustic DOA diverge from the direct source path.
ba5rWVXYJe.method: TargetDOA extracts target-specific arrival distributions from acoustic mixtures, supervised with paired target-only references that exclude competing sources while preserving propagation. DREAM then reshapes these distributions into reward-aligned navigation direction preferences using local geometry and egomotion-aligned history.
ba5rWVXYJe.key_idea: Supervise a target-conditioned arrival distribution with target-only reverberant references, then convert it into navigation direction preferences using depth and pose-aligned history.
ba5rWVXYJe.evidence: Single-source and multi-source navigation evaluations (the multi-source comparison is against ENMuS3), ablations of DREAM, and a benchmark introduced in the cut-off part of the abstract.
ba5rWVXYJe.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract is cut off before any results are given.
ba5rWVXYJe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating acoustic arrival direction from navigation direction is well motivated for multi-source reverberant scenes, and that target-only supervision and the TargetDOA and DREAM modules are sensible and clearly described.
ba5rWVXYJe.main_concern: The claim that acoustic-arrival supervision beats geometric source-direction supervision is not tested in a controlled navigation experiment, and the main multi-source comparison uses only one recent baseline.

79XDOKNJ2l.one_liner: Allocates pre-training tokens across clusters by held-out loss reduction and selects within clusters by length-adjusted inverse-density sampling.
79XDOKNJ2l.problem: Language-model pre-training must split a fixed token budget across semantic regions and pick examples within each, where informative clusters can get too little capacity and budgets fill with redundant examples.
79XDOKNJ2l.method: GRIP allocates tokens across clusters using static quality scores and normalized held-out loss reductions measured under a rapid adaptation probe. Within each cluster it uses length-adjusted inverse-density sampling to improve geometric coverage while retaining long documents.
79XDOKNJ2l.key_idea: Allocate cluster budgets by measured loss reduction under a short adaptation probe, and correct inverse-density sampling for the length bias of averaged document embeddings.
79XDOKNJ2l.evidence: Eight code benchmarks with 8B and 16B mixture-of-experts models trained on up to 300B tokens (three to five paired seeds), an ablation of allocation and selection, and a separate 8B FineWeb experiment, all against UniGeM.
79XDOKNJ2l.claimed_gains: At 300B tokens GRIP beats UniGeM by 0.9 and 1.3 average-score points for the 8B and 16B models, at 100B tokens the 8B model scores 35.5 ± 0.3 (1.2 points above UniGeM), and on FineWeb it improves mean accuracy across four tasks by 3.20 percentage points and cuts held-out perplexity by 3.02%.
79XDOKNJ2l.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that data selection for pre-training is an important problem and that the evaluation is large-scale, training 8B and 16B MoE models from scratch with multiple seeds.
79XDOKNJ2l.main_concern: The advantage over UniGeM depends on a length exponent chosen without a separate validation set, since GRIP scores below UniGeM without length correction, and evaluation is limited mainly to code data.

GLX4jwxjQ6.one_liner: Splits aerial-ground scenes into root regions with local instance codebooks, then learns cross-root connectivity to fuse leaves into global instances.
GLX4jwxjQ6.problem: Instance-level semantics in large aerial-ground scenes are hard because per-view observations are sparse over a large identity space and projected scale and detail vary across views, yielding over- or under-segmented 2D masks with inconsistent supervision.
GLX4jwxjQ6.method: SSCL organizes the scene into spatial root regions, each with a compact codebook of leaves for local instance identities, and jointly learns cross-root connectivity to fuse leaves into globally consistent instances. A granularity-aware codebook learning method mitigates conflicting instance supervision, and the AG-Seg benchmark is introduced.
GLX4jwxjQ6.key_idea: Give each spatial root its own small codebook of instance leaves and learn cross-root connectivity, supervised by 2D mask co-occurrence, to merge leaves into global identities.
GLX4jwxjQ6.evidence: Experiments on the new AG-Seg benchmark (seven scenes) for click-based instance segmentation and text-based open-vocabulary retrieval, with ablations and rendering-efficiency results.
GLX4jwxjQ6.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract only claims substantial improvements over state-of-the-art methods on AG-Seg in both instance segmentation and open-vocabulary retrieval.
GLX4jwxjQ6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the motivation and design are coherent, with local codebooks and cross-region association addressing sparse view coverage, that results beat baselines on all scenes, and that AG-Seg is a useful benchmark.
GLX4jwxjQ6.main_concern: The central claim of cross-view global instance consistency is not directly measured, since the metrics are per-image 2D IoU that can score high even when the same building gets conflicting IDs across aerial and ground views.

hP1yMU1rEj.one_liner: Post-training ternarization of LLMs via low-rank ternary factorization, mixed-rank allocation, and task-aligned refinement.
hP1yMU1rEj.problem: Existing ternary post-training quantization methods have limited ternary representation capacity, ignore heterogeneous sensitivity across Transformer modules, and optimize local reconstruction that mismatches model-level objectives.
hP1yMU1rEj.method: Ternova combines Hessian-Aware Annealed Ternary Factorization (HATF), Sensitivity-Reweighted Mixed-Rank Allocation (SRMA), and Task-Aligned Ternary Refinement (TATR, with global scale calibration and sparse topology refinement), keeping a ternary form without extra dense high-precision branches.
hP1yMU1rEj.key_idea: Represent weights as low-rank ternary factors found by sensitivity-aware factorization with annealed discrete refinement, allocate rank per module by sensitivity, and calibrate scales and topology against task behavior.
hP1yMU1rEj.evidence: Experiments across diverse LLM families (abstract truncated), with tables on MMLU, HumanEval, and GSM8K, a storage-matched DBF+PV comparison, and component ablations per reviews.
hP1yMU1rEj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is practically important and the three components address plausible sources of compression error in a coherent framework evaluated on several model families.
hP1yMU1rEj.main_concern: Baselines are missing or unmatched: recent ternary PTQ methods (PT2-LLM, PTQTP) are absent, and DBF+PV is not compared at matched optimization cost, so gains cannot be attributed to the proposed mechanisms.

RRXBxewWmQ.one_liner: Trains a pre-call routing value estimator jointly with a training-only response-informed estimator over a shared representation for multi-turn LLM routing.
RRXBxewWmQ.problem: Multi-turn routing must pick each model before its response exists, and intermediate choices have no independent task-quality label because success is revealed only after the interaction ends.
RRXBxewWmQ.method: RIVET trains a deployable Routing Value Estimator (RVE) on pre-call information and a training-only Response-Informed Value Estimator (RIVE) that also observes the realized response; both regress the same discounted return and share a state-model representation, and inference uses RVE alone.
RRXBxewWmQ.key_idea: Condition an auxiliary value estimator on the realized response so response-induced return variation becomes an observed covariate, reducing error in the shared representation the pre-call router uses.
RRXBxewWmQ.evidence: 141 held-out MINT tasks with six candidate models, compared against MTRouter and fixed-model baselines such as Avengers-Pro, plus a result that the auxiliary regression provably reduces estimation error of the shared representation.
RRXBxewWmQ.claimed_gains: Solves 124 of 141 held-out MINT tasks using 74.7% less total call cost than MTRouter, which solves 120.
RRXBxewWmQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the approach practical and well motivated, with competitive accuracy, clear cost savings over prior routers and no extra model calls at inference.
RRXBxewWmQ.main_concern: Evidence is thin: the MINT gain is four tasks from a single seed without variance, the accuracy-cost frontier is incomplete (Avengers-Pro reaches 85.82% at lower cost), and novelty over privileged-information value learning is limited.

Ze6gLD2MEO.one_liner: Swaps patch and tests in SWE instances to build test-generation tasks verified against damaged patches and rewritten sources.
Ze6gLD2MEO.problem: RL for repository-level coding agents is limited by the supply of executable tasks, and fail-to-pass status alone is satisfied by tests that exercise no behaviour.
Ze6gLD2MEO.method: Exchanging the roles of the reference patch and reference tests in an issue-resolution instance defines a task of writing a test that reproduces the reported behaviour in the existing environment.
