A submitted test must fail on the buggy snapshot and on snapshots with the reference patch damaged, and pass on the repaired snapshot and on behaviour-preserving rewrites of its source.
Ze6gLD2MEO.key_idea: Use the reference tests to decide which damaged-patch variants to keep and require passes on behaviour-preserving source rewrites, so trivial tests cannot earn fail-to-pass reward.
Ze6gLD2MEO.evidence: Conversion of three collections of instances, with a verifier audit, and forty steps of joint reinforcement learning on issue resolution and test generation, evaluated on SWE-Bench Verified, SWE-Bench Pro and TDD-Bench Verified (per reviews).
Ze6gLD2MEO.claimed_gains: The conversion yields 30,605 fail-to-pass test-generation tasks, of which 23,520 pass an audit of their verifiers; the joint-RL gains are cut off in the abstract.
Ze6gLD2MEO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the role-swap idea and the carefully defined, practical verifier compelling, and see the joint training gains and the generated task set as useful.
Ze6gLD2MEO.main_concern: There is no RL run with the plain fail-to-pass reward under identical tasks and hyperparameters, so the gain from the strengthened verifier is not isolated from joint training.

ZShem2YFMC.one_liner: Training-free multi-view visual token pruning using offline PCA subspaces from attention-selected tokens to guide relevance-weighted, diversity-aware selection.
ZShem2YFMC.problem: Processing visual tokens from multiple cameras in driving VLMs is costly, and pruning must keep relevant content and diversity while splitting a limited budget across views.
ZShem2YFMC.method: Offline, text-to-vision attention selects question-relevant tokens from a subset of training data and they are summarized into view-specific PCA subspaces. Online, the stored subspaces estimate token relevance and guide diversity-aware selection before the multimodal projector, jointly across views under a shared budget.
ZShem2YFMC.key_idea: Use view-specific PCA subspaces built offline from attention-selected tokens as a cheap relevance proxy, then select tokens jointly across views under one shared budget.
ZShem2YFMC.evidence: Autonomous-driving benchmarks (DriveLMM-o1 and MAPLM) on driving VLMs including DriveMM, with component ablations and prefill speedup measurements.
ZShem2YFMC.claimed_gains: Improves the DriveLMM-o1 Overall Reasoning score by 1.13 points and the MAPLM average score by 2.53 points over state-of-the-art baselines at about 90% token reduction.
ZShem2YFMC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the offline-subspace relevance prior is a practical training-free design and that ablations show relevance and diversity play complementary roles.
ZShem2YFMC.main_concern: Offline per-benchmark subspaces ignore the current question and their transfer under distribution shift is untested, and novelty over attention-plus-diversity pruning is questioned.

AH85wPRxxy.one_liner: Concept unlearning as distributional alignment to an energy-tilted target, trained with residual nabla-GFlowNet score corrections on diffusion generators.
AH85wPRxxy.problem: Common erasure objectives do not specify which post-unlearning distribution should approximate a retain-only reference, leaving retention of quality, diversity and coverage as an implicit byproduct of heuristic updates.
AH85wPRxxy.method: TILDE defines the target as the minimum-deviation conditional distribution from the pretrained model under a forgetting constraint, an energy-tilted anchor-free target that downweights concept-expressing images while preserving benign relative mass per prompt. It approximates this target with residual nabla-GFlowNet training that learns only a score correction relative to the pretrained sampler.
AH85wPRxxy.key_idea: Define the unlearned model as the closest distribution to the pretrained one under a forgetting constraint, and learn it as a residual score correction via GFlowNet training.
AH85wPRxxy.evidence: Text-to-image diffusion and rectified-flow models including SD v1.5, with retention evaluation over 60+ concepts and ablations mainly on one concept (Pikachu), per reviews.
AH85wPRxxy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the formulation is principled, with a clear motivation for defining the desired post-unlearning distribution through a KL-based target, supported by broad retention experiments.
AH85wPRxxy.main_concern: Each concept needs a separate 2-5 hour optimization with per-concept threshold and scale calibration, and compute comparisons and multi-concept results are missing.

4EHSX5RZEG.one_liner: Compresses reusable LLM skills into an adaptive number of soft tokens, trained in stages to preserve procedural execution.
4EHSX5RZEG.problem: Placing full skill text in every context raises prefill cost and latency, and existing text compression targets factual documents rather than procedural knowledge.
4EHSX5RZEG.method: SKIM is an adaptive multi-resolution soft-token compression framework that creates a different number of soft tokens depending on each skill's complexity and allows lightweight offline compression of frequently updated skills. Reviewers describe a three-stage training design and a selector choosing between two compressed budgets and full text.
4EHSX5RZEG.key_idea: Skill-complexity-dependent soft-token budgets, learned through staged training from content reconstruction to procedural questions to downstream tasks, replace full skill text in the prompt.
4EHSX5RZEG.evidence: Five datasets with Qwen3-8B and Phi-4 (14B), compared with LLMLingua-2 and soft-compression baselines, plus human evaluation, LoRA comparisons, and retrieval tests on a single H20 GPU.
4EHSX5RZEG.claimed_gains: SKIM's fixed-budget configurations compress skills to as few as 15 to 55 percent of their original token length (the result for the adaptive variant is cut off in the abstract).
4EHSX5RZEG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that reducing the cost of repeatedly loaded procedural skills is a practical goal and that the experiments are fairly broad.
4EHSX5RZEG.main_concern: The motivation and baselines are under-supported: no evidence of where existing methods break procedural dependencies, no full-text prefix-caching baseline, and unclear technical novelty over existing compression architectures.

DnofhHOGd3.one_liner: GraphForge synthesizes workspace-agent training tasks and rubrics from evidence graphs built over real files.
DnofhHOGd3.problem: Training working agents needs tasks on many real files with verifiable results, but existing pipelines either generate unrealistic files with models or use real files without task-specific verifiers.
DnofhHOGd3.method: For each task seed, GraphForge crawls real files, builds an evidence graph of their relations, and compiles it into task statements and rubrics with evidence anchors. A rollout checks executability and a revise agent repairs task statements and rubrics against the original files before the final trajectory is collected.
DnofhHOGd3.key_idea: Compile an evidence graph over real workspace files into tasks and rubrics with evidence anchors that tell the judge which files to check for each rubric.
DnofhHOGd3.evidence: Fine-tuning Qwen3.6-27B on 2,169 trajectories, evaluated on GDPVal, Workspace-Bench-Lite, and SpreadsheetBench II, then offline rejection fine-tuning with the rubrics (abstract cut off); reviews cite RL comparisons and a GDPVal overlap audit.
DnofhHOGd3.claimed_gains: GDPVal reaches 1445.7 (+65.7), Workspace-Bench-Lite 63.7 (+7.7), and SpreadsheetBench II 24.0 (+13.7).
DnofhHOGd3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that grounding tasks and rubrics in real workspace files is a practical, traceable way to produce agent training data and that the SFT gains are substantial across scaffolds.
DnofhHOGd3.main_concern: The rubric judge barely penalizes factual corruption (row, number, or citation changes shift scores by only 0.013 to 0.022 versus 0.377 for deleting a worksheet), and the evidence graph's own contribution is not ablated.

cEtOHBR2Rk.one_liner: Z-RoboSTAR harnesses VLMs as System 2 robot planners around a persistent symbolic scene graph, plus a benchmark and distilled model.
cEtOHBR2Rk.problem: Long-horizon manipulation needs a System 2 agent that tracks progress from partial observations as interventions change the world and invalidate earlier beliefs and completed subtasks.
cEtOHBR2Rk.method: A harness built on a dynamically updated symbolic scene graph that serves as a persistent shared state for scene understanding, task progress, and planning, supporting failure recovery and reconciliation. They add Z-RoboSTAR-Bench (57 tabletop scenes) and distill Z-RoboSTAR-27B from trajectories.
cEtOHBR2Rk.key_idea: Keep a dynamically updated symbolic scene graph as the shared state that synchronizes scene beliefs, task progress, and planning, so completed subtasks can be reconsidered.
cEtOHBR2Rk.evidence: An offline open-loop benchmark over 57 tabletop scenes comparing open- and closed-source VLMs, checked by human-executed closed-loop ranking, and real-robot tests on a Galaxea R1 Lite with a fine-tuned pi0.5 System 1 controller.
cEtOHBR2Rk.claimed_gains: Z-RoboSTAR-27B achieves a 63.6% task success rate on real-world long-horizon manipulation tasks (abstract cut off before the ranking).
cEtOHBR2Rk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that maintaining task progress under interventions is a well-motivated problem and that the persistent scene-graph harness with an intervention benchmark is a coherent solution.
cEtOHBR2Rk.main_concern: The advantage over existing scene-graph and feedback-driven replanning systems (such as SayPlan, Thea, and Statler) is not demonstrated, and ablations do not isolate which component drives the gains.

aa4t0nt3mz.one_liner: Rotates gradients in every singular direction but stores optimizer states for only r directions, estimating the rest from neighbors.
aa4t0nt3mz.problem: Low-rank gradient projection couples rotation coverage and state storage through one rank r, so it degrades sharply as r decreases, while full-rank rotation needs the memory to store a basis and states for every direction.
aa4t0nt3mz.method: COAST rotates every direction but keeps optimizer states for only r stored directions, estimating the updates of the remaining directions from their stored neighbors. This rests on the observations that whitened update magnitude stays nearly flat along the spectral index and that adjacent second moments have high cosine similarity.
aa4t0nt3mz.key_idea: Decouple rotation coverage from state storage: rotate all gradient directions in the singular basis while keeping Adam states for only r directions and inferring neighbors' updates.
aa4t0nt3mz.evidence: LLaMA pre-training at multiple scales (60M to 1B per reviews) compared with Adam and low-rank methods.
aa4t0nt3mz.claimed_gains: COAST outperforms Adam with 0.42-0.63x Adam's optimizer memory, improves on low-rank methods at similar memory, and halving the storage budget changes perplexity by less than 1% at every scale.
aa4t0nt3mz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating rotation coverage from state storage is a useful perspective, with consistent pretraining gains over Adam and low-rank baselines and little degradation when storage is halved.
aa4t0nt3mz.main_concern: Practical memory benefit and attribution of gains are not established: comparisons with Muon, SOAP, and similar memory-matched optimizers are missing, measured peak memory barely differs from Adam, and scale stops at 1B.

j7DhswzDqJ.one_liner: Triggers graph retrieval inside diffusion-LM decoding only when the set of graph-linkable entities in the draft expands, accelerating GraphRAG.
j7DhswzDqJ.problem: GraphRAG on autoregressive LMs is slow because generation is sequential, and with diffusion LMs the partially denoised drafts are dynamic and noisy, making synchronous graph retrieval and multi-hop aggregation prohibitively costly.
j7DhswzDqJ.method: Ladder uses event-driven self-clocking retrieval: since 88% of target entities emerge early in the partially denoised state, leading final commitment by 5.7-9.6 steps on average, graph retrieval triggers only when the set of graph-linkable entities expands, giving an asynchronous policy with no learned gate (abstract truncated).
j7DhswzDqJ.key_idea: Use entities emerging in a partially denoised draft as both the trigger and the seed for graph retrieval and propagation, replacing synchronous multi-round retrieval.
j7DhswzDqJ.evidence: Multi-hop reasoning datasets including held-out MuSiQue against six GraphRAG baselines under one controller, with Dream-7B as the diffusion backbone according to reviews (abstract truncated).
j7DhswzDqJ.claimed_gains: Reduces latency by 3.4x while improving multi-hop reasoning accuracy (per the TL;DR).
j7DhswzDqJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that graph retrieval keyed to emerging entities is a clean, well-motivated fit for diffusion decoding and gives large speedups over prior GraphRAG baselines.
j7DhswzDqJ.main_concern: Gains are not attributed: the backbone differs from most baselines (Dream-7B versus Qwen2.5-7B), there is no non-graph retrieval baseline, and retrieving once in a single pass is already slightly faster, so speedup may come from single-pass decoding rather than entity triggering.

jn2HDFcUaG.one_liner: Spiking forecaster that estimates a fractional Fourier order from history and reuses it to reconstruct the future phase.
jn2HDFcUaG.problem: A fixed orthogonal Fourier basis spreads chirp-like signals across many coefficients, limiting sparse spiking forecasting.
jn2HDFcUaG.method: A spiking selector estimates the fractional Fourier order from observed history, the forecasting head predicts residual dynamics, and the same order reconstructs the future phase. Signed Dual-Region Log-Temporal Coding (DR-LTC) covers strong coefficients logarithmically and maps weak ones to zero-event states, and the compact head projects once and reuses current across leaky integrate-and-fire steps.
jn2HDFcUaG.key_idea: Pair an adaptive fractional Fourier input representation with future-phase reconstruction using the same history-estimated order, and encode coefficients sparsely with DR-LTC.
jn2HDFcUaG.evidence: A three-seed repartitioned NeLoRa benchmark against SpikF, a synthetic factorization study, a matched three-epoch coding study, and board-level energy measurements on HM100.
jn2HDFcUaG.claimed_gains: 79.28% spectral peak agreement at spreading factor 10 versus 73.67% for SpikF, with 97.23% fewer core multiply-accumulate operations and 38.3% less mean board-level dynamic energy than SpikF's decoder on HM100.
jn2HDFcUaG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that pairing an adaptive fractional Fourier input with matched future-phase reconstruction is well motivated for chirp-like signals and supported by a controlled 2-by-2 ablation.
jn2HDFcUaG.main_concern: Gains are not cleanly attributed to adaptive fractional representation or spiking computation: a fixed-FFT variant with the same compact head already reaches 75.48% agreement, so most MAC savings come from the smaller head.

AHOdphwgU7.one_liner: Maintains an evolving population of composite tool-use skills, localizing and adapting only those invalidated when API interfaces are replaced.
AHOdphwgU7.problem: Tool-learning methods assume stable tool environments, but tool names, parameters, and output fields change, and agents must keep unaffected skills while adapting broken ones.
AHOdphwgU7.method: CATE represents tool-use experience as reusable skills capturing tool order and dependencies, grows them from single-tool skills through interaction, recombination, and failure-driven refinement, and on environment change localizes affected skills and adapts them through experience inheritance. Introduces DynaToolBench for API interface replacement.
AHOdphwgU7.key_idea: Evolve a population of ordered multi-tool skills and, on interface change, adapt only affected skills by inheriting valid experience instead of relearning the tool space.
AHOdphwgU7.evidence: DynaToolBench, a controlled benchmark with a versioned adapter over a fixed MirrorAPI backend, comparing CATE with baselines across settings; the abstract is cut off before results.
AHOdphwgU7.claimed_gains: not stated in the visible abstract.
AHOdphwgU7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the cleanly controlled benchmark that separates interface change from backend instability and the inspectable, reproducible skill-evolution mechanism.
AHOdphwgU7.main_concern: The contribution of skill evolution and experience inheritance is not isolated against simple patching of names, parameters, and output fields or prior experience-bank methods, and margins over baselines are small on small task sets.

eDbpIIt8i3.one_liner: Proves complete reflection-even third-order geometric invariants determine point clouds up to five neighbors and first fail at six.
eDbpIIt8i3.problem: It is unknown when complete reflection-even third-order information in three dimensions first fails to determine a point cloud up to permutation and O(3).
eDbpIIt8i3.method: A universal theorem for single-type clouds of at most five distinct neighbors, combined with a known six-neighbor collision family, gives the sharp threshold; the proof uses value-preserving reduction, structural classification, and low-rank Gram geometry, and is checked in Lean. Paired experiments connect the floor to learning, and SNAP descriptors are tested on silicon data.
eDbpIIt8i3.key_idea: Reduce all ambiguity cases of third-order invariants to a finite set of templates eliminated by Gram-matrix geometry and exact certificates, matching the known six-point collision.
eDbpIIt8i3.evidence: A Lean-checked theorem with exact certificates, controlled paired experiments showing a representation floor, and tests on real silicon energy and force data with SNAP and a periodic DFT comparison.
eDbpIIt8i3.claimed_gains: A five-channel four-neighbor supplement improves source-held-out linear SNAP force error by 16.77% (2.97% with shared regularization) and independent-test neural force error by 3.27% across twelve paired seeds.
eDbpIIt8i3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the threshold is a sharp, exactly certified result, with learning experiments that cleanly separate a representation floor from readout capacity.
eDbpIIt8i3.main_concern: Practical relevance is undemonstrated: the benchmark samples exactly on the collision family, no near-collisions appear in real molecular environments, and the proof gives little insight.

WIQKv12R3p.one_liner: Training-free test-time adaptation fusing raw, low-rank, and semantic relation graphs over the target set to refine point-cloud logits.
WIQKv12R3p.problem: Point cloud test-time adaptation methods for vision-language models rely on a single relation view, which is unreliable under diverse corruptions.
WIQKv12R3p.method: LoReTTA builds raw, low-rank, and semantic relation views from frozen target features and zero-shot predictions, models target dependencies through self-representation, and regularizes the views with a relation-mode low-rank proximal update. The refined relations are fused into a sparse consensus graph for residual logit refinement.
WIQKv12R3p.key_idea: Exploit that corrupted target relations remain low-rank: jointly regularize three relation views with a low-rank proximal update and fuse them into a sparse consensus graph to refine logits.
WIQKv12R3p.evidence: Experiments across multiple datasets and backbones on corruption benchmarks such as ModelNet-C and ShapeNet-C, per reviews; the abstract text is cut off before results.
WIQKv12R3p.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the multi-view relational perspective (raw, low-rank, semantic) is well motivated and outperforms compared methods in most settings across datasets and backbones without updating the backbone.
WIQKv12R3p.main_concern: The comparison protocol is unmatched: LoReTTA adapts over the whole target set with dense relation matrices while baselines are single-sample or online, so gains may come from extra information access.

Fq7maQpCRp.one_liner: Chooses speculative-decoding verification length from acceptance estimates and measured latency, then prunes tokens at the first MoE router.
Fq7maQpCRp.problem: For hybrid GDN-MoE target models, verification time grows much faster with verification length than for dense models, so tokens verified after the first rejection are costly wasted work.
Fq7maQpCRp.method: HybridSpec selects the verification length on the GPU from draft-side acceptance estimates and measured target latency. It verifies that length plus one extra token up to the first MoE router, where a lightweight routing correction uses observed expert assignments to decide whether to keep that token, with block-parallel GDN kernels avoiding per-token state storage.
Fq7maQpCRp.key_idea: Run one tentative extra token up to the first MoE router and keep or drop it using observed expert assignments, with GDN kernels that avoid per-token state storage.
Fq7maQpCRp.evidence: A single-request profile of Qwen3.6-35B-A3B with DFlash against a dense Qwen3-4B target, and comparisons with SGLang and DFlash2 and with EVICT per reviews, mostly at batch size one on A100.
Fq7maQpCRp.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract text is cut off before results; its numbers describe the verification-time profile, not gains).
Fq7maQpCRp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the observation that GDN-MoE verification cost is sensitive to verification length is sharp and timely, and that faster rounds yield higher throughput than strong baselines despite slightly shorter drafts.
Fq7maQpCRp.main_concern: Evaluation is limited to single-request decoding on A100 with gains shrinking under concurrency, and the contribution of each component (length selection, acceptance estimates, implementation) is not separated.

ii8vx1IGDE.one_liner: Confidence bands define distributional ambiguity sets for Bayesian experimental design under model misspecification.
ii8vx1IGDE.problem: Misspecified likelihood models can produce overconfident posteriors and unreliable experimental designs.
ii8vx1IGDE.method: DR-BED constructs ambiguity sets from lower and upper confidence bands for the data-generating process. It derives coverage guarantees and a dual formulation optimized with stochastic subgradients, permitting confidence-level updates during sequential experimentation.
ii8vx1IGDE.key_idea: Optimize experimental designs against distributions enclosed by confidence-band ambiguity sets with experimenter-chosen coverage.
ii8vx1IGDE.evidence: Theoretical coverage holds under Hölder continuity, compact design spaces, and bounded outcome support; reviewers report experiments across multiple settings.
ii8vx1IGDE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the relevance of misspecification-aware design and the value of theoretical coverage and a tractable optimization formulation.
ii8vx1IGDE.main_concern: The surrogate objective may not represent information gain or recover expected information gain under correct specification.

UQdTSYe13E.one_liner: Regime-local reduced models evolve independently while a hierarchical expert router fuses their predictions in physical space.
UQdTSYe13E.problem: A single reduced representation and dynamics model can lose accuracy when parameters cross dynamical regimes.
UQdTSYe13E.method: RAL-MoE-ROM augments local projected Galerkin models with sparse expert corrections trained through autonomous rollouts. A parameter-only router selects specialists, and a history-conditioned gate fuses their reconstructed fields.
UQdTSYe13E.key_idea: Keep specialists in their own reduced coordinates and combine their reconstructed physical fields through a learned gate.
UQdTSYe13E.evidence: Three flow benchmarks covering steady, Hopf-onset, and periodic regimes include routing comparisons and parameter-matched architectural ablations.
UQdTSYe13E.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value physical-space fusion of independent local reduced models and the supporting ablations.
UQdTSYe13E.main_concern: Manually prescribed regime partitions and specialist pairings weaken the claim of automatic regime adaptation.

5badcBv3AZ.one_liner: Server-side planning, deterministic tool execution, and live-state verification turn service goals into reusable validated workflows.
5badcBv3AZ.problem: Tool-access schemas do not encode reliable multi-step service use, leaving general-purpose agents to plan and judge their own execution.
5badcBv3AZ.method: MCA compiles goals into ordered tool calls, replays them through a deterministic executor, and verifies outcomes by querying the live service. A task generator converts verified runs into reusable planner knowledge.
5badcBv3AZ.key_idea: Move service-specific planning and verification to the server and reuse verified execution traces as planning knowledge.
5badcBv3AZ.evidence: Evaluation covers 125 multi-step tasks on GitHub, PostgreSQL, Playwright, and Yahoo Finance with twelve backbones from five providers.
5badcBv3AZ.claimed_gains: MCA verifies 71% of tasks against 40% for matched ReAct and is significantly ahead in 34 of 48 campaigns.
5badcBv3AZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers support the service-specific architecture, explicit planning, and verification against actual system state.
5badcBv3AZ.main_concern: The comparisons do not separate gains from planning, verifier access, reusable knowledge, and other differences from the baseline.

PTO4ZmYpYT.one_liner: State-conditioned gating mixes plan, skill, and neutral teacher distributions to supervise agent reinforcement learning.
PTO4ZmYpYT.problem: A successful privileged plan may provide unsuitable guidance after a student agent deviates from its intended trajectory.
PTO4ZmYpYT.method: SCOUT scores the same student history under Gold, Skill, and Neutral teacher views, using an online buffer of successful skills. A parameter-free gate mixes these distributions using compatibility and applicability signals during training.
PTO4ZmYpYT.key_idea: Adapt the distillation target to the current student state by gating three privileged-information views.
PTO4ZmYpYT.evidence: Three backbones on ALFWorld, WebShop, and search-based QA compare Gold-only distillation with SCOUT, both alone and with GRPO.
PTO4ZmYpYT.claimed_gains: With Qwen3.5-4B and GRPO, ALFWorld success rises from 88.2% to 93.2%, WebShop success from 68.7% to 77.4%, and search-QA exact match from 45.74% to 49.93%.
PTO4ZmYpYT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the distinction between task correctness and state applicability and the training-only adaptation of supervision.
PTO4ZmYpYT.main_concern: The evidence does not directly show that the gate detects state mismatch and supplies recovery guidance beyond ordinary skill conditioning.

0P4DipCXgj.one_liner: Reconstructing orchestrated reasoning executions into standalone trajectories supplies reinforcement learning with solutions that native rollouts miss.
0P4DipCXgj.problem: Reasoning reinforcement learning stalls when native sampling rarely finds successful trajectories on difficult problems.
0P4DipCXgj.method: HAIR uses an agentic harness on problems that defeat native rollouts, then InverseHarness reconstructs successful executions into self-contained trajectories while preserving policy-generated reasoning. It refreshes these trajectories from the evolving policy and interleaves them with standard RL.
0P4DipCXgj.key_idea: Convert successful externally orchestrated executions into policy-generated standalone trajectories for iterative reinforcement learning.
0P4DipCXgj.evidence: Mathematical reasoning experiments use Intern-S2-Preview at 35B and 397B against GRPO with matched backbones, corpora, and optimizer steps.
0P4DipCXgj.claimed_gains: At 397B, pass@1 rises from 55.5 to 68.8 on IMO-Proof-Bench and from 29.2 to 38.4 on PhD-Paper.
0P4DipCXgj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find learning from externally solved hard problems worthwhile and the mathematical reasoning results supportive.
0P4DipCXgj.main_concern: Missing comparisons with simpler trajectory rewriting or distillation leave the added design and computational cost insufficiently justified.

zS1WMZtvhI.one_liner: Cross-modal dual-guided latent diffusion embeds typographic and scene-level forensic signatures into host images for RAG tracing.
zS1WMZtvhI.problem: Synthetic visual canaries with unnatural compositions or arbitrary acronyms violate natural image distributions and are filtered out by pre-ingestion anomaly sanitization in black-box multimodal RAG systems.
zS1WMZtvhI.method: SemantiTrace embeds micro-scale forensic signatures into benign host images by mutating existing typography or adding branded scene elements via Cross-modal Dual-Guided Latent Diffusion, coupling visual retrieval pull with teacher-forced textual decoding. Support-preserving output projection, Dual-Space Soft Latent Blending, and spatially gated gradients suppress off-canvas pixel drift and mask-edge artifacts.
zS1WMZtvhI.key_idea: Embed micro-scale typographic or branded scene mutations into host images via dual-guided latent diffusion coupling visual retrieval pull with teacher-forced text decoding.
zS1WMZtvhI.evidence: Evaluations cover pre-ingestion anomaly filtering on DENSE-10K and MMQA, multiple black-box retrieval and generator setups, corpus-wide repair, and AnyText2 baselines.
zS1WMZtvhI.claimed_gains: SemantiTrace passes pre-ingestion anomaly filters with a 1.8% rejection rate on DENSE-10K and MMQA.
zS1WMZtvhI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that embedding subtle, contextually coherent visual edits in benign host images is a practical approach to surviving pre-ingestion outlier filtering for RAG copyright tracing.
zS1WMZtvhI.main_concern: Reviewers highlight unacknowledged overlap with semantic and physical backdoor watermarking literature, dense presentation obscuring the default audit workflow, and narrow stealthiness metrics.

rQLwHaJmrQ.one_liner: Adding a training-free log-alpha attention-logit bias toward reference keys improves multi-person identity preservation in image editing.
rQLwHaJmrQ.problem: Frozen diffusion-transformer image editors often lose distinctive facial features or swap attributes across individuals during reference-guided multi-person editing.
rQLwHaJmrQ.method: FaceRoute applies a training-free inference intervention that adds a log-alpha bias from target-image queries to either whole-image (FaceRoute-W) or face-local (FaceRoute-F) reference VAE keys without modifying model weights.
rQLwHaJmrQ.key_idea: Add a training-free log-alpha bias from target-image queries to whole-image or face-local reference VAE keys in frozen diffusion-transformer editors.
rQLwHaJmrQ.evidence: Experiments evaluate Qwen-Image-Edit-2511 and FLUX.2-klein-base-9B on MultiID-Bench and XVerseBench using paired bootstrap intervals, multi-seed runs, multiple face encoders, and copy-paste/aesthetic metrics.
rQLwHaJmrQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the attention-logit reweighting is simple, training-free, plug-and-play on modern diffusion-transformer editors, and supported by transparent statistical reporting of identity-versus-aesthetic trade-offs.
rQLwHaJmrQ.main_concern: Reviewers find the logit-bias mechanism incremental, note small multi-person and small-face evaluation subsets, and point out weak controlled evidence for when spatial selectivity outperforms whole-image routing.

B8Fw1UP9xa.one_liner: Minimizing worst-case node-feature distortion over graph homomorphisms defines a structural pseudo-metric and GNN encoding.
B8Fw1UP9xa.problem: Combinatorial graph expressivity analyses focus on discrete structure while ignoring continuous node attributes, failing to quantify graded similarity between attributed graphs.
B8Fw1UP9xa.method: Graph Homomorphism Distortion (GHD) defines a pseudo-metric measuring the minimal worst-case distortion applied to node features under graph homomorphisms from one graph to another. The authors derive an approximation under structural assumptions and use distances to reference graphs as attributed homomorphism encodings for graph neural networks.
B8Fw1UP9xa.key_idea: Measure the minimal worst-case node-feature distortion induced by graph homomorphisms between attributed graphs and use approximations as GNN structural encodings.
B8Fw1UP9xa.evidence: Theoretical expressivity properties are paired with structural discrimination experiments on BREC and downstream molecular property prediction benchmarks.
B8Fw1UP9xa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that combining homomorphism-constrained structural mappings with continuous feature distortion offers a distinctive graded similarity measure and useful GNN structural encoding.
B8Fw1UP9xa.main_concern: Reviewers identify theoretical gaps and inaccuracies in comparing GHD with Weisfeiler-Lehman distinguishability, including a Theorem 2 counterexample on unequal-order cycles and handling infinite distortion when no homomorphism exists.

X5SIoxj5CC.one_liner: Paired dorsal CA1 calcium imaging and 2D/3D pose recordings benchmark freely moving neural encoding and decoding.
X5SIoxj5CC.problem: Neural encoding and decoding are typically benchmarked in head-fixed or trial-structured paradigms rather than continuous, naturalistic freely moving behavior.
X5SIoxj5CC.method: FreeCAB curates 58 session-level recordings pairing dorsal CA1 miniscope calcium imaging with synchronized multi-view 2D position and reconstructed 3D pose alongside explicit tracking-quality controls. A unified interface benchmarks bidirectional single-session encoding and decoding, locomotor-state dependence, multi-session pretraining, and joint training.
X5SIoxj5CC.key_idea: Pair 58 curated dorsal CA1 miniscope calcium recordings with synchronized 2D position and 3D pose under unified bidirectional encoding-decoding tasks.
X5SIoxj5CC.evidence: Five general-purpose sequence baselines (plus supplementary neural baselines) are evaluated across single-session 2D/3D encoding and decoding, speed thresholds, and multi-session transfer splits.
X5SIoxj5CC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that temporally aligned multi-session hippocampal calcium imaging paired with high-quality 2D position and 3D pose tracking under free movement is a valuable naturalistic dataset.
X5SIoxj5CC.main_concern: Reviewers note that empirical findings largely confirm known hippocampal coding properties without new machine-learning insights, while cross-session splits mostly reuse the same animals and sideline neural-domain baselines.

XYraMFsPEd.one_liner: ReMind periodically resamples mastered prompts and requeues regressed ones while preserving the per-step RLVR rollout budget.
XYraMFsPEd.problem: Aggregate RLVR improvements can hide regression on mastered prompts whose all-correct rollouts provide no reward gradient.
XYraMFsPEd.method: ReMind tracks mastered prompts, revisits them with fresh rollouts, and requeues prompts that regress. Pre-rollout batch replacement allocates reviews without increasing the per-step rollout budget.
XYraMFsPEd.key_idea: Periodic on-policy review detects regression on previously mastered prompts and returns them to training before forgetting accumulates.
XYraMFsPEd.evidence: Experiments span 20 image-text, video, and text-only reasoning benchmarks and compare GRPO, DAPO, and review-policy baselines.
XYraMFsPEd.claimed_gains: ReMind improves average accuracy by 3.81 and 3.44 percentage points over GRPO and DAPO, respectively.
XYraMFsPEd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the simple, practical review mechanism and consistent gains across domains and RLVR algorithms.
XYraMFsPEd.main_concern: Reviewers question whether the targeted review provides a distinct anti-forgetting benefit beyond simpler replay or curriculum-based sample selection.

9x8MmI8Xsn.one_liner: MOLRN-BO combines a regularized shared-spectral GP with historical calibration and alternating Pareto-local and global acquisition search.
9x8MmI8Xsn.problem: Expressive nonstationary Gaussian processes can fit observed data well yet produce inaccurate and overconfident acquisition decisions.
9x8MmI8Xsn.method: MOLRN-BO adds objective-specific residuals to a shared-spectral surrogate and applies prequential mean correction with tempered covariance scaling. It optimizes qLogEHVI locally around the Pareto region with periodic global search.
9x8MmI8Xsn.key_idea: Regularized cross-objective spectral structure, historical residual calibration, and local-global acquisition search jointly shape Bayesian optimization decisions.
9x8MmI8Xsn.evidence: Experiments compare nine algorithms on 12 deterministic bi-objective benchmarks using normalized hypervolume, inverted generational distance, tail performance, and ablations.
9x8MmI8Xsn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that diagnosing the mismatch between regression fit and acquisition reliability is useful and supported by decision-relevant measurements.
9x8MmI8Xsn.main_concern: Reviewers agree that stationary surrogates need the same calibration and search controls to isolate the nonstationary model's contribution.

KBNp692qau.one_liner: SBR reconstructs task-specific projected expert responses from weights, while SBR-R retains cross-task responses on which experts agree.
KBNp692qau.problem: Data-free weight-space merging lacks direct constraints on preserving each expert's output behavior.
KBNp692qau.method: SBR constructs layer-local response targets from task vectors and reconstructs self-responses within task-specific input and output subspaces while suppressing cross-task responses. SBR-R selectively preserves cross-task responses shared by the experts.
KBNp692qau.key_idea: Weight-derived subspace response targets distinguish expert self-responses from cross-task responses, retaining the latter when experts agree.
KBNp692qau.evidence: Experiments compare data-free merging methods on CLIP, Qwen-14B LoRA, and InternVL2.5, with predictive-distribution diagnostics and solver ablations.
KBNp692qau.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the behavior-oriented formulation, explicit self-response and cross-response distinction, and evaluations across model architectures.
KBNp692qau.main_concern: Reviewers agree that task performance is sensitive to solver depth and can deteriorate as the optimization converges more accurately.

VRcvw9QG6d.one_liner: Autoregressive occupancy generation converts BEV layouts into geometry for temporally consistent driving videos with flexible cameras.
VRcvw9QG6d.problem: Driving generators struggle to combine faithful layout control, temporal geometry consistency, and flexible viewpoints beyond recorded scenes.
VRcvw9QG6d.method: AnyScene autoregressively generates semantic occupancy sequences from BEV layouts, then conditions multi-view video synthesis on the resulting geometry. It supports reference-free generation and camera configurations chosen at inference time.
VRcvw9QG6d.key_idea: Generate occupancy sequences from BEV layouts and render their geometry as conditioning for multi-view video synthesis.
VRcvw9QG6d.evidence: Experiments use the nuScenes-based 12 Hz nuCraftv2 dataset, evaluate zero-shot occupancy generation from unseen layouts and global maps, and test video generation and camera changes.
VRcvw9QG6d.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the high-frequency occupancy dataset and the reported driving-scene generation results.
VRcvw9QG6d.main_concern: Missing comparisons against prior BEV-to-occupancy methods leave the claimed controllability insufficiently established.

O7a08TTnlE.one_liner: OOD-derived competing gradients update selected server-side kernels before federated rounds to counter persistent backdoor accumulation.
O7a08TTnlE.problem: Defenses applied after local training can leave backdoor influence that accumulates during sustained federated poisoning.
O7a08TTnlE.method: FedHarden trains the global model on OOD-derived auxiliary data before each communication round. It restricts these competing-gradient updates to selected convolutional kernels and associated batch-normalization parameters without identifying malicious clients.
O7a08TTnlE.key_idea: Inject competing gradients through selected convolutional kernels and batch-normalization parameters before each federated round.
O7a08TTnlE.evidence: Experiments cover multiple attacks, datasets, model architectures, client distributions, and poisoning strengths, including CIFAR10 with 600 poisoning rounds.
O7a08TTnlE.claimed_gains: On CIFAR10 with 600 poisoning rounds, backdoor accuracy falls to 10.00% versus 42.44% for the strongest baseline, a 4.2× reduction.
O7a08TTnlE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the persistent-poisoning problem relevant and the detection-free server intervention empirically promising across varied attacks.
O7a08TTnlE.main_concern: The paper does not establish that kernels selected using flood-data responses correspond to the low-activity parameters motivating the defense.

juv4oFeB0T.one_liner: Shared reference responses, paired statistical tests, and token caps compare fidelity among closely matched quantized vision-language models.
juv4oFeB0T.problem: Static-text metrics omit visual inputs, while full visual benchmarks cost too much to distinguish closely matched quantized models.
juv4oFeB0T.method: GAP teacher-forces quantized candidates on shared image-conditioned responses from their full-precision reference model. It compares item-level fidelity with paired tests and limits scoring to pre-validated token caps.
juv4oFeB0T.key_idea: Score candidates on identical reference-generated visual responses and pair item-level differences, truncating responses at validated token caps.
juv4oFeB0T.evidence: The abstract reports evaluation of 124 quantized checkpoints, comprising 118 4-bit and six 3-bit checkpoints, across eight VLMs and six visual benchmarks.
juv4oFeB0T.claimed_gains: Token caps retain on average over 92% of full-horizon paired signal-to-noise ratio, while thinking-mode pairing cuts sample budgets by 7.9× at 74–98% lower wall-clock cost than free-form generation.
juv4oFeB0T.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the practical value of comparing near-identical quantized candidates and the usefulness of the statistical protocol and empirical coverage.
juv4oFeB0T.main_concern: The methodological contribution largely combines established teacher-forced divergence measurements and paired statistical inference.

T244mmc39e.one_liner: Cross-world few-shot demonstrations shift graph representations and increase their use in language-model predictions.
T244mmc39e.problem: Language models can encode in-context graph structure without effectively using it for subsequent predictions.
T244mmc39e.method: The study supplies few-shot demonstrations generated from different worlds with shared or different graph topologies. Linear probes, subspace analyses, and representation interventions examine changes in graph encoding and predictive use.
T244mmc39e.key_idea: Demonstrations from other worlds relocate graph representations into nearly orthogonal directions that interventions test for predictive relevance.
T244mmc39e.evidence: Graph-tracking experiments cover 9 models from 7 families, with probing and interventions plus evaluations on ARC-AGI-1&2, web-agent tasks, and Othello.
T244mmc39e.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the distinction between constructing and using world representations and the empirical analyses across models and graph settings.
T244mmc39e.main_concern: The interventions do not establish that representation relocation itself causes the observed prediction gains.

xcaXcND0dQ.one_liner: Spectral decorrelation, water-filling bit allocation, and sensitivity equalization adapt existing vector quantizers to anisotropic embeddings.
xcaXcND0dQ.problem: Correlated, anisotropic embeddings violate the geometric assumptions of standard quantizers used for maximum inner product search.
xcaXcND0dQ.method: VENICE wraps base quantizers with spectral decorrelation, water-filling rate allocation, and sensitivity equalization to form decoupled sub-vectors. Norm restoration corrects shrinkage in quantized outputs.
xcaXcND0dQ.key_idea: Reshape embedding geometry and allocate bits by spectral sensitivity before applying a base codec, then restore vector norms.
xcaXcND0dQ.evidence: The paper provides mathematical properties and experiments across five benchmarks, six codecs, and 4-, 2-, and 1-bit regimes.
xcaXcND0dQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the reusable preprocessing framework and its empirical coverage across different codecs and bit budgets.
xcaXcND0dQ.main_concern: Reported bit rates do not clearly account for total storage, including vector norms and other side information.

ui3Bo0ZNzM.one_liner: CueDuet weights text distillation by cue-dependent teacher disagreement and separately distills expressive speech on student replies.
ui3Bo0ZNzM.problem: Spoken dialogue models struggle to adapt both response content and vocal delivery to paralinguistic cues.
ui3Bo0ZNzM.method: A text teacher evaluates student response prefixes with and without cues, using prediction divergence to weight supervision. An expressive speech teacher conditions on student replies to guide faithful content and vocal style through on-policy distillation.
ui3Bo0ZNzM.key_idea: Weight text supervision by cue-aware versus cue-agnostic teacher divergence while distilling speech delivery on the student's own responses.
ui3Bo0ZNzM.evidence: Emotion- and age-sensitive evaluations span three benchmarks and two speech-model architectures, with offline and matched on-policy baselines and weighting ablations.
ui3Bo0ZNzM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize improved paralinguistic behavior and useful evaluation across models, benchmarks, and controlled ablations.
ui3Bo0ZNzM.main_concern: General-capability retention remains insufficiently established, particularly without component-level analysis of text weighting and speech distillation effects.

5HP00vNiuV.one_liner: SigDINO adapts DINOv3 on synthetic signatures and compares stroke-responsive patch features through local structural matching.
5HP00vNiuV.problem: Offline signature verification becomes unstable with limited training writers and often generalizes poorly across languages.
5HP00vNiuV.method: Self-supervised adaptation on synthetic signature images adjusts DINOv3 to sparse strokes. Intermediate patch tokens receive deeper-layer residual information, and local structural matching computes signature-pair distances.
5HP00vNiuV.key_idea: Adapt pretrained visual tokens to signature strokes, combine intermediate and deeper-layer information, and match local structures between signature pairs.
5HP00vNiuV.evidence: Four benchmark datasets include cross-language transfer, a five-writer training setting, and backbone, adaptation, layer-selection, and matching ablations.
5HP00vNiuV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers acknowledge strong cross-language and limited-writer results supported by multi-dataset evaluation.
5HP00vNiuV.main_concern: Most improvement appears attributable to the pretrained DINOv3 backbone, with limited additional benefit from the proposed adaptation and matching components.

Vi4KeJHIJA.one_liner: PREMO alternates verified preference proposal and memo generation to learn concise personalized summaries from long user histories.
Vi4KeJHIJA.problem: The complete set of query-relevant preferences in noisy user histories is unobserved, making faithful memo generation difficult to supervise.
Vi4KeJHIJA.method: A single model alternates between proposing atomic preferences verified against history and generating query-conditioned memos. Proposer training expands verified supervision, while memo rewards encourage covering accepted preferences without asserting rejected ones.
Vi4KeJHIJA.key_idea: Alternate verified atomic-preference discovery with memo training that rewards coverage of accepted preferences and penalizes rejected assertions.
Vi4KeJHIJA.evidence: Theory studies proposer-then-memo training, and shopping, movie, and everyday-decision experiments include matched memo-only training and verification ablations.
Vi4KeJHIJA.claimed_gains: A trained 4B model produces memos of about 170 tokens for histories 40 to 100 times longer and improves downstream accuracy by up to 3.7 points.
Vi4KeJHIJA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value separating preference recognition from expression while retaining simple memo generation at deployment.
Vi4KeJHIJA.main_concern: Incomplete preference-reference pools and limited task-specific personalization comparisons constrain claims about broad personalization quality.

je6EuHVrID.one_liner: Controlled slide interventions and region-anchored QA assess whether pathology language models use slide-specific visual evidence.
je6EuHVrID.problem: Strong whole-slide QA scores do not establish that pathology models use diagnostically relevant visual information.
je6EuHVrID.method: The study analyzes inputs, representations, and predictions through visual interventions and matched slide swaps. VAPath supplies pathologist-annotated regions for comparing model-derived visual signals with independent pathology retrieval.
je6EuHVrID.key_idea: Hold questions fixed while changing slide evidence, then compare decision sensitivity and model localization against annotated pathology regions.
je6EuHVrID.evidence: Representative pathology models undergo counterfactual, matched-pair, spatial, retrieval, and instruction-tuning analyses, including VAPath's 3,605 WSI–QA–ROI samples described in reviews.
je6EuHVrID.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the distinction between answer accuracy and visual reliance, supported by complementary interventions and annotated regions.
je6EuHVrID.main_concern: External retrieval and model-derived signals operate at different representation levels, so their comparison does not locate where diagnostically useful evidence is lost.

OZXwQZJuMz.one_liner: TimEE meta-trains on synthetic time-series tasks to classify queries directly from labeled support examples without target-dataset fitting.
OZXwQZJuMz.problem: Two-stage time-series classifiers separate representation learning from classification and require per-dataset training.
OZXwQZJuMz.method: TimEE is a prior-data fitted network trained exclusively on synthetic classification tasks with structured distributional shifts. Its class-aware architecture processes labeled support series and queries together to output class probabilities.
OZXwQZJuMz.key_idea: Meta-train a support-query classifier on structured synthetic tasks so task labels influence prediction directly through in-context attention.
OZXwQZJuMz.evidence: A 4.5M-parameter model is evaluated on the 128-dataset UCR archive against supervised and foundation-model baselines for accuracy, calibration, and speed.
OZXwQZJuMz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize competitive classification results and the practical value of inference without task-specific training.
OZXwQZJuMz.main_concern: The relation between the single synthetic prior family and real-world transfer remains insufficiently characterized, leaving generalization limits unclear.

W0o3P4EJyY.one_liner: SLICE contrasts full-model logits with a prompt-adaptive layer-skipped branch to guide diffusion language-model decoding.
W0o3P4EJyY.problem: Diffusion language models do not fully exploit internal computation structure for inference-time quality improvements.
W0o3P4EJyY.method: SLICE skips selected redundant layers to create a weakened branch without training. It bounds and normalizes strong-weak logit differences to reweight token distributions while retaining the original decoding procedure.
W0o3P4EJyY.key_idea: Construct a weakened branch by adaptive layer skipping and use bounded full-versus-weak logit contrast to reweight each decoding step.
W0o3P4EJyY.evidence: Eight benchmarks evaluate two LLaDA-family models, with weak-only and random-skip controls plus KL-objective and single-step deviation analyses.
W0o3P4EJyY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize training-free structural contrast within one model and positive benchmark results.
W0o3P4EJyY.main_concern: Configuration-selection subsets overlap final evaluation sets, leaving the independence and generalization of reported gains unresolved.

LaXQcKDlyI.one_liner: AutoGUIWorld combines structured screenshot generation, action planning, and chained image edits to synthesize grounded GUI trajectories.
LaXQcKDlyI.problem: GUI-agent training coverage is constrained by the engineering required to construct and run diverse software environments.
LaXQcKDlyI.method: Structured world sampling produces initial screenshots and tasks. A planner specifies atomic actions and consequences, Image2 edits screenshots into subsequent states, and a grounding module annotates action targets.
LaXQcKDlyI.key_idea: Separate semantic action planning from visual transition generation to produce screenshot-action-screenshot training trajectories without executing the target software.
LaXQcKDlyI.evidence: Reviews describe 79,266 grounded filtered steps and downstream training evaluations on OSWorld and ScienceBoard.
LaXQcKDlyI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize environment-free trajectory generation as useful for broader training coverage and acknowledge downstream agent improvements.
LaXQcKDlyI.main_concern: Generated visual artifacts and unmeasured cumulative transition errors leave trajectory fidelity and the simulation-to-reality gap insufficiently established.

pF7mm8ukxK.one_liner: RPA aligns brain signals with all intermediate vision-transformer patch tokens through a lightweight residual adapter.
pF7mm8ukxK.problem: Global visual embeddings may discard local information useful for identifying viewed images from EEG and MEG signals.
pF7mm8ukxK.method: RPA adapts the full intermediate patch-token set of a pretrained visual transformer for brain-image representation alignment. Pooling, masking, and feature analyses examine the contributions of local visual detail and semantics.
pF7mm8ukxK.key_idea: Retain and adapt every intermediate visual patch token instead of aligning brain signals with one global image embedding.
pF7mm8ukxK.evidence: THINGS-EEG2 and THINGS-MEG evaluations cover within- and cross-subject retrieval, adapter and layer comparisons, and six quantitative feature analyses.
pF7mm8ukxK.claimed_gains: Reported Top-1 accuracies are 95.4% within-subject and 35.5% cross-subject on THINGS-EEG2, and 65.2% and 6.7%, respectively, on THINGS-MEG.
pF7mm8ukxK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the retrieval improvements substantial and the comparisons of intermediate patches with global embeddings useful.
pF7mm8ukxK.main_concern: Visual-layer and other configuration choices use test performance, making headline retrieval scores optimistically selected.

e7KTsFHCDP.one_liner: TEH selects attention heads by counterfactual effects on answer support and steers them using sample-specific temporal differences.
e7KTsFHCDP.problem: Heads sensitive to video reordering do not necessarily support correct temporal-order answers.
e7KTsFHCDP.method: TEH swaps head representations between original and temporally reordered videos, ranking heads by changes in correct-answer support. At inference, selected heads receive adjustments along each sample's original-counterfactual representation difference without parameter training.
e7KTsFHCDP.key_idea: Rank heads by answer-support changes under counterfactual activation swaps, then steer selected heads along sample-specific temporal representation differences.
e7KTsFHCDP.evidence: TempCompass, VidHalluc-TSH, and Vinoground evaluations cover five Video-MLLMs from 2B to 8B with head-selection and counterfactual ablations.
e7KTsFHCDP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find answer-relevant head localization and targeted temporal steering promising for video temporal reasoning.
e7KTsFHCDP.main_concern: The answer-support head-ranking signal is unstable across discovery subsets and relies on setting-specific selection heuristics.

GW4BSxXtrQ.one_liner: CAMEL combines typed message graphs with query-time retrieval, term linking, and contextual grounding for collaborative agent memory.
GW4BSxXtrQ.problem: Collaborative answers require evidence scattered across speakers and time, with changing decisions and inconsistent terminology.
GW4BSxXtrQ.method: CAMEL retains attributed messages in an offline graph of reply, decision, and term relations without generative ingestion calls. Query decomposition, hybrid retrieval, graph expansion, bidirectional term alignment, and contextual grounding assemble an ordered evidence window.
GW4BSxXtrQ.key_idea: Retain raw attributed messages and assemble query-specific evidence through typed graph expansion, term alignment, and speaker-time grounding.
GW4BSxXtrQ.evidence: EverMemBench, GroupMemBench, and SocialMemBench experiments compare ten baselines across answer models and evidence budgets, with component ablations and judge checks.
GW4BSxXtrQ.claimed_gains: CAMEL improves answer accuracy over the strongest of ten baselines by 12.5, 11.4, and 11.7 percentage points on EverMemBench, GroupMemBench, and SocialMemBench, respectively.
GW4BSxXtrQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that speaker attribution, changing decisions, and distributed evidence make collaborative memory a useful problem.
GW4BSxXtrQ.main_concern: Underdocumented baseline access to metadata and processing makes it unclear whether gains come from evidence selection under equivalent information budgets.

rLVmGSzgNZ.one_liner: Task-, group-, and token-level PPO critic analyses motivate decoupling samples used to train critics and policies.
rLVmGSzgNZ.problem: PPO critic learning dynamics and their effects on credit assignment remain poorly understood in language-model reinforcement learning.
rLVmGSzgNZ.method: The study analyzes trajectory advantages and belief rankings across task, group, and token scales. Its CPSD method filters samples for policy optimization while retaining broader samples for critic training.
rLVmGSzgNZ.key_idea: Decouple critic and policy training samples so policy filtering does not remove the critic's broader learning coverage.
rLVmGSzgNZ.evidence: Reasoning and coding experiments analyze normalization-like advantage patterns, soft silencing, length preferences, and CPSD improvements across two models.
rLVmGSzgNZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the usefulness of examining critic behavior and identifying length-related failure patterns beyond aggregate PPO performance.
rLVmGSzgNZ.main_concern: Observed advantage-length associations do not establish that policy updates favor longer responses, leaving the proposed length-bias mechanism insufficiently supported.

ZdpvRDduo4.one_liner: Predicts multi-step LEGO assembly feasibility by rolling forward anchor tokens in a multi-granularity graph latent world model.
ZdpvRDduo4.problem: Look-ahead search in LEGO assembly sequence planning requires evaluating whether candidate brick placements leave the remaining structure physically buildable without querying an expensive physics simulator at every search step.
ZdpvRDduo4.method: The authors represent a partial LEGO assembly as a multi-granularity heterogeneous graph containing brick-level interlocking topology and a master node of geometric anchor tokens. A learned latent dynamics model locally updates anchor tokens after each candidate placement, allowing multi-step look-ahead feasibility prediction while verifying committed actions with an exact solver.
ZdpvRDduo4.key_idea: Advances local geometric anchor tokens on a multi-granularity assembly graph via a learned latent dynamics model to score multi-step buildability during look-ahead search.
ZdpvRDduo4.evidence: Evaluated on held-out test structures from the StableText2Lego benchmark against assembly-sequence baselines and look-ahead depth ablations.
ZdpvRDduo4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the multi-granularity graph representation and combining learned latent look-ahead with exact verification at committed steps is a sensible and safe planning design.
ZdpvRDduo4.main_concern: The evaluation excludes timeouts from the headline success rate, omits optimized exact-search or constraint-solver baselines, and does not compare against re-encoding known next states without learned dynamics.

8Tt8BrhS3b.one_liner: Proves that retaining a constant-size local menu of edges per arriving vertex preserves near-optimal global stochastic bipartite matching.
8Tt8BrhS3b.problem: Prior guarantees for two-stage local sparsification in stochastic bipartite matching required restrictive assumptions on how matching mass is spread across edges.
8Tt8BrhS3b.method: Under independent vertex arrivals where each request retains at most k incident edges before global maximum matching, the authors prove that a menu size depending only on epsilon preserves a (1 - epsilon) fraction of the expected maximum matching without spread assumptions. Menus are generated from any benchmark matching rule via marginal-weighted sampling or sampled realization simulations, analyzed via a locally computable large-marginal surrogate and fractional completion.
8Tt8BrhS3b.key_idea: Samples a constant number of edges per vertex from a benchmark matching rule's marginals and certifies global matching size via a local computation surrogate.
8Tt8BrhS3b.evidence: Supported by theoretical proofs using local computation algorithms (Theorem 3.1) and empirical matching simulations.
8Tt8BrhS3b.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that removing the spread condition to prove a universal constant menu size for heterogeneous independent vertex arrivals is a strong theoretical result.
8Tt8BrhS3b.main_concern: The proof is difficult to follow due to heavy notation, and the theoretical bound on menu size has a double-exponential dependence on 1/epsilon that is far from the O(1/epsilon) lower bound.

xHUvgp5vaZ.one_liner: Conditions remote sensing layout-to-image diffusion on an object-background relation graph populated via geometry-aware feature bank retrieval.
xHUvgp5vaZ.problem: Layout-to-image diffusion models for remote sensing encode bounding boxes independently and leave background terrain unconstrained, producing implausible object-background pairings and spatial arrangements.
xHUvgp5vaZ.method: LayGraph represents oriented bounding box layouts as a graph linking object nodes to spatial neighbors and a background super-node to condition the diffusion denoiser. A geometry features bank stores training-crop instance descriptors on graph nodes during training and fills those slots via geometry-aware cluster retrieval during layout-only inference.
xHUvgp5vaZ.key_idea: Conditions diffusion denoising on an object-and-background spatial relation graph whose node slots are populated at inference via geometry-aware cluster retrieval from a training feature bank.
xHUvgp5vaZ.evidence: Evaluated on DIOR-R and DOTA remote sensing datasets for image generation quality, layout consistency, and downstream synthetic-data detector training.
xHUvgp5vaZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that modeling object-object and object-background relations improves layout-conditioned remote sensing generation and downstream object detection performance on DIOR-R and DOTA.
xHUvgp5vaZ.main_concern: The method is only evaluated on a U-Net (Stable Diffusion 1.5) rather than modern DiT architectures, lacks a non-graph pairwise transformer baseline, and omits recent remote sensing layout generators.

f5OddDAmU4.one_liner: Trains a diverse cohort of decoupled LLMs and VLMs via reinforcement learning using peer majority-vote pseudo-labels as rewards.
f5OddDAmU4.problem: Reinforcement learning for reasoning relies on costly ground-truth verifiable rewards, while single-model self-rewarding RL reinforces internal biases and suffers from response homogenization and collapse.
f5OddDAmU4.method: Co-RL simultaneously optimizes multiple decoupled models (sharing no parameters) with reinforcement learning using rewards derived from peer models' predictions. Cohort diversity is increased by combining heterogeneous model families, parameter scales, and rephrased prompts to decorrelate errors.
f5OddDAmU4.key_idea: Optimizes a heterogeneous cohort of parameter-decoupled models simultaneously via GRPO where each model receives reward supervision from its peers' completions.
f5OddDAmU4.evidence: Evaluated across seven text-only reasoning benchmarks and four multimodal reasoning benchmarks across multiple model families and sizes.
f5OddDAmU4.claimed_gains: Without ground-truth labels, improves base models by 3.0-7.2% on average across seven text benchmarks and by 1.6-4.4% across four multimodal benchmarks.
f5OddDAmU4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that cross-agent peer supervision across heterogeneous model families is a simple and effective way to reduce self-reinforcing collapse in label-free RL.
f5OddDAmU4.main_concern: The method lacks a mechanism to filter unreliable peer pseudo-labels when peers share correlated errors, and experiments do not isolate simultaneous mutual co-training from static distillation from a frozen peer.

QPYkMnE5mx.one_liner: Crafts poisoned corpus documents with circular information gaps to trap agentic RAG systems in resource-exhausting retrieval loops.
QPYkMnE5mx.problem: Iterative retrieval in Agentic RAG exposes an unexplored Denial-of-Efficiency attack surface where poisoned corpus documents can induce unbounded retrieval and reasoning loops.
QPYkMnE5mx.method: CyclicRA is a two-stage corpus-poisoning attack that constructs sequences of intermediate queries forming a directed cycle and generates corresponding poisoned documents. Each document supplies partial evidence while introducing unresolved information gaps that steer the agent to issue the next query in the loop.
QPYkMnE5mx.key_idea: Injects poisoned corpus documents engineered with cyclic unresolved information dependencies that steer an agentic RAG system back to previously issued queries.
QPYkMnE5mx.evidence: Evaluated across five LLM backbones on single-hop and multi-hop question-answering benchmarks.
QPYkMnE5mx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that studying resource-exhaustion attacks via retrieval loops in agentic RAG is a realistic and consequential security problem.
QPYkMnE5mx.main_concern: The no-loop ablation removes cross-document coordination entirely rather than testing an open chain, the fraction of runs completing a full cycle is not isolated, and system-level defenses or attack generation overhead are underexplored.

QkVGq74LtQ.one_liner: Preserves reasoning-answer consistency in VLM RLVR by scaling token-level KL regularization by actor-reference entropy gaps and token position.
QkVGq74LtQ.problem: Relaxing reference-policy KL regularization during VLM reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) degrades reasoning-answer consistency and reduces reliance on generated reasoning.
QkVGq74LtQ.method: Position- and Entropy-Aware KL Anchoring (PEAK) applies token-adaptive KL regularization toward the pre-RLVR reference policy. Guided by the observation that inconsistent responses exhibit larger actor-reference entropy gaps and elevated late-position entropy, PEAK assigns stronger KL penalties to tokens with large positive entropy gaps and adapts strength by response position.
QkVGq74LtQ.key_idea: Modulates token-level KL divergence penalties during VLM RLVR according to each token's actor-reference entropy gap and sequence position.
QkVGq74LtQ.evidence: Evaluated across seven multimodal reasoning benchmarks, multiple VLM sizes, and RLVR backbones (including DAPO).
QkVGq74LtQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the empirical diagnosis showing that equal final-answer accuracy can hide large drops in reasoning-answer consistency and Pass@k, as well as the simplicity of the token-adaptive KL objective.
QkVGq74LtQ.main_concern: Causal intervention experiments on reasoning reliance suffer from confounding differences between clean and unrelated donor traces, accuracy gains over uniform KL are small (0.50-1.26 pp) without multi-seed confidence intervals, and entropy-based token selection lacks shuffled-token controls.

maQnnAp3hR.one_liner: Continually trains genomic foundation models by combining token-level generative losses with a latent sequence-level JEPA objective.
maQnnAp3hR.problem: Genomic foundation models pretrained only with masked language modeling or next-token prediction focus on local token reconstruction at the expense of sequence-level functional representations.
maQnnAp3hR.method: JEPA-DNA is a model-agnostic continual pretraining framework that augments standard generative objectives (MLM or NTP) with a Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) loss and VICReg regularization. It trains a predictor to map the global latent representation of a corrupted DNA sequence to the EMA-encoded global representation of the unmasked sequence.
maQnnAp3hR.key_idea: Jointly optimizes token-level generative reconstruction and a latent JEPA objective that predicts the unmasked DNA sequence's global embedding from a corrupted view.
maQnnAp3hR.evidence: Evaluated across three genomic foundation model backbones (including NTv3 and DNABERT-2) on 17 genomic benchmark tasks under linear-probing and zero-shot protocols.
maQnnAp3hR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the continual training recipe transfers cleanly across three distinct genomic model architectures and is supported by step- and compute-matched ablations.
maQnnAp3hR.main_concern: The linear probe evaluates a single pooled global vector directly shaped by the VICReg/JEPA head under a fixed 3-epoch probing schedule, which may reward readout geometry rather than genuine biological functional grounding.

ixhwQhUA8C.one_liner: Benchmarks active visual search in MLLMs on information-dense scenes and verifies tool reliance via a crop-blackout intervention.
ixhwQhUA8C.problem: High MLLM scores on fine-grained perception benchmarks are inflated by language priors, coarse global visual cues, and unfaithful visual tool use.
ixhwQhUA8C.method: VisualNeedle curates a 300-question benchmark of information-dense scenes where evidence is confined to tiny regions and filters out items solvable via text priors or global glances. It introduces a counterfactual crop-black evaluation setting that replaces tool-returned image crops with black images to causally test whether models rely on intermediate visual evidence.
ixhwQhUA8C.key_idea: Evaluates MLLM active visual search on shortcut-filtered high-resolution scenes while replacing tool-returned crops with black images to measure causal reliance on visual tools.
ixhwQhUA8C.evidence: Evaluated across 9 frontier MLLMs under text-only, no-tool, standard tool-enabled, and crop-black settings.
ixhwQhUA8C.claimed_gains: Text-only accuracy stays below 10% across evaluated MLLMs.
ixhwQhUA8C.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the counterfactual crop-blackout intervention is a simple and effective way to expose whether tool-using MLLMs genuinely use returned visual crops.
ixhwQhUA8C.main_concern: The benchmark is relatively small (300 questions, with 76 missed by all human annotators), image provenance is undisclosed, and using Gemini 3.1 Pro as the automatic judge inflates scores by 3 to 4.7 percentage points according to the human audit.

sVmsN21Ltd.one_liner: Routes action-relevant features across tokens and layers of a frozen VLA into a compact state vector for online RL adaptation.
sVmsN21Ltd.problem: Adapting frozen Vision-Language-Action models with online RL suffers from poor sample efficiency when actor-critic state representations rely on external encoders or fixed VLA feature compression.
sVmsN21Ltd.method: eRLT extracts a fixed-dimensional RL state token from a frozen VLA using learned routing tokens that aggregate visual-language features within multiple layers and a lightweight layer router that combines them across depths. The routing module is initialized offline to predict expert demonstration actions and refined online using critic feedback.
sVmsN21Ltd.key_idea: Aggregates multi-layer, multi-token features from a frozen VLA via learned spatial routing tokens and a depth router initialized with behavior cloning and updated by the RL critic.
sVmsN21Ltd.evidence: Evaluated across seven simulated manipulation tasks in LIBERO and RoboTwin as well as real-world robotic insertion experiments.
sVmsN21Ltd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that investigating which internal frozen-VLA features best serve online actor-critic RL is well-motivated and supported by controlled layer/token comparisons.
sVmsN21Ltd.main_concern: Ablations show that offline action-predictive initialization drives almost all the performance gain while online critic refinement and layer routing add very small improvements (~0.015-0.021 AUC), and uncertainty estimates across training seeds are missing.

nTufDko9kF.one_liner: Derives MMSE bounds for fine-tuning adaptation versus pre-training retention and proves anytime retention for an input-gated linear predictor.
nTufDko9kF.problem: Linear fine-tuning updates, including full fine-tuning and LoRA, face an inherent trade-off between adapting to downstream tasks and retaining pre-trained capabilities.
nTufDko9kF.method: Using a linear prediction framework, the authors characterize the minimum mean-square error (MMSE) predictor when pre-training and fine-tuning populations overlap, deriving matching upper and lower loss bounds governed by correction-weighted population overlap. When only fine-tuning data are available and the target correction is fixed, they analyze an input-dependent gated predictor under Gaussian gradient flow to guarantee small fine-tuning loss and bounded forgetting throughout training.
nTufDko9kF.key_idea: Bounds unavoidable adaptation-retention error via correction-weighted distribution overlap and proves gradient-flow retention guarantees for learning an input-dependent correction gate.
nTufDko9kF.evidence: Supported by theoretical MMSE bounds, Gaussian gradient-flow trajectory theorems, and synthetic/MNIST regression experiments with fixed corrections.
nTufDko9kF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the clear exposition, the tight correction-weighted population overlap bounds on MMSE, and the gradient-flow trajectory analysis providing anytime retention guarantees.
nTufDko9kF.main_concern: The main learning guarantee assumes the true correction matrix is already known and fixed (analyzing only gate learning) under restrictive zero-mean Gaussian separation conditions.

7kTk5p5dK7.one_liner: Rewards multimodal RL reasoning traces using the policy's own answer-confidence gain with and without image access.
7kTk5p5dK7.problem: Final-answer verifiable rewards in multimodal reinforcement learning fail to penalize flawed reasoning trajectories or visual hallucinations that happen to reach the correct answer.
7kTk5p5dK7.method: Centered-Adaptive Residual Visual Transport (CA-RVT) reuses the policy model to probe reference-answer confidence with and without the generated reasoning trace across both multimodal (with image) and text-only (without image) views. It combines multimodal reasoning utility with a batch-calibrated cross-view visual dependency residual inside GRPO without external reward models.
7kTk5p5dK7.key_idea: Augments GRPO answer rewards by probing how a generated reasoning trace shifts the policy's own ground-truth answer likelihood with and without the visual input.
7kTk5p5dK7.evidence: Evaluated by post-training Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct on 2.1K Geometry3K problems and testing across four mathematical reasoning and seven general multimodal benchmarks.
7kTk5p5dK7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that CA-RVT provides a lightweight, consistent improvement over matched GRPO across math and general multimodal benchmarks without needing process labels or external reward models.
7kTk5p5dK7.main_concern: Ablations reveal that standard multimodal confidence gain accounts for nearly the entire improvement (+2.0 of +2.7 points), while the novel cross-view visual residual and calibration add negligible gains within seed noise.

Nldmlt41Y1.one_liner: Combines line plots and normalized delay-embedding images as complementary visual views in a VLM for time-series reasoning.
Nldmlt41Y1.problem: Exposing a Time Series Language Model to a single representation imposes a fixed inductive bias that struggles to simultaneously preserve absolute numerical values and scale-invariant dynamical structure.
Nldmlt41Y1.method: The authors encode each time series into two complementary visual representations: a line plot that preserves absolute coordinates and measurements, and a normalized delay embedding that factors out amplitude scale and offset to highlight temporal dynamics. Dedicated visual encoders extract tokens from both views and fuse them at multiple levels into a shared Qwen3-VL-8B backbone.
Nldmlt41Y1.key_idea: Fuses visual tokens from coordinate-preserving line plots and scale-invariant normalized delay embeddings inside a vision-language model for time-series reasoning.
Nldmlt41Y1.evidence: Evaluated on Qwen3-VL-8B across TSRBench, TSExam, and transformation invariance intervention tests.
Nldmlt41Y1.claimed_gains: Improves overall TSRBench accuracy from 45.2% with line plots alone to 54.0% (exceeding the strongest dedicated TSLM baseline at 36.7%) and achieves 89.9% accuracy on TSExam.
Nldmlt41Y1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that pairing coordinate-preserving line plots with scale-invariant delay embeddings is well-motivated and clearly validated by single-view and transformation-invariance ablations.
Nldmlt41Y1.main_concern: A reviewer demonstrates that on the TSRBench event prediction subset driving much of the headline gain, a trivial majority-class baseline ('no rain') matches the model's 84.2% accuracy, and scaling to multivariate or long series is unclear.

4UxGPqy5Kc.one_liner: Calibrates VLM text anchors with a whitened visual prototype head estimated under an inferred class prior for label-free image annotation.
4UxGPqy5Kc.problem: Zero-shot VLM image annotation degrades when candidate vocabularies reach thousands of classes and target pools exhibit unknown class imbalance, while confidence-filtered pseudo-labeling introduces selection bias.
4UxGPqy5Kc.method: Robust prototyping performs closed-form transductive adaptation on an unlabeled target image pool by assigning pseudo-labels under an estimated class prior without confidence filtering. It constructs a whitened visual classifier head using shared second-order covariance statistics over all assigned images and fuses it with the VLM text semantic anchor.
4UxGPqy5Kc.key_idea: Fuses VLM text embeddings with a shared-covariance whitened visual classifier built from unfiltered prior-matched pseudo-label assignments across the unlabeled target pool.
4UxGPqy5Kc.evidence: Evaluated across 18 VLM encoder-dataset pairs (including CLIP and SigLIP2 on ImageNet subsets, TinyImageNet, and SUN397) under balanced, long-tailed, and missing-class settings.
4UxGPqy5Kc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the careful empirical diagnosis of selection bias in confidence filtering and the fast, closed-form pipeline that consistently improves over zero-shot VLMs.
4UxGPqy5Kc.main_concern: The method closely combines existing transductive optimal-transport assignment, Gaussian discriminant analysis whitening, and prototype fusion techniques, yielding small (<1 point) average gains over strong transductive baselines like InMaP.
