gfACAuOdxZ.one_liner: Compresses multimodal chain-of-thought into structured symbolic traces disentangling visual observations from deductions via SFT and trace-grounded GRPO.
gfACAuOdxZ.problem: Verbose, free-form natural language chain-of-thought in multimodal LLMs incurs high token overhead, dilutes key information, and weakens visual grounding.
gfACAuOdxZ.method: Dense Reasoning Trace (DRT) represents reasoning as compact intermediate states linked by symbolic connectors that separate visual observations from logical deductions. The model is trained via Dense Trace Initialization (SFT on rewritten traces) followed by Trace-Grounded Reinforcement Learning using GRPO with tri-perspective verified reference traces and structured process/hallucination rewards.
gfACAuOdxZ.key_idea: Replaces verbose multimodal CoT with structured symbolic traces separating visual observations from logical steps, trained via SFT and multi-reward GRPO.
gfACAuOdxZ.evidence: Evaluated across multimodal reasoning and hallucination benchmarks against standard CoT and efficient-reasoning baselines.
gfACAuOdxZ.claimed_gains: Achieves a 5.5x token efficiency improvement while improving accuracy by 1.3 points over the baseline.
gfACAuOdxZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the inspectable, structured compression format delivers a practical 5.5x token reduction with competitive accuracy.
gfACAuOdxZ.main_concern: The pipeline relies heavily on distillation and judging from massive external models (GPT-5.1 and Qwen3-235B), trails full Qwen-Thinking accuracy (67.2 vs. 72.2), and shows limited gains on dedicated visual grounding benchmarks like HallusionBench.

4TbOJySYGS.one_liner: StructSeek trains a graph agent to invoke structural and semantic operators and use their outputs for zero-shot predictions.
4TbOJySYGS.problem: Graph language models struggle to recover pairwise structural relations needed for link prediction from serialized or implicitly encoded graph context.
4TbOJySYGS.method: StructSeek exposes task-relevant graph structure through dedicated operators that an agent learns to select and invoke. Teacher-trajectory supervised fine-tuning is followed by reinforcement learning to train evidence acquisition and prediction.
4TbOJySYGS.key_idea: Let graph operators compute structural quantities while the language-model agent learns which evidence to request and use.
4TbOJySYGS.evidence: Experiments evaluate node classification and link prediction across unseen graph domains, with controlled comparisons adding structural operators and training.
4TbOJySYGS.claimed_gains: StructSeek-3B outperforms the strongest baseline by 12.9–25.8 percentage points across four unseen graphs on link prediction.
4TbOJySYGS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the motivation clear and the separation between structural computation and language-model evidence selection reasonable.
4TbOJySYGS.main_concern: The link-prediction evaluation lacks classical structural heuristic baselines and clearly specified negative sampling, leaving the source of large gains uncertain.

xnyk4ThUib.one_liner: RELY learns probabilistic urban relations and routes their reliability separately into crime-count intensity and excess-zero predictions.
xnyk4ThUib.problem: Sparse crime histories make urban dependencies uncertain, but deterministic graphs commit to potentially unreliable structural estimates.
xnyk4ThUib.method: RELY initializes probabilistic pairwise links and group memberships from geographic, functional, and historical information and refines them per observation window through differentiable sampling. Relation reliability controls separate routing into the intensity and excess-zero components of a zero-inflated negative binomial decoder.
xnyk4ThUib.key_idea: Refine probabilistic relation structures and use channel reliability to route evidence separately for count intensity and excess-zero probability.
xnyk4ThUib.evidence: Chicago and New York experiments compare forecasting accuracy and examine relations between estimated reliability and prediction errors.
xnyk4ThUib.claimed_gains: RELY reduces MAE by 6.9% on Chicago and 4.5% on New York over the strongest evaluated baselines.
xnyk4ThUib.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value modeling sparse counts with separate relation mixtures for intensity and excess zeros.
xnyk4ThUib.main_concern: Randomly splitting overlapping forecast windows permits later training observations and does not establish generalization to future periods.

MRdrxZsxyG.one_liner: IBIS jointly crafts detectable privacy canaries with influence-based initialization, embedding orthogonality, and incremental bilevel updates.
MRdrxZsxyG.problem: Canaries inserted together can interfere with each other's membership signals and weaken one-run privacy audits.
MRdrxZsxyG.method: IBIS greedily initializes canaries using influence estimates and refines them with a bilevel objective balancing detectability and an embedding-orthogonality regularizer. Incremental updates reuse one model rather than retraining from scratch after each canary change.
MRdrxZsxyG.key_idea: Regularize jointly optimized canaries toward orthogonal embeddings while updating a shared model incrementally during bilevel refinement.
MRdrxZsxyG.evidence: Membership-inference and privacy-auditing experiments compare attack accuracy and crafting cost, including MNIST evaluations and checks with clipping and data augmentation.
MRdrxZsxyG.claimed_gains: IBIS reduces computational cost by up to two orders of magnitude while improving membership-inference metrics.
MRdrxZsxyG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value reducing interference among canaries and report substantial computational savings with similar or better attack accuracy.
MRdrxZsxyG.main_concern: Ordinary embedding orthogonality lacks sufficient justification as a proxy for cross-canary interference in deep models.

Ff4orOoZlT.one_liner: DTS applies task-conditioned binary masks to learned features so nonlinear task heads use sparse latent-factor subsets.
Ff4orOoZlT.problem: Task-sparsity methods for disentanglement have been limited to linear heads because discrete feature selection resists gradient optimization.
Ff4orOoZlT.method: DTS formulates task sparsity through task-conditioned binary masking rather than constraining the nonlinear predictor itself. Nonlinear heads learn from masked features, and sparse downstream tasks test reuse of the learned representation.
Ff4orOoZlT.key_idea: Impose task sparsity through binary feature masks while allowing nonlinear task heads to operate on selected factors.
Ff4orOoZlT.evidence: Experiments on a CLEVR-style multi-task dataset evaluate latent-factor recovery, sparse downstream learning, and out-of-distribution generalization.
Ff4orOoZlT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate a simple masking formulation that extends task-sparsity disentanglement beyond linear predictors.
Ff4orOoZlT.main_concern: Highly controlled synthetic tasks with predefined sparse factors leave applicability to less structured real-world tasks uncertain.

OOww1dIwyk.one_liner: Sequential occupancy planning splits zero-sum partially observable game backups into player-specific stages while preserving simultaneous-action game values.
OOww1dIwyk.problem: Linear-programming backups for finite-horizon zero-sum partially observable games remain computationally demanding.
OOww1dIwyk.method: The approach factorizes joint decision-rule optimization into two central-planning substages while preserving each player's information constraints and simultaneous actions. It derives sequential occupancy-state recursions and integrates the backups into point-based value iteration with exploitability bounds.
OOww1dIwyk.key_idea: Factor each joint decision-rule backup into ordered player-specific planning substages without changing the underlying simultaneous-action game.
OOww1dIwyk.evidence: Proofs establish occupancy-state sufficiency, value preservation, structural properties, and exploitability bounds, with medium-to-large benchmark comparisons against competing solvers.
OOww1dIwyk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value extending sequential occupancy planning to zero-sum games and the supporting theory and benchmark results.
OOww1dIwyk.main_concern: Exploitability guarantees cover the unpruned algorithm, while the evaluated implementation uses pruning without sufficient analysis or ablation.

7AhtZ7fPHm.one_liner: IERE aligns subject states with updated intermediate-entity representations through dependency-ordered edits to propagate single-hop knowledge changes.
7AhtZ7fPHm.problem: Successful single-hop knowledge edits often fail to change related multi-hop predictions.
7AhtZ7fPHm.method: IERE converts desired-object hidden-state interventions into persistent parameter updates. It orders interacting edits downstream to upstream, refreshes desired-object representations recursively, aligns subject states, and then applies batched factual editing using only single-hop requests.
7AhtZ7fPHm.key_idea: Refresh desired-object representations in dependency order and align subject states to them before batched factual editing.
7AhtZ7fPHm.evidence: Hidden-state intervention studies and editing experiments on Llama-3-8B-Instruct and GPT-J-6B evaluate direct editing and forward multi-hop propagation.
7AhtZ7fPHm.claimed_gains: IERE achieves the highest forward multi-hop accuracy among single-hop-only methods in all six settings.
7AhtZ7fPHm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value multi-hop gains from single-hop edit requests without edit-specific multi-hop questions, paths, or target answers.
7AhtZ7fPHm.main_concern: The final edited models do not directly verify the intended representation shift or its causal role in the observed multi-hop gains.

7WJBskIhxM.one_liner: EvoTrias separates search governance, candidate construction, and private evaluation through typed contracts and enforced runtime boundaries.
7WJBskIhxM.problem: Misallocated autonomy in LLM-driven program evolution can constrain proposals, increase cost, and compromise evaluator independence.
7WJBskIhxM.method: EvoTrias assigns cross-round search control to Structured Governance, task-local construction to Open Proposal, and validity and fitness decisions to Protected Judgment. Typed contracts and runtime hooks maintain these boundaries, including a private evaluator.
7WJBskIhxM.key_idea: Give governance, proposal, and judgment distinct owners that communicate only through typed contracts enforced by runtime hooks.
7WJBskIhxM.evidence: Experiments span mathematical, systems, and algorithm-design benchmarks with multiple LLM backbones, baseline comparisons, repeated runs, and ablations.
7WJBskIhxM.claimed_gains: Separating Governance from Proposal cuts token cost by 64%.
7WJBskIhxM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the evaluation across multiple benchmarks and models and the reported performance of the program-evolution framework.
7WJBskIhxM.main_concern: The research contribution beyond combining existing role separation and evaluator-protection mechanisms remains unclear.

cGBo0GVond.one_liner: Interlock compiles typed completion graphs into workspaces, requests, and verification rubrics for training long-horizon agents.
cGBo0GVond.problem: Agents can satisfy individual requirements while missing dependencies and required downstream effects across task artifacts.
cGBo0GVond.method: Interlock represents evidence-to-decision grounding, joint component constraints, and decision-to-effect realization in a typed completion graph. It compiles tasks and rubrics from the graph, reviews source coverage and public support, and retains agent-verified successful trajectories for fine-tuning.
cGBo0GVond.key_idea: Encode evidence, coupled requirements, and downstream effects in one typed graph that constrains both task generation and completion verification.
cGBo0GVond.evidence: Two Qwen3.6 backbones train on their own accepted trajectories and undergo external-benchmark evaluations, including AutomationBench and verification-strategy comparisons.
cGBo0GVond.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value addressing overall task completion and report training benefits across multiple backbones and external environments.
cGBo0GVond.main_concern: Unmatched data and trajectory-selection baselines do not isolate the benefit of typed completion graphs from filtering successful self-generated rollouts.

KjRXEELcFH.one_liner: Complexity-Balanced Splitting partitions diffusion time by estimated approximation burden and assigns specialized networks to the resulting segments.
KjRXEELcFH.problem: Uniformly deploying a large generative network across noise and data regimes wastes capacity on unequal computational demands.
KjRXEELcFH.method: CBS estimates temporal complexity with a lightweight auxiliary model using flow Dirichlet energy or sampling-trajectory acceleration. It partitions the timeline into equal-burden segments and trains specialized subnetworks for those regions.
KjRXEELcFH.key_idea: Choose temporal boundaries by equalizing cumulative complexity estimated from flow Dirichlet energy or trajectory acceleration.
KjRXEELcFH.evidence: Experiments span SiT, JiT, and UNet architectures, multiple datasets, latent and pixel-space models, and auxiliary-model and splitting ablations.
KjRXEELcFH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers describe the boundary-selection rule as simple and inexpensive, with stable splits and consistent experimental support.
KjRXEELcFH.main_concern: Comparisons omit stronger splitting heuristics and matched total-training-compute controls, leaving the specific advantage of complexity-based splitting uncertain.

obiT5Ft7c2.one_liner: A payoff-basis reduction enables aggregate-feedback online learning in security games with varying attacker populations and intensities.
obiT5Ft7c2.problem: Fixed-intensity security-game models do not capture changing attacker capabilities or learning from aggregate attack feedback.
obiT5Ft7c2.method: The framework models varying follower counts, types, and intensities and constructs an exact mixed-integer optimization oracle for full-information learning. Under bandit feedback, basis strategies and a barycentric spanner support unbiased candidate-payoff estimates for EXP2.
obiT5Ft7c2.key_idea: Represent candidate-defense payoffs through basis strategies so one aggregate payoff observation supports unbiased estimates for all candidates.
obiT5Ft7c2.evidence: Regret proofs cover full-information and aggregate-feedback settings with adversarial sequences, a matching lower bound, and numerical simulations of the oracle and learning algorithms.
obiT5Ft7c2.claimed_gains: Both feedback regimes achieve expected O(√T) regret without additional logarithmic factors in T, matching an Ω(√T) lower bound.
obiT5Ft7c2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value modeling variable attack intensity and the game-specific reduction for aggregate-feedback learning.
obiT5Ft7c2.main_concern: The bandit method enumerates a potentially enormous strategy set and updates every candidate, making realistic computational scalability unclear.

SEHpvea2rc.one_liner: AnchorSLU aligns target-speech representations with sentence-matched multilingual speech anchors during supervised adaptation.
SEHpvea2rc.problem: Class-level supervision leaves exact cross-lingual sentence correspondence unused in low-resource spoken-language understanding.
SEHpvea2rc.method: AnchorSLU synthesizes sentence-matched speech in eight high-resource languages and encodes it offline with a frozen backbone to build multilayer semantic anchors. Adaptation combines target-only cross-entropy with anchor alignment, and inference uses only the adapted target model.
SEHpvea2rc.key_idea: Aggregate frozen representations of sentence-matched multilingual speech and align natural target-speech states to these anchors across layers.
SEHpvea2rc.evidence: Experiments cover 20 low-resource SIB-Fleurs languages and 60-intent Speech-MASSIVE, with Qwen2.5-Omni and a larger backbone plus correspondence and alignment controls.
SEHpvea2rc.claimed_gains: AnchorSLU improves SIB-Fleurs Accuracy by 4.39 points and Macro-F1 by 5.04 points, and Speech-MASSIVE Accuracy by 3.19 points and Macro-F1 by 3.52 points.
SEHpvea2rc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate representation-level supervision and experiments examining cross-lingual alignment across low-resource speech tasks.
SEHpvea2rc.main_concern: Missing comparisons that use the same parallel-data resources or stronger alignment and cascaded baselines leave the anchor-specific benefit uncertain.

4KyXuzmElZ.one_liner: BanduraBench scores theory-specific mechanism components separately from final educational decisions to expose gaps hidden by answer accuracy.
4KyXuzmElZ.problem: Correct educational decisions can mask incorrect evidence selection or recovery of the mechanisms supporting those decisions.
4KyXuzmElZ.method: BanduraBench builds tasks from an expert-reviewed ontology, human-verified seeds, and human-adjudicated acceptable pathways. Structured scoring separately measures source, self-efficacy, course-design interpretation, and causal-claim strength, accounting for conjunctive errors.
4KyXuzmElZ.key_idea: Evaluate explicit theory-grounded mechanism components alongside final answers and distinguish component accuracy from strict joint recovery.
4KyXuzmElZ.evidence: A 4,530-item benchmark evaluates 15 LLMs using construct and contextual reasoning tasks, component-level analyses, and shortcut and permutation controls.
4KyXuzmElZ.claimed_gains: DesignReasoning answer accuracy averages 96.6% (95.3-98.2%), normalized four-component recovery averages 65.5% (45.1-84.7%), and strict four-component recovery averages 21.4%.
4KyXuzmElZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value examining correct decisions with unsupported reasoning and the systematic, expert-reviewed benchmark construction.
4KyXuzmElZ.main_concern: Agreement with a predefined Bandura-based ontology may measure label mapping rather than broader educational reasoning competence.

blmZ2YtXVD.one_liner: PULSE selects reusable preference evidence for profile updates and converts relevant stored preferences into request-specific response-evaluation criteria.
blmZ2YtXVD.problem: Personalization systems can persist temporary feedback and apply valid preferences where they do not fit the current request.
blmZ2YtXVD.method: PULSE selects evidence-bearing interaction events and decides between no update, local refinement, and long-term revision before producing sourced profile statements. It translates updated profiles into request-specific criteria for personalized candidate-response evaluation.
blmZ2YtXVD.key_idea: Separate evidence-grounded profile revision from request-specific preference application, linking profile statements and evaluation criteria to their sources.
blmZ2YtXVD.evidence: Offline ranking experiments cover two model families, static and evolving preferences, seen and unseen users, and profile-update and reward-model analyses.
blmZ2YtXVD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value separating when profiles should change from when stored preferences should influence responses, with traceable evidence links.
blmZ2YtXVD.main_concern: Ablations and missing anchor-only or query-only baselines do not isolate the contribution of profile updating and selective personalization.

ki673uxHST.one_liner: LightMTP predicts future latent representations using a model's own hidden states as lightweight multi-token training targets.
ki673uxHST.problem: Next-token supervision emphasizes local patterns, while existing multi-token objectives add substantial computation or require external representation teachers.
ki673uxHST.method: LightMTP bootstraps future-token representations from the same model's hidden states. Two parameter-efficient latent prediction variants extend supervision beyond the immediate next token without an external helper model.
ki673uxHST.key_idea: Train lightweight latent predictors against future hidden states from the model's own forward pass.
ki673uxHST.evidence: Experiments evaluate general language modeling, planning, coding, and reasoning, with comparisons of prediction horizons, target layers, regularization, and existing multi-token methods.
ki673uxHST.claimed_gains: LightMTP adds at most 1% extra parameters.
ki673uxHST.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the simplicity and low training overhead of reusing same-model hidden states without changing inference.
ki673uxHST.main_concern: Incomplete comparisons and unmatched auxiliary-loss or baseline configurations leave advantages over related multi-token approaches uncertain.

Pl9YE0reNt.one_liner: Projects student rollouts onto a positive-negative teacher exponential-family path and sets distillation targets a fixed step ahead.
Pl9YE0reNt.problem: Single-teacher on-policy distillation specifies only one target distribution to imitate, providing neither an explicit extrapolation direction nor adaptation to the student's current capability state.
Pl9YE0reNt.method: Contrastive On-Policy Distillation (COPD) combines positive-teacher attraction and negative-teacher repulsion in a conditional KL loss on student prefixes, defining a closed-form exponential-family path of virtual teachers. State-Aware COPD (SACOPD) projects each student rollout onto this path via one-dimensional convex reverse-KL minimization and places the distillation target a fixed coordinate increment ahead of that projection.
Pl9YE0reNt.key_idea: Localize each student rollout along a positive-negative teacher exponential-family path via 1D reverse-KL projection and set the distillation target a fixed increment ahead.
Pl9YE0reNt.evidence: Mathematical derivation of the virtual-teacher identity and reverse-KL projection alongside experiments with a Qwen3-4B student (300 training rollouts) on mathematics and three code benchmarks against OPD and extrapolative baselines.
Pl9YE0reNt.claimed_gains: With a Qwen3-4B student and 300 training rollouts, static COPD raises mathematics sample accuracy from matched OPD's 46.17% to 58.91% (compared with the positive teacher's 49.04%), while SACOPD reaches 59.48% and improves accuracy and coverage over COPD on all three code benchmarks.
Pl9YE0reNt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the virtual-teacher exponential-family formulation and reverse-KL projection provide a coherent mathematical framework that improves over standard on-policy distillation on math and code benchmarks.
Pl9YE0reNt.main_concern: Reviewers find empirical gains over strong extrapolative baselines such as W2S-OPD modest, question mathematical equivalence to G-OPD up to scaling, and note missing static-sweep and global-replay controls on code to isolate state conditioning.

qdUVSy55Cz.one_liner: Trains an RL knowledge-bank curator for LLM agents using marginal task-success rewards and token-wise mutual-information feedback.
qdUVSy55Cz.problem: Training an experience curator solely on standalone task success reinforces generic advice that duplicates existing entries rather than adding complementary value to a growing knowledge bank.
qdUVSy55Cz.method: Knowledge Weaver uses reinforcement learning to train a language model to distill reusable knowledge entries from agent trajectories. Its reward combines standalone task success, marginal success comparing execution with and without the new entry added to the retrieved bank, and a token-wise mutual-information-inspired contrast encouraging distinct trajectory-specific content.
qdUVSy55Cz.key_idea: Combine bank-relative marginal task-success rewards with token-wise mutual-information likelihood contrasts to RL-train a curator that writes non-redundant knowledge-bank entries.
qdUVSy55Cz.evidence: Evaluated on ALFWorld and WebShop with k=10 retrieved entries against standalone GRPO, prompt-based curators, and existing knowledge banks, with reward-component ablations.
qdUVSy55Cz.claimed_gains: On ALFWorld and WebShop with k=10 retrieved entries, Knowledge Weaver achieves mean success rates of 54.0% and 42.0%, exceeding GRPO by 16.9 and 18.7 percentage points, respectively.
qdUVSy55Cz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that distinguishing marginal utility within an existing knowledge bank from standalone entry utility is a meaningful and well-motivated formulation for agent memory curation.
qdUVSy55Cz.main_concern: Reviewers point out that the ablations omit a standalone-plus-marginal-success baseline without the MI term—leaving the necessity of MI unproven—and question conceptual differentiation from prior RL-trained skill and memory curators.

GZUtb8xWwd.one_liner: Aligns medical vision-language models via span-level preference optimization on minimally edited self-generations and lesion-corrupted counterfactual images.
GZUtb8xWwd.problem: Response-level DPO in medical vision-language models fails to localize credit to clinically decisive phrases and exploits stylistic differences from reference responses without improving clinical accuracy.
GZUtb8xWwd.method: Fine-grained Regularized Medical Preference Optimization (FiRe-MPO) constructs on-policy preference pairs by minimally editing the model's own outputs on clinically decisive spans so stylistic confounding is removed. It combines span-level textual preference supervision with lesion-corrupted counterfactual images that withhold supporting visual evidence to enforce visual grounding.
GZUtb8xWwd.key_idea: Construct preference pairs by minimally editing clinically decisive spans in self-generated responses and pair them with lesion-corrupted images withholding visual support.
GZUtb8xWwd.evidence: Evaluated across two medical LVLM backbones and multiple medical VQA benchmarks (including SLAKE and VQA-RAD), accompanied by token-level reward-localization analyses and objective ablations.
GZUtb8xWwd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that diagnosing stylistic reward hacking and constructing minimally edited span-level preference pairs is a well-motivated approach to fine-grained clinical alignment.
GZUtb8xWwd.main_concern: Reviewers raise concerns about single-run statistical reporting with apparent table discrepancies, incremental differences over prior medical DPO methods, and shortcut leakage from coupling ground-truth-localized image corruption with preference reversal.

dFKjXSa0dl.one_liner: Groups tasks, mixes cross-branch features, and merges branches across depth to compress multi-task spatial audio encoders.
dFKjXSa0dl.problem: Assigning a separate transformer branch to sound event detection, distance prediction, and direction-of-arrival estimation triples encoder computation despite shared parameters.
dFKjXSa0dl.method: Guided by layer-wise representational affinity between sound event, distance, and direction tasks, Efficient SpatialAST (ESpAST) groups compatible tasks, inserts lightweight cross-branch mixers, and merges branches in deeper layers. The reduced-computation encoders are evaluated standalone and coupled with large language models for spatial audio question answering.
dFKjXSa0dl.key_idea: Use layer-wise task-affinity profiles to group spatial audio tasks, couple branches with lightweight mixers, and merge branches in deeper transformer layers.
dFKjXSa0dl.evidence: Controlled grid experiments crossing task groupings, merge depths, and cross-branch mixers across multiple seeds on SpatialSoundQA, including downstream LLM spatial audio question-answering evaluations.
dFKjXSa0dl.claimed_gains: On SpatialSoundQA, ESpAST-1.5B_DOA^M achieves a 7.89% average relative improvement across three tasks over a three-branch baseline while reducing encoder multiply-accumulate operations by 52.2%.
dFKjXSa0dl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the systematic controlled ablations demonstrate roughly half the three-branch encoder compute can be cut while preserving or improving multi-task spatial audio performance.
dFKjXSa0dl.main_concern: Reviewers note that performance gains stem largely from multi-task optimization (FAMO) and cross-branch mixers rather than branch merging itself, and miss comparisons against standard early-sharing/late-branching or recent FOA and array spatial encoders.

fYBDP9snn5.one_liner: Discretizes bid-ask prices on two coupled grids with Hedge to achieve root-T regret under limit-order-book feedback.
fYBDP9snn5.problem: Prior online market-making algorithms under limit-order-book censored feedback—where trader valuations are observed only when no trade occurs—achieved suboptimal O-tilde(T^(2/3)) regret.
fYBDP9snn5.method: The authors discretize the continuous bid-ask space using two coupled price grids and combine this discretization with Hedge, first under full feedback and then adapted to one-sided limit-order-book feedback under i.i.d. trader valuations and adversarial market prices. They also prove an impossibility bound showing sublinear regret is unattainable when both market prices and trader valuations are chosen adversarially.
fYBDP9snn5.key_idea: Couple two discretized bid and ask price grids with Hedge updates adapted to censored non-trade limit-order-book valuation feedback.
fYBDP9snn5.evidence: Formal high-probability regret upper bounds in full-feedback and limit-order-book feedback settings plus an impossibility proof for fully adversarial market prices and trader valuations.
fYBDP9snn5.claimed_gains: Improves online market-making regret under limit-order-book feedback from expected O-tilde(T^(2/3)) to a high-probability bound of O-tilde(sqrt(T)), and proves sublinear regret is impossible under doubly adversarial prices and valuations.
fYBDP9snn5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the paper is clearly written, sharpens the limit-order-book regret rate from T^(2/3) to sqrt(T), and contributes a pertinent impossibility result for doubly adversarial market making.
fYBDP9snn5.main_concern: Reviewers question practical realism—specifically assuming a known horizon T, observing private trader valuations upon non-execution, and lacking empirical baselines—as well as technical advancement beyond classical Hedge bandit analyses.

ztsOyosv31.one_liner: GIGA groups worker-wise sparse gradient means to control update coalescing in recommendation training.
ztsOyosv31.problem: Large-batch CTR training coalesces sparse updates unevenly, hurting frequent and rare IDs differently under one learning-rate multiplier.
ztsOyosv31.method: GIGA averages each active ID's gradients within worker groups, sums group means for the numerator, and separately accumulates their elementwise squares for Adagrad state.
ztsOyosv31.key_idea: Worker grouping controls how many per-ID gradient terms survive coalescing without frequency statistics, extra collectives, or persistent ID state.
ztsOyosv31.evidence: Controlled experiments vary workers, batches, aggregation rules, and group sizes, with multi-day tests and scaling to 512 workers.
ztsOyosv31.claimed_gains: In a controlled 96-worker comparison, GIGA improves AUC and request-level GAUC by 0.03 and 0.13 percentage points, respectively.
ztsOyosv31.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that GIGA cleanly couples sparse aggregation with optimizer state and offers practical distributed-training integration.
ztsOyosv31.main_concern: Reviewers most often note that simpler aggregation methods match GIGA at the largest scale, leaving its incremental benefit unclear.

kJA2gTmfDZ.one_liner: O²PD aligns reliable rollout prefixes with overlap-gated support corrections for on-policy distillation.
kJA2gTmfDZ.problem: Top-k on-policy distillation applies unreliable teacher guidance on student rollouts and discards probability mass outside teacher support.
kJA2gTmfDZ.method: O²PD restricts alignment to rollout prefixes and uses overlap-gated support strategies, including a reset atom for mass outside the teacher's top-k support.
kJA2gTmfDZ.key_idea: Token-set overlap gates alternative divergence support while prefix-only alignment limits unreliable teacher supervision.
kJA2gTmfDZ.evidence: The paper combines formal analysis of top-k failure modes with experiments across teacher–student model pairs on reasoning tasks.
kJA2gTmfDZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the theoretical characterization of top-k OPD is clear and that O²PD improves consistently across tested model pairs.
kJA2gTmfDZ.main_concern: Reviewers most often challenge the evidence for prefix-only alignment and the link between set overlap and the probability-mass conditions in the theory.

fS0JztNNf6.one_liner: ANNO reuses steady-state-trained spatial eigenmodes with known modal dynamics for transient PDE prediction.
fS0JztNNf6.problem: Neural PDE solvers usually require transient trajectories and retraining despite governing equations already specifying temporal evolution.
fS0JztNNf6.method: ANNO learns lifting functions, spatial eigenmodes, and modal coefficients from steady-state problems, then freezes the networks and advances modal coefficients using target-PDE dynamics.
fS0JztNNf6.key_idea: An eigenproblem-constrained spatial representation separates learned steady structure from equation-specified temporal evolution.
fS0JztNNf6.evidence: Seven experiments cover steady solutions, eigenstructure recovery, 1D diffusion, 2D wave dynamics, and 2D and 3D thermal dynamics.
fS0JztNNf6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that reusing explicit eigenstructure without transient training is interpretable and supported by within-family experiments.
fS0JztNNf6.main_concern: Reviewers most often question its advantage over classical modal methods because tests use linear, constant-coefficient problems with known or cheap eigensolutions.

Hdwn4xkEHp.one_liner: Applies deterministic mutation testing with 10,303 injected CUDA faults to measure and optimize GPU-kernel benchmark correctness checkers.
Hdwn4xkEHp.problem: Correctness checkers for LLM-generated GPU kernels use loose tolerances and few random inputs without any quantitative measure of fault-detection adequacy.
Hdwn4xkEHp.method: Deterministic mutation rules inject 10,303 compilable faults into verified CUDA kernels for 189 KernelBench problems, retaining 7,384 faults with independent kill witnesses. Test protocols are scored by kill fraction, and compact high-detection test suites are selected via set cover over the kill matrix.
Hdwn4xkEHp.key_idea: Injects deterministic compilable CUDA mutants with independent kill witnesses to score and optimize GPU-kernel benchmark oracles.
Hdwn4xkEHp.evidence: Evaluates official KernelBench, KernelBench-Verified, and a published fuzzing recipe across 7,384 witnessed mutants plus 60 LLM-generated kernels.
Hdwn4xkEHp.claimed_gains: Official KernelBench misses 16.9% of witnessed faults (8.7% arithmetic, 78.6% precision); KernelBench-Verified splits into +4.0 hidden-input and +4.5 tolerance points; set-cover optimization reaches 98.0% detection with two inputs per problem.
Hdwn4xkEHp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the importance of quantifying GPU-kernel oracle adequacy and value the large-scale mutation fault-family analysis.
Hdwn4xkEHp.main_concern: Synthetically injected mutants in reference CUDA code may not reflect real LLM-generated kernel bugs, and set-cover suites are evaluated in-sample on the same kill matrix.

UhZ92ST1bV.one_liner: Constructs bounded offline warm-start bandit attacks that combine target-arm promotion and non-target suppression with optimal sublinear cost.
UhZ92ST1bV.problem: Prior bandit attack analyses focus on online reward suppression, overlooking realistic offline warm-start poisoning where target promotion is often required.
UhZ92ST1bV.method: Under a bounded offline-only threat model injecting valid action-reward pairs into warm-start logs, the paper proves target promotion is mandatory near the lower reward boundary and derives an optimal allocation between target promotion and non-target suppression for UCB, extending to Thompson Sampling and epsilon-greedy.
UhZ92ST1bV.key_idea: Proves near-boundary offline bandit attacks must allocate a 2/3 cost share to target promotion and designs matching sublinear-cost injections.
UhZ92ST1bV.evidence: Derives matching upper and lower attack-cost bounds for UCB and evaluates on synthetic and real-world bandit datasets.
UhZ92ST1bV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the realistic offline-only bounded threat model and the nontrivial UCB lower/upper cost bounds with 2/3 target allocation.
UhZ92ST1bV.main_concern: Tight optimality bounds hold only in a narrow regime with near-boundary targets and O(1) clean logs per arm, and empirical baselines are online rather than offline-matched.

uXlRrFrvsy.one_liner: Updates on-policy RL actors via self-normalized importance sampling against an entropy- and KL-regularized forward-KL target without critic gradients.
uXlRrFrvsy.problem: Actor-critic methods rely on critic action gradients that can be inaccurate when critics are only trained to predict scalar returns.
uXlRrFrvsy.method: FERPO derives an optimal policy-improvement target regularized by entropy and KL divergence from the rollout policy, then fits the actor by minimizing forward KL using self-normalized importance sampling (SNIS) with an effective-sample-size controller.
uXlRrFrvsy.key_idea: Fits the actor to an entropy- and KL-regularized target distribution via forward-KL self-normalized importance sampling without differentiating the critic.
uXlRrFrvsy.evidence: Evaluates across 34 continuous-control tasks on MuJoCo Playground and ManiSkill with runtime measurements and ablations.
uXlRrFrvsy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the derivative-free actor update practical, well explained, and backed by broad continuous-control benchmarks.
uXlRrFrvsy.main_concern: Rollout-policy sampling fails to cover unvisited high-value modes as claimed by forward-KL motivation, and positioning/comparison against MORE and V-MPO is missing.

9gMTTrqcvP.one_liner: Decouples temporal and structural learning by feeding foundation temporal embeddings, local summaries, and supra-Laplacian encodings into a GNN.
9gMTTrqcvP.problem: Temporal graph models entangle temporal dynamics with structural propagation, limiting zero-shot transfer across unseen graphs.
9gMTTrqcvP.method: MOSAIC extracts three domain-agnostic priors—foundation-model temporal embeddings, local temporal-context summaries, and supra-Laplacian positional encodings of evolving topology—before passing them to a GNN without recurrent BPTT.
9gMTTrqcvP.key_idea: Composes pretrained temporal foundation embeddings, local summaries, and supra-Laplacian positional encodings as decoupled inputs to a GNN.
9gMTTrqcvP.evidence: Evaluates on supervised temporal graph benchmarks and zero-shot transfer across 20 unseen networks in MiNT, plus memory/runtime scaling.
9gMTTrqcvP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the simple, BPTT-free modular design and flat memory/runtime scaling across long input windows.
9gMTTrqcvP.main_concern: The zero-shot MiNT benchmark has constant node features, rendering both temporal priors uninformative so transfer results only test supra-Laplacian structural encodings.

thVLeQiv87.one_liner: Projects LoRA input factors onto orthogonal complements of old-task activation subspaces sized by Fisher sensitivity coverage.
thVLeQiv87.problem: Sequential LoRA continual learning suffers additive interference when new adapters produce non-zero responses along input directions important to prior tasks.
thVLeQiv87.method: SPACE-LoRA projects the input factor of a new LoRA branch onto the orthogonal complement of historical activation subspaces after each step while keeping both factors trainable. Module-specific protection coverage is allocated using empirical Fisher sensitivity.
thVLeQiv87.key_idea: Orthogonally projects new LoRA input factors away from old activation subspaces with per-module coverage allocated by Fisher sensitivity.
thVLeQiv87.evidence: Evaluates on vision (ImageNet-R) and 10-task language continual learning benchmarks under class- and task-incremental protocols.
thVLeQiv87.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the clean, exact module-level null-response projection guarantee and cross-modal evaluation on vision and language tasks.
thVLeQiv87.main_concern: Novelty over GPM/InfLoRA is incremental, and the Fisher-allocation ablation does not match total protection budgets or compare against activation-energy sizing.

LiPYCDhjOm.one_liner: Jointly optimizes dynamic sparse training and concept erasure in diffusion U-Nets using a concept-ratio pruning criterion.
LiPYCDhjOm.problem: Sequential pruning and concept erasure in diffusion models either erases on a suboptimal sparse topology or restores erased concepts during sparsity recovery.
LiPYCDhjOm.method: EwS progressively reduces model density under joint erasure and preservation losses, applying magnitude pruning and gradient regrowth to conv layers and a concept-ratio score to prune cross-attention key/value weights.
LiPYCDhjOm.key_idea: Co-optimizes dynamic sparse topology and concept erasure using gradual magnitude pruning in convolutions and target-relative concept-ratio pruning in cross-attention.
LiPYCDhjOm.evidence: Evaluations on Stable Diffusion 1.4 across artistic-style, object-class, and explicit-content erasure under matched sparse budgets.
LiPYCDhjOm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the joint sparse-and-safe diffusion deployment problem is well motivated and shows strong empirical trade-offs on SD 1.4.
LiPYCDhjOm.main_concern: Evaluation is restricted to U-Net (SD 1.4) at 75% density without DiT validation, standard unlearning benchmarks (e.g., UnlearnCanvas), or fair sequential recovery setups.

7IzEsa2wdO.one_liner: Enforces policy checks via a code approval layer and learns hidden environment rules through abductive trajectory diagnosis.
7IzEsa2wdO.problem: Enterprise LLM agents face hidden side effects under partial observability and must strictly obey organizational policies over long-horizon tasks.
7IzEsa2wdO.method: E-Ledger gates every action through a code approval layer and tracks dynamic state in a world ledger, while WorldAbduct diagnoses trajectories across four views to hypothesize and verify latent rules via targeted interactions.
7IzEsa2wdO.key_idea: Combine pre-execution programmatic policy gating and a persistent world ledger with abductive hypothesis testing of hidden environment rules.
7IzEsa2wdO.evidence: Evaluations across four LLM backbones on World of Workflows (WOW), plus ScienceWorld and DiscoveryWorld experiments and ablations, support the framework.
7IzEsa2wdO.claimed_gains: On World of Workflows, E-Ledger with WorldAbduct outperforms the strongest evolution baseline by 5-15 percentage points across four LLM backbones.
7IzEsa2wdO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that policy enforcement and abductive verification of hidden environment dynamics address an important enterprise agent challenge.
7IzEsa2wdO.main_concern: All reviewers flag the tiny evaluation scale (20 WOW test tasks evaluated with single runs and no confidence intervals, where 5-15 points equals 1-3 tasks) and missing training-cost comparisons.

b3lZofUyGC.one_liner: Uses causal interventions on GLA, GDN, and hybrid models to trace how linear attention writes, couples, and reads facts.
b3lZofUyGC.problem: How fixed-size recurrent states in linear-attention models store, interfere across, and retrieve multiple facts compared to KV caches is poorly understood.
b3lZofUyGC.method: Combining an analytical decomposition with causal interventions (write blocking, state replacement, output patching) on pretrained GLA, GDN, and hybrid Qwen3.5 models, the authors trace memory writes, cross-fact coupling, and read pathways.
b3lZofUyGC.key_idea: Apply targeted causal state and output interventions to isolate content-dependent writes, overlap-driven interference, and sparse query-time read heads in recurrent states.
b3lZofUyGC.evidence: Controlled key-value association interventions on 340M GLA/GDN models, Qwen3.5 hybrids, PG19, and RULER benchmarks support the analysis.
b3lZofUyGC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the clean causal intervention design and the replicated finding that hybrid models shift recall to full-attention KV states.
b3lZofUyGC.main_concern: Reviewers note that the full lifecycle analysis is limited to synthetic single-token key-value tasks at short contexts (128-1024 tokens) and argue that some read-pathway tests are confounded by construction.

Qz5KFKVFeD.one_liner: Supervises intermediate MLLM latent states using a training-only frozen visual teacher encoding dynamically selected image regions.
Qz5KFKVFeD.problem: Existing multimodal latent reasoning methods lack adaptive intermediate supervision specifying what visual evidence each latent state should predict.
Qz5KFKVFeD.method: TraViS lets each intermediate latent state select task-relevant visual regions from the evolving context and aligns it with continuous embeddings from a frozen crop teacher during training. At inference, the crop teacher is disabled so the model performs self-feedback latent rollout over a single global image encoding.
Qz5KFKVFeD.key_idea: A training-only frozen visual teacher encodes context-selected crops to supervise intermediate latent states, which revert to single-encoding rollout at inference.
Qz5KFKVFeD.evidence: Evaluations span multiple VLM backbones across eight multimodal reasoning benchmarks.
Qz5KFKVFeD.claimed_gains: Delivers over 2.5% average improvement across eight multimodal reasoning benchmarks while reducing inference latency.
Qz5KFKVFeD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that supervising intermediate latent trajectories with an external visual teacher only during training is an interesting and inference-efficient design.
Qz5KFKVFeD.main_concern: Reviewers cite missing data-matched SFT and unsupervised-latent baselines, fixed rollout lengths, and unclear region selection or potential bias on tasks not needing region-to-region trajectories.

4wPAgbk91f.one_liner: Shows that step-pooled GRPO's within-group standard deviation division cancels small auxiliary reward coefficients and collapses agent performance.
4wPAgbk91f.problem: Small coefficients and telescoping episodic bounds on auxiliary rewards fail to prevent policy collapse in multi-turn LLM agent RL.
4wPAgbk91f.method: The authors analyze next-observation prediction rewards in step-pooled GRPO on ALFWorld and WebShop, showing that standardizing steps before telescoping allows residual prediction increments to dominate when task returns tie, canceling the coefficient. They test removing std division and filtering all-failure groups.
4wPAgbk91f.key_idea: Demonstrates that step-pooled within-group std division in GRPO cancels small auxiliary-reward coefficients when task returns tie, and restores learning by removing std division.
4wPAgbk91f.evidence: Experiments on Qwen3-1.7B, 4B, and 8B on ALFWorld and WebShop with coefficient sweeps, normalization ablations, and variance measurements.
4wPAgbk91f.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the empirical collapse across model scales striking and the mathematical explanation of std-division coefficient cancellation clear.
4wPAgbk91f.main_concern: Reviewers note overlap with prior GRPO normalization critiques (e.g., Dr. GRPO), reliance on specific boundary/initialization conditions, and dense presentation.

CuajMjgjh2.one_liner: Extracts recurring object cues from image variants and conditions VLM rollouts on them to synthesize grounded preference pairs.
CuajMjgjh2.problem: Preference alignment for VLM hallucination mitigation either deviates from the policy distribution via interventions or underuses visual grounding during sampling.
CuajMjgjh2.method: ViPSy synthesizes semantically aligned image variants to extract recurring object-level visual cues, then conditions the policy's own rollouts on those cues to build preference pairs for DPO.
CuajMjgjh2.key_idea: Uses cross-variant recurring visual cues to guide the target VLM's own rollouts when constructing visually grounded preference pairs.
CuajMjgjh2.evidence: Experiments across LLaVA and Qwen2.5-VL models at 7B and 13B scales on hallucination and general vision benchmarks with extensive ablations.
CuajMjgjh2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers acknowledge substantial hallucination reductions on benchmarks like AMBER alongside preserved object recall and thorough ablations.
CuajMjgjh2.main_concern: Reviewers question whether cue-conditioned rollouts remain distributionally aligned with cue-free DPO/inference and note heavy reliance on Qwen2.5-VL-72B and costly image synthesis.

lvwKF2rVUG.one_liner: Pretrains a single PPG Transformer across 10s, 30s, and 240s stages with duration-partitioned parameters and retained-target supervision.
lvwKF2rVUG.problem: Existing PPG foundation models pretrain at a single fixed signal duration, ignoring that different physiological features require different observation durations.
lvwKF2rVUG.method: RAE-PPG trains one Transformer sequentially on 10 s, 30 s, and 240 s inputs. Each stage introduces duration-appropriate physiological targets and updates only its assigned parameter group while reading frozen earlier groups and retaining earlier-target supervision.
lvwKF2rVUG.key_idea: Partitions a single Transformer into duration-specific parameter groups trained sequentially from 10 s to 240 s with retained supervision on shorter-duration physiological targets.
lvwKF2rVUG.evidence: Evaluated on 18 downstream tasks across eight datasets against five PPG foundation models, plus feature-decodability and reuse analyses.
lvwKF2rVUG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the duration-grounded motivation sound and praise the broad, carefully controlled 18-task benchmarking with confidence intervals.
lvwKF2rVUG.main_concern: Reviewers note that progressive frozen-stage training is not compared against joint multi-duration training, a simple GRU/LSTM over fixed-length baselines, or standard SSL methods (SimCLR/TF-C) on the same backbone.

xQLW4Y2mei.one_liner: Guides robot program edits with failure frontiers and checks for regressions via stateful API replay of prior successes.
xQLW4Y2mei.problem: Updating embodied control programs risks leaving structural failures unresolved or introducing regressions on previously solved tasks.
xQLW4Y2mei.method: SCOPE annotates a shared diagnostic graph with failure frontiers to guide edits, and runs selective behavioral certification via stateful API replay (restoring recorded responses and mutations) to check if edits preserve prior successes.
xQLW4Y2mei.key_idea: Pairs failure-frontier diagnostic graphs with stateful API replay of recorded successful executions to detect regressions during iterative robot program repair.
xQLW4Y2mei.evidence: Evaluated across 60 LIBERO-PRO task-setting pairs, seven Robosuite tasks, component ablations, and physical robot tasks against ASPIRE.
xQLW4Y2mei.claimed_gains: Achieves mean success rates of 80.66% on LIBERO-PRO and 84.48% on Robosuite, with respective gains of 6.51 and 3.48 percentage points over the strongest baseline.
xQLW4Y2mei.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that balancing failure repair with regression avoidance is a real problem and note consistent gains across LIBERO-PRO, Robosuite, and real robots.
xQLW4Y2mei.main_concern: Reviewers point out missing direct seed re-execution and budget-matched ASPIRE controls, and note that certification only checks exact API-tape matches (38.9–60.6% of edits) without gating acceptance.

n39FGhK2ph.one_liner: Shows on-policy distillation can improve pass@1 while hurting large-K pass@K, and proposes TAS@K for pre-training teacher selection.
n39FGhK2ph.problem: On-policy distillation (OPD) is typically evaluated only at pass@1, obscuring when distillation gains reverse under large test-time sampling budgets (pass@K).
n39FGhK2ph.method: The authors theoretically characterize conditions where reverse-KL OPD improves pass@1 yet degrades large-K pass@K. To select between candidate teachers for a target budget K before training, they propose the Teacher Advantage Score (TAS@K) computed from base-student and teacher likelihoods.
n39FGhK2ph.key_idea: Characterizes pass@1-to-pass@K reversals in reverse-KL on-policy distillation and introduces TAS@K to predict which candidate teacher yields higher pass@K before training.
n39FGhK2ph.evidence: Evaluated across three domains (math, code, fact), thirteen benchmarks, eight student-teacher configurations, and sampling budgets up to pass@1024.
n39FGhK2ph.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that showing OPD can improve pass@1 while degrading large-K pass@K is an important empirical and theoretical observation for test-time scaling.
n39FGhK2ph.main_concern: Reviewers question the practical utility of TAS@K, noting its 83.6% agreement pools correlated budgets across only four teacher pairs and underperforms simply picking the teacher with higher pass@K in Code.

luqpwMQ2MV.one_liner: Maintains a query-specific anchor buffer of judged responses for coarse-to-fine ranking rewards in open-ended RL.
luqpwMQ2MV.problem: Pointwise rewards in open-ended RL suffer from poor calibration, while full pairwise/listwise ranking of rollouts incurs heavy LLM-judge costs.
luqpwMQ2MV.method: RankBuffer stores an evolving, query-specific ordered buffer of anchor responses. New rollouts undergo an independent coarse judgment to locate an anchor interval, followed by local fine ranking only among rollouts sharing that interval, converting the resulting order into bounded rank rewards.
luqpwMQ2MV.key_idea: Uses an evolving per-query buffer of anchor responses to route new rollouts into intervals via coarse judging before performing local fine ranking only within each interval.
luqpwMQ2MV.evidence: Evaluated across four open-ended benchmarks against pointwise and ranking-based reward baselines (RRC-SCR, ArenaRL, Tournament-GRPO) with ablations.
luqpwMQ2MV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the anchor-based coarse-to-fine ranking framework clear, easy to implement, and effective at reducing judge tokens and requests while matching strong ranking baselines.
luqpwMQ2MV.main_concern: Reviewers point out that training and all four evaluations rely on the same Qwen3-30B-A3B judge without independent human/cross-judge validation, and question multi-epoch query-revisiting assumptions.

x7dbIE7vzc.one_liner: Augments diffusion L2 measurement guidance with patch-wise Earth Mover's Distance over depth histograms for LiDAR restoration.
x7dbIE7vzc.problem: Applying 2D diffusion inverse-problem solvers with L2 guidance to LiDAR range views ignores 2.5D spatial depth correlations under weather corruptions.
x7dbIE7vzc.method: They add a correlative guidance term implemented as a patch-wise Earth Mover's Distance (EMD) comparing local depth histograms to standard L2 measurement guidance in a pretrained LiDAR diffusion model.
x7dbIE7vzc.key_idea: Augments pixel-wise L2 diffusion guidance with a patch-wise Earth Mover's Distance loss over local LiDAR depth histograms.
x7dbIE7vzc.evidence: Evaluations across eight corruption types on 4,071 SemanticKITTI frames using a pretrained R2DM model, plus runtime and loss ablations.
x7dbIE7vzc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the simple, low-overhead guidance term that reuses a pretrained LiDAR diffusion model across eight corruptions.
x7dbIE7vzc.main_concern: The statistical premise conflates conditional noise independence with signal independence, and evaluations use exact corruption metadata while omitting R2DM/RePaint baselines.

o6p3lP7PfM.one_liner: Analyzes how distillation divergence choices (forward KL, reverse KL, JS) and data sampling implicitly control student entropy.
o6p3lP7PfM.problem: The mechanisms by which distillation divergences and sampling distributions shape student predictive entropy in LLM training are not well understood.
o6p3lP7PfM.method: The authors prove an identity showing forward KL inflates student entropy above the teacher, analyze reverse KL and intermediate divergences theoretically and in toy models, and test self-distillation with privileged conditioning.
o6p3lP7PfM.key_idea: Proves forward KL inflates student entropy above the teacher while reverse KL deflates it until task difficulty triggers inflation.
o6p3lP7PfM.evidence: Information-geometric proofs, categorical toy models, and LLM pretraining, SFT, GSM8K, Chemistry, and self-distillation experiments.
o6p3lP7PfM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the interpretable forward-KL entropy identity and the disentanglement of sampling distribution from divergence choice.
o6p3lP7PfM.main_concern: Token-summed versus length-normalized entropy conventions are inconsistent between theory and metrics, and large-model experiments mostly use single seeds on narrow tasks.

lH9II2H8AZ.one_liner: Extracts activation steering vectors for frozen open-source agents by replaying contrasted frontier-model text traces.
lH9II2H8AZ.problem: Transferring frontier-agent capabilities to smaller open-source agents via distillation or latent communication typically requires target-model training or source-model internal access.
lH9II2H8AZ.method: REVEAL replays successful and failed textual frontier-model rollouts through a frozen target agent to profile anchored states across feedback-response cycles. It contrasts matched local response transitions to derive a target-specific steering vector applied before each response without training.
lH9II2H8AZ.key_idea: Replays contrasted successful and failed frontier-model text traces in a frozen target agent to extract local activation steering vectors.
lH9II2H8AZ.evidence: Evaluated within-benchmark on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and Humanity's Last Exam with tools across three target models.
lH9II2H8AZ.claimed_gains: Reports higher accuracy than unmodified agents across three target models (exact numbers not stated in abstract).
lH9II2H8AZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that training-free transfer using only frontier text traces without teacher hidden states is practically appealing.
lH9II2H8AZ.main_concern: Reviewers raise concerns about within-benchmark evaluation lacking a held-out task split to separate adaptation from generalization, and unclear steering stability under autonomous divergence.

QiA1kAVyWR.one_liner: Elicits offline privileged rationales from frontier MLLMs for on-policy self-distillation in omni-modal affective reasoning.
QiA1kAVyWR.problem: Outcome-based RL for affective computing provides sparse sequence-level rewards that can reinforce correct labels paired with misinterpreted multimodal cues.
QiA1kAVyWR.method: OmniOPSD uses ground-truth affective labels as priors to elicit evidence-rich rationales offline from frontier MLLMs, then runs on-policy student rollouts supervised at the token level via JSD by a local EMA self-teacher conditioned on those privileged rationales.
QiA1kAVyWR.key_idea: Decouples offline frontier-MLLM rationale elicitation from online token-level JSD self-distillation on student rollouts using a rationale-privileged EMA teacher.
QiA1kAVyWR.evidence: Evaluated across two model scales, in-distribution and out-of-distribution affective benchmarks, and rationale/thinking ablations.
QiA1kAVyWR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the motivation of replacing sparse label rewards with dense token-level supervision without online frontier-model calls.
QiA1kAVyWR.main_concern: Reviewers cite strong methodological overlap with privileged-context OPD works (Vision-OPD, ViCuR), lack of factual audits on generated rationales, and missing expert human evaluation.

Kd0yKjgnuy.one_liner: Supervises environment observation tokens during SFT to improve exploration and generalization in subsequent RL.
Kd0yKjgnuy.problem: Standard agent SFT masks environment observation tokens from the loss, potentially yielding suboptimal initializations for downstream reinforcement learning.
Kd0yKjgnuy.method: ActObs unmasks and applies next-token cross-entropy supervision to both action and observation tokens during SFT prior to GRPO reinforcement learning.
Kd0yKjgnuy.key_idea: Applies standard SFT cross-entropy loss to environment observation tokens alongside action tokens without extra data, parameters, or forward passes.
Kd0yKjgnuy.evidence: Evaluated on Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B (plus 3B) using GRPO on Terminal-Bench 2.0 and cross-domain code editing on aider-polyglot.
Kd0yKjgnuy.claimed_gains: On Qwen3-8B, ActObs improves pass@16 by +3.4 pp on Terminal-Bench 2.0, and on Qwen3-4B improves aider-polyglot pass@1 by +4.2 pp.
Kd0yKjgnuy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that unmasking observation tokens during SFT is simple, cheap, and trivial to adopt while revealing an interesting SFT-to-RL gap.
Kd0yKjgnuy.main_concern: Reviewers note narrow evaluation limited to terminal coding tasks, small gains over ActionSFT+ECHO, missing training-seed variance, and overlap with prior world-modeling RL work.

vpxCnpfkBh.one_liner: Proves that an agent's interventional and counterfactual action preference rankings are generically underdetermined from lower-layer behavioral data.
vpxCnpfkBh.problem: It is unclear whether observing an agent's behavior or lower-level interventions suffices in principle to identify its higher-layer action preference rankings.
vpxCnpfkBh.method: The authors prove a preference-level counterpart to the Causal Hierarchy Theorem using structural causal models and topological stability arguments.
vpxCnpfkBh.key_idea: Establishes via structural causal models and measure-theoretic genericity that even coarse action rankings at higher causal layers are underdetermined by lower-layer distributions.
vpxCnpfkBh.evidence: Purely theoretical results (Theorems 3 and 4) with illustrative examples.
vpxCnpfkBh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that extending the Causal Hierarchy Theorem from probabilities to action rankings is a well-motivated theoretical warning for agent evaluation.
vpxCnpfkBh.main_concern: Reviewers question the product-measure assumption, note that non-identifiability of a full ordering does not imply ambiguity in optimal action choice, and flag a potential convexity error across causal orders.

M4YFmS6Tmt.one_liner: Pairs mutual GNN-MLP distillation with a momentum teacher to prevent cross-domain interference in multi-domain graph pre-training.
M4YFmS6Tmt.problem: Graph foundation models often fail to improve with more pre-training domains due to propagation flattening node relations and unstable early domain alignment.
M4YFmS6Tmt.method: FLO combines reciprocal knowledge transfer between a GNN and an MLP to capture attribute-predictable relations beyond message passing with a slow momentum teacher to stabilize multi-domain alignment, leaving only the GCN encoder at inference.
M4YFmS6Tmt.key_idea: Uses fast-slow reciprocal GNN-MLP mutual learning with a momentum teacher to retain non-propagated attribute structure and reduce cross-domain interference.
M4YFmS6Tmt.evidence: Evaluated with leave-one-domain-out transfer across six source domains and downstream tasks, with ablations.
M4YFmS6Tmt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers note the paper tackles a relevant multi-domain graph pre-training problem with competitive transfer results and zero inference overhead.
M4YFmS6Tmt.main_concern: The method recombines existing techniques (GLNN/DML/BGRL), experiments use a single pre-training seed with inconsistent target hyperparameters, and mechanistic claims lack direct evidence.

ssZspQkJEI.one_liner: Introduces a 190k-frame UAV infrared-visible video dataset with text descriptions and a frame-level text-guided fusion baseline.
ssZspQkJEI.problem: Infrared-visible image fusion is typically developed on isolated image pairs, leaving continuous UAV video streaming and text conditioning underexplored.
ssZspQkJEI.method: The authors release UAV-VIVID, comprising 375 scene-disjoint continuous UAV segments (190,978 paired frames) with structured text descriptions across low-altitude registered, high-altitude, and unregistered splits. They also propose RT-FuseNet, a frame-level baseline using Adaptive Residual Balancing and Text-Affine and Gated Modulation.
ssZspQkJEI.key_idea: Benchmarking continuous UAV infrared-visible video fusion with scene-disjoint text-annotated splits and a frame-level text-modulated fusion network.
ssZspQkJEI.evidence: Experiments on the 96,087 registered low-altitude pairs of UAV-VIVID evaluating frame quality, sequence behavior, text conditioning, and PGD augmentation.
ssZspQkJEI.claimed_gains: Releases 375 continuous scene segments and 190,978 paired frames (96,087 registered low-altitude, 79,992 higher-altitude, and 14,899 unregistered low-altitude pairs).
ssZspQkJEI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the scene-disjoint UAV-VIVID video dataset with text annotations is a useful community resource for continuous IR-VI fusion.
ssZspQkJEI.main_concern: Reviewers note limited novelty in RT-FuseNet's non-temporal architecture, lack of evaluation protocols on the high-altitude and unregistered subsets, and insufficient ablations of text gating.

H1EYLTqTxd.one_liner: Trains coding agents on three-step development consequence chains using a test-gated hindsight judge reward for downstream extensibility.
H1EYLTqTxd.problem: Coding agents trained only on immediate task rewards often write patches that pass current tests while making subsequent sequential requirements infeasible or harder to implement.
H1EYLTqTxd.method: The authors mine three-requirement consequence chains from development histories where early structural decisions affect later steps. They train agents with asynchronous PPO using a gated reward R = A + λAJ, requiring whole-chain test correctness (A) before adding a hindsight judge score (J) that evaluates downstream extensibility.
H1EYLTqTxd.key_idea: Training agents on mined multi-step consequence chains with a test-gated hindsight LLM judge rewarding code extensibility across future requirements.
H1EYLTqTxd.evidence: Evaluated on ChainSWE and SlopCodeBench across 2B to 35B models compared against base models and Claude Opus 4.6.
H1EYLTqTxd.claimed_gains: Improves complete-chain success rate on ChainSWE by at least 28% relative to base models across 2B–35B scales; the 27B model reaches 45.7% sequential bug-resolution rate versus 42.4% for Claude Opus 4.6.
H1EYLTqTxd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that training coding agents for long-horizon code extensibility is an important problem and the gated reward formulation is clean.
H1EYLTqTxd.main_concern: Reviewers point out that ablations fail to isolate the hindsight judge and consequence-chain data from general code-quality rewards, and ChainSWE gains represent few chains without multi-seed variance.

YhD2cLYIsQ.one_liner: Reshapes GRPO outcome rewards, unnormalized step-level process token weights, and rollout filtering for agentic compile-fix under weak feedback.
YhD2cLYIsQ.problem: In agentic code repair under weak online execution feedback, GRPO suffers from coarse binary outcome rankings, diffuse intra-trajectory credit, and incomparable rollouts.
YhD2cLYIsQ.method: The method layers outcome rewards (0/0.5/1) to separate non-compiling, compile-only, and semantically correct repairs using an offline judge (Kimi-K2.5). It applies step-level process scores outside group normalization as token loss weights and enforces failure-cause-aware rollout governance to maintain within-group comparability.
YhD2cLYIsQ.key_idea: Combining layered compile-semantic outcome rewards, unnormalized process-score token weights, and failure-cause rollout governance for GRPO.
YhD2cLYIsQ.evidence: Evaluated on an internal C/C++ CI compile-fix dataset with one base model family, controlled training-fork ablations, and blind human evaluation on 400 instances.
YhD2cLYIsQ.claimed_gains: Improves strict compile-and-semantic accuracy from 0.385 zero-shot to 0.535; process-score weighting raises accuracy from 0.48 to 0.53 over layered rewards alone.
YhD2cLYIsQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that decomposing GRPO's weak-feedback failure modes into outcome ranking, process credit, and rollout comparability is well-structured with clean ablations.
YhD2cLYIsQ.main_concern: Reviewers note narrow scope (single proprietary C/C++ dataset and one base model), heavy reliance on an expensive LLM judge (Kimi-K2.5), and unvalidated 0/0.5/1 heuristic reward ordering.

RA8pOQlbPm.one_liner: Extracts reusable visual-cue utilization skills and case experiences from trajectories to guide multimodal search agents without retraining.
RA8pOQlbPm.problem: Multimodal search agents often omit or misuse visual cues during multi-step tool execution, leading to irrelevant retrieval and task failure.
RA8pOQlbPm.method: V-CUES bootstraps a skill library from historical trajectories capturing how visual cues should be used across contexts, refined by case-level experiences from new interactions. At inference, a Mentor component contextualizes these skills to guide an Actor agent without updating model parameters.
RA8pOQlbPm.key_idea: Bootstrapping and contextualizing a visual-cue utilization skill and experience library to guide frozen multimodal search agents.
RA8pOQlbPm.evidence: Evaluated across four knowledge-intensive benchmarks and three model backbones (including GPT-5.2, GPT-5.4, and Gemini 3 Flash) against XSKILL and tool-only baselines.
RA8pOQlbPm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that shifting focus from tool-calling mechanics to visual-cue omission and misuse is well-motivated and requires no parameter updates.
RA8pOQlbPm.main_concern: Reviewers note incremental novelty over XSKILL, minimal ablation impact from the experience library (0.2–0.4 points), higher token consumption (31.0k vs. 22.2k), and potential expert-data budget imbalance.

IsfTWIhKMW.one_liner: Removes direct action-to-target-evidence edges in a world model so MPC visual tracking ranks actions through ego-motion.
IsfTWIhKMW.problem: Generic action-conditioned world models trained on logged tracking data learn action-to-target shortcuts ('causal hallucination') that misrank candidate actions during planning.
IsfTWIhKMW.method: CST-WM splits latent state into target-evidence, robot, and observation branches, removing the same-step edge from action to target evidence so actions affect target evidence only through robot ego-motion and predicted observations. Rollout-based model-predictive control uses this single model for steady following and post-loss target re-acquisition.
IsfTWIhKMW.key_idea: Architecturally masks the direct same-step action-to-target-evidence transition so actions influence predicted target evidence only via robot motion and observation branches.
IsfTWIhKMW.evidence: Evaluations on EVT-Bench and Habitat 3.0 covering standard tracking, target-loss recovery, cross-dataset transfer, paired simulator action-ranking interventions, and a real-robot test.
IsfTWIhKMW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the paired simulator action-ranking protocol, the matched masking ablation showing clear gains on re-acquisition and ranking correlation, and the real-robot demonstration.
IsfTWIhKMW.main_concern: Reviewers caution that because the robot branch still encodes raw action embeddings and the evidence head reads observation tokens, the architecture does not strictly guarantee exclusion of action shortcuts, and planning is slow in simulation.

mOZfmdlbJD.one_liner: Continually adapts an input-level MoE pre-router for all layers using supervision from main-model expert-weighting gates.
mOZfmdlbJD.problem: Hidden-state MoE routing blocks expert prefetching, while existing input-token pre-routers freeze their routing policies and stop adapting during training.
mOZfmdlbJD.method: AhaMoE initializes a standalone all-layer pre-router and partially reuses parameters from an early source model. During target training, original gates retained solely to weight expert outputs provide continual distillation supervision so the pre-router adapts expert assignments before layer computation.
mOZfmdlbJD.key_idea: Continually supervises a standalone all-layer input pre-router by distilling logits from the main model's expert-output weighting gates.
mOZfmdlbJD.evidence: Experiments on 2.6B-parameter MoE target models trained on 32B tokens comparing against pre-routed and hidden-routed baselines, plus component ablations and offloading latency measurements.
mOZfmdlbJD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that continual pre-router supervision via weighting gates is a useful idea for MoE expert prefetching and shows solid results over pre-routed baselines.
mOZfmdlbJD.main_concern: Reviewers question whether gains over hidden-routed baselines stem from partial parameter reuse rather than pre-routing, noting missing matched-reuse/compute controls, single-scale evaluation, and missing head-to-head timing comparisons.

jIdwjAUN0r.one_liner: Replaces layer-private MoE experts with cross-layer shared Meta Experts to reduce redundancy and parameter storage.
jIdwjAUN0r.problem: Mainstream hierarchical MoE architectures store layer-private experts that exhibit substantial cross-layer similarity and parameter redundancy.
jIdwjAUN0r.method: The authors propose Meta Experts shared across layers alongside Local Experts, systematically exploring sharing ratios, boundary-layer privacy, and sub-pool partitioning. They also analyze cross-layer sharing theoretically as creating flexible residual pathways for information retrieval.
jIdwjAUN0r.key_idea: Shares a pool of Meta Experts across Transformer layers (while keeping boundary layers private) to eliminate cross-layer expert redundancy.
jIdwjAUN0r.evidence: Multi-dimensional empirical comparison across four training scales (up to 200B tokens) with controlled activation counts, parameter-reduction experiments, similarity analyses, and six downstream benchmarks.
jIdwjAUN0r.claimed_gains: With activated expert quantity and granularity held fixed, the Meta Expert model matches Vanilla MoE performance using only 70% of the experts.
jIdwjAUN0r.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the systematic architectural exploration of Meta/Local ratios, boundary-layer treatment, and sub-pool organization under controlled activation budgets.
jIdwjAUN0r.main_concern: Reviewers note missing real-world throughput/latency/communication measurements, unverified cross-layer routing heatmaps, and weak empirical/theoretical support for the 'bidirectional residual pathway' claim.

al4nZlLNE8.one_liner: Solves low-rank matrix and tensor single-index bandits with unknown Lipschitz links via rank-adaptive Stein estimation.
al4nZlLNE8.problem: Low-rank matrix/tensor bandits typically assume known reward links, whereas single-index bandits with unknown links do not exploit low-rank structure.
al4nZlLNE8.method: For monotone links, T-ESTOR combines robust, rank-adaptive Stein estimation with epoch-based greedy arm selection; for nonmonotone links, T-BSTOR pairs structured estimation with robust bin-based learning. The authors prove matching upper and lower regret bounds under regular candidate distributions and finite-variance noise.
al4nZlLNE8.key_idea: Combines rank-adaptive low-rank Stein estimation with epoch-based greedy selection (monotone) or bin-based learning (nonmonotone) to exploit low-rank structure under unknown link functions.
al4nZlLNE8.evidence: Upper and lower regret theorems for monotone and nonmonotone settings, plus synthetic and CCLE-based experiments against vectorized and single-index baselines.
al4nZlLNE8.claimed_gains: T-ESTOR achieves square-root regret matching the monotone lower bound up to logarithmic factors in rank, dimension, and horizon, while T-BSTOR attains the optimal O~(T^{2/3}) horizon rate for nonmonotone links.
al4nZlLNE8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the rigorous regret analysis exploiting low-rank structure without knowing the link function or rank, and the careful treatment of adaptive arm-selection distribution shift.
al4nZlLNE8.main_concern: Reviewers point out strong oracle assumptions requiring known candidate distributions, exact selected Stein scores, and a uniformly positive Stein signal that are difficult to compute or certify in practice.

zIqMGRBb6a.one_liner: Compares physics-informed input features against loss regularization for probabilistic solar forecasting under leakage-free distribution shift.
zIqMGRBb6a.problem: It remains unclear whether incorporating physical knowledge as input representations or as training-time regularization provides stronger predictive and OOD gains.
zIqMGRBb6a.method: The authors evaluate physics-informed input features versus training-time constraint penalties under matched-capacity controls across multiple forecast horizons and held-out campuses. After auditing and removing future-observation leakage in gap-filling, they re-run leakage-free experiments and redesign an inactive nighttime penalty.
zIqMGRBb6a.key_idea: Contrasts physics-based input representations against output loss penalties under matched capacity, leakage-free preprocessing, and cross-campus distribution-shift evaluation.
zIqMGRBb6a.evidence: Multi-seed experiments across 42 solar inverters on five campuses at 15-minute, 1-hour, and 4-hour horizons with leakage audits and independent-dataset replication.
zIqMGRBb6a.claimed_gains: Under leakage-free evaluation, physics-informed inputs change CRPS by -0.55% (95% CI [-1.87, +3.16]) at 1 hour, -0.40% ([-1.47, +0.26]) at 15 minutes, and -3.93% ([-7.29, -0.70]) at 4 hours, while regularization offers limited predictive benefit.
zIqMGRBb6a.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the careful, transparent statistical methodology, campus-level inference, leakage audit, and controlled separation of representation versus regularization.
zIqMGRBb6a.main_concern: Reviewers note that the regularization baseline barely activates (nearly zero training violations), continuous features and penalties encode different information, and evaluation is confined to one university climate.

RaErSw2646.one_liner: Adds federated client-conditioned residual experts atop a frozen global model to correct systematic client-dependent logit errors.
RaErSw2646.problem: Frozen shared federated models retain systematic client-dependent errors, yet it is unclear when residual predictive structure exists and can be corrected without updating the deployed model.
RaErSw2646.method: FedCoREx freezes the global model and federatively trains a bank of shared residual experts with a client-conditioned router driven by frozen representations, base probabilities, and local class-conditional confusion contexts. The authors also decompose available post-freeze log-loss gains into sample-only misspecification and client-conditioned information.
RaErSw2646.key_idea: Routes a bank of globally shared logit-correction experts using frozen features, base probabilities, and local class-conditional confusion contexts while keeping the base model frozen.
RaErSw2646.evidence: Log-loss decomposition theory and experiments on four datasets including controlled visual concept shifts, FEMNIST, and Sentiment140.
RaErSw2646.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the well-motivated frozen-base correction setting, local context privacy, zero-output initialization, and paired-checkpoint controls.
RaErSw2646.main_concern: Reviewers note that large gains occur mainly on synthetic concept shifts with modest or near-zero gains on FEMNIST and Sentiment140, and that controls do not isolate the benefit of expert routing over a single context-conditioned residual model.

UNbFiikjJ0.one_liner: Combines learned static/dynamic 4D point-cloud segmentation with attentive test-time training memory for feedforward dynamic novel-view synthesis.
