UNbFiikjJ0.problem: Feedforward dynamic novel-view synthesis methods face a trade-off: explicit 3D representations lose fidelity from geometry errors, while implicit renderers lack multi-view consistency.
UNbFiikjJ0.method: GG4D separates static and dynamic regions without off-the-shelf optical flow or segmentation models to build a 4D point cloud that provides explicit geometric guidance. It then renders target views in real time using Large Chunk Attentive Test-Time Training (LaCAT), which encodes observations into a fast-weight scene memory.
UNbFiikjJ0.key_idea: Guides an implicit fast-weight test-time-training renderer (LaCAT) with an explicit 4D point cloud built from learned static-dynamic segmentation.
UNbFiikjJ0.evidence: Evaluated on monocular and multi-view dynamic novel-view synthesis benchmarks including DyCheck and Neural3D across rendering quality, MEt3R consistency, camera-pose, and resolution settings.
UNbFiikjJ0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that GG4D achieves strong empirical rendering quality and multi-view consistency gains (e.g., ~3.6 dB on DyCheck, ~2.6 dB on Neural3D) with efficient post-construction rendering.
UNbFiikjJ0.main_concern: Reviewers highlight a complex multi-stage pipeline with strong dependence on an external geometry backbone, insufficient sensitivity analysis of the segmentation module, and missing comparisons to closely related motion-segmentation works like Easi3R and DAS3R.

qER0ECtkAL.one_liner: Dynamically selects instruction-tuning data by refreshing layer-wise PCA geometric references from current model forward passes without a curated reference set.
qER0ECtkAL.problem: Dynamic instruction-data selectors must adapt ranking criteria as the model evolves without incurring the high cost of training a separate selection policy or relying on curated reference sets.
qER0ECtkAL.method: ReGIFT estimates layer-wise principal directions from a small uniform probe of the training pool at each refresh and uses them to adjust loss-entropy rankings via candidate hidden states reused from existing scoring forward passes. The authors bound reference drift between refreshes using Davis-Kahan perturbation analysis.
qER0ECtkAL.key_idea: Refreshes pool-derived PCA principal directions from current model hidden states and reuses scoring forward passes to geometrically adjust loss-entropy data rankings.
qER0ECtkAL.evidence: Davis-Kahan stability analysis plus instruction-tuning experiments selecting 10% of the pool per refresh across an eight-task benchmark compared against full-data fine-tuning and RL-based Data Agent.
qER0ECtkAL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that reusing scoring forward passes without training a separate selection policy makes ReGIFT practically simpler and faster than RL-based Data Agent while improving task averages.
qER0ECtkAL.main_concern: All three reviewers note that ReGIFT's geometric alignment score is almost fully predictable from sequence length (R² = 0.991–0.992), making the unique value of the geometry beyond length selection unclear.

HHwx5u260Q.one_liner: Certifies individual and collective feature necessity under inexact multi-label supervision via counterfactual deletion over a strongly convex Rashomon set.
HHwx5u260Q.problem: Feature selection methods under ambiguous multi-label supervision return a single sparse support, which cannot certify whether selected features are necessary across all near-optimal predictors.
HHwx5u260Q.method: The authors define individual necessity and collective non-removability via counterfactual feature deletion and re-optimization over the near-optimal predictor family. They instantiate this with a strongly convex ambiguity-aware row-sparse objective, deriving safe deletion-cost bounds for screening and structured search.
HHwx5u260Q.key_idea: Formulates feature necessity over near-optimal predictors via counterfactual feature deletion costs bounded using strong convexity of an ambiguity-aware set-valued multi-label objective.
HHwx5u260Q.evidence: Theoretical bounds on optimization error and deletion costs validated on controlled synthetic and real-world multi-label datasets (including Mediamill and HumanPseAAC).
HHwx5u260Q.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that certifying feature necessity across near-optimal predictors under set-valued multi-label supervision is an interesting, theoretically principled formulation.
HHwx5u260Q.main_concern: Reviewers note weak empirical validation and unablated predictive gains—when no features are certified necessary, the ranking reduces identically to the single base solution's row norms—alongside unclear novelty framing.

rGsLpbw7un.one_liner: Improves LLM forecasting by iteratively revising an explicit belief state with incoming evidence to direct follow-up research and calibrated aggregation.
rGsLpbw7un.problem: Forecasting agents typically dump all retrieved evidence into a single context after search finishes, underusing the evidence and yielding higher Brier loss.
rGsLpbw7un.method: BRIEF initializes an explicit belief state from multi-perspective research, iteratively updates it under a Bayesian-inspired revision rule as new evidence arrives, and uses unresolved gaps and conflicts to guide subsequent search. A final refinement stage aggregates candidate judgments with calibration and target-specific structural adjustments.
rGsLpbw7un.key_idea: Maintains and iteratively revises an explicit belief state as evidence arrives, using its unresolved conflicts to direct further retrieval before calibrated judgment aggregation.
rGsLpbw7un.evidence: Controlled fixed-corpus ablation plus evaluations against twelve baselines across FutureX, ForecastBench, and Prophet Arena over three runs.
rGsLpbw7un.claimed_gains: On a fixed corpus, revising an explicit belief lowers Brier loss from 19.34 (all-at-once) and 18.13 (rounds) to 16.52; against the strongest baseline, BRIEF improves FutureX by 7.86 points and reduces ForecastBench Brier loss by 5.3%.
rGsLpbw7un.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that studying evidence utilization in forecasting is relevant and that BRIEF achieves strong, low-variance results across three major benchmarks.
rGsLpbw7un.main_concern: Multiple reviewers consider the method incremental relative to closely related belief-state forecasting work (specifically BLF) and note that main benchmark comparisons do not control for retrieval differences.

Y8BL9P7KOq.one_liner: Benchmarks general-purpose agents on direct embodied robot manipulation via an interactive interface for observation selection, tool use, and native actions.
Y8BL9P7KOq.problem: It remains unclear whether general-purpose agents' planning, tool-use, and feedback-revision skills transfer from digital environments to direct embodied robot manipulation.
Y8BL9P7KOq.method: LIBERO-Agent wraps 200 manipulation tasks—and a 30-task primary suite spanning perception, short-horizon execution, and long-horizon composition—in an agent-native interactive interface. Agents choose observations to inspect, process them with their own tools, and issue native robot action commands rather than fixed scripts or high-level skills.
Y8BL9P7KOq.key_idea: Exposes robotic manipulation tasks through an agent-native interactive interface where general-purpose agents actively select observations, run tools, and issue low-level actions.
Y8BL9P7KOq.evidence: Evaluates frontier agents (including GPT-6 Astra) on the 30-task primary suite with three repetitions per task, plus observation and demonstration ablations.
Y8BL9P7KOq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the agent-native observation and action interface is a clean, well-written setting for diagnosing execution and contact bottlenecks in embodied agents.
Y8BL9P7KOq.main_concern: Reviewers point out that evaluating only 30 tasks with one fixed initial scene lacks statistical robustness and reference VLA/planning baselines, and question the benchmark's added value over existing LIBERO variants.

eTQM22BeeX.one_liner: Strengthens federated model poisoning by concentrating base-attack perturbations into Shapley-ranked parameter blocks scaled within an adaptive Euclidean radius.
eTQM22BeeX.problem: Byzantine-robust federated aggregators inspect complete model updates, creating a granularity mismatch that lets compact malicious subspace perturbations evade detection.
eTQM22BeeX.method: GRASP is an attack-agnostic wrapper that ranks parameter blocks using a scalable second-order Shapley approximation capturing individual and cooperative layer effects without enumerating coalitions. It concentrates a base attack's perturbation into top-ranked blocks, injects it into a reference update, and scales it to the maximum adaptive Euclidean radius.
eTQM22BeeX.key_idea: Uses a second-order Shapley approximation to select influential parameter blocks and scales base poisoning residuals inside an adaptive Euclidean norm bound to evade whole-update defenses.
eTQM22BeeX.evidence: Evaluated across five poisoning strategies and nine Byzantine-robust defenses on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and CIFAR-10, with theoretical scale selection and block-selection ablations.
eTQM22BeeX.claimed_gains: GRASP outperforms the base attack in 85 of 95 settings (89.5%), raises average Attack Impact from 22.17 to 33.02 points, and increases malicious admission under FLAME (40% malicious) from 28.09% to 99.80%.
eTQM22BeeX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the granularity-mismatch framing, Shapley-guided block selection, and attack-agnostic plug-and-play formulation are clean and substantially boost poisoning impact.
eTQM22BeeX.main_concern: Reviewers note reliance on a strong omniscient-adversary threat model, missing evaluations against coordinate-wise defenses (CWTM/CWMed) and pre-aggregation (NNM/bucketing), and small vision datasets.

AEUWZSiYx6.one_liner: Improves 4D Gaussian Splatting densification by localizing under-reconstructed regions via pixel errors and regulating growth with temporal gradient-direction consistency.
AEUWZSiYx6.problem: Existing 4D Gaussian Splatting densification strategies over-populate well-reconstructed regions and ignore temporal gradient consistency, inflating storage and hurting dynamic scene quality.
AEUWZSiYx6.method: ELGD-GS introduces error-guided Gaussian localization that tracks pixel-wise photometric residuals and high-frequency structural discrepancies over time to restrict densification to under-reconstructed regions. It pairs this with gradient consistency-aware density control that splits Gaussians experiencing conflicting temporal gradients while suppressing growth where gradients are directionally consistent.
AEUWZSiYx6.key_idea: Restricts 4D Gaussian densification to high-error pixels and uses temporal gradient-direction consistency to trigger splitting on conflicting gradients while suppressing redundant growth.
AEUWZSiYx6.evidence: Evaluated on three dynamic scene datasets atop the TAD-GS backbone, reporting PSNR (including dynamic-only regions), SSIM, LPIPS, primitive count, and storage.
AEUWZSiYx6.claimed_gains: Achieves comparable or better reconstruction quality with nearly 50% fewer Gaussians.
AEUWZSiYx6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the densification diagnosis is clear and that integrating error-guided localization and gradient consistency halves primitive counts while improving quality on TAD-GS.
AEUWZSiYx6.main_concern: Reviewers note that headline storage savings are confounded by a 3D hash table absent from the baseline, and that novelty over adapting static-3DGS GDAGS to TAD-GS is insufficiently isolated.

6DKekJZxpN.one_liner: Mitigates multi-modal clustering conflicts by decomposing graphs into edge-disjoint neighborhoods ranked by cross-modal edge frequency.
6DKekJZxpN.problem: Modality-specific noise and topological inconsistencies create conflicting neighborhood graphs that degrade multi-modal clustering.
6DKekJZxpN.method: The authors decompose multi-modal kNN graphs into edge-disjoint subgraphs stratified by cross-modal edge frequency, treating edges recurring across more modalities as more reliable. They introduce a structure alignment objective enforcing hierarchical ordering in the joint representation and prove it minimizes an upper bound on the k-means cost.
6DKekJZxpN.key_idea: Stratifies multi-modal kNN edges into disjoint frequency-ordered neighborhoods and trains joint representations with a ranking alignment loss that upper-bounds k-means cost.
6DKekJZxpN.evidence: Theoretical upper bounds on the alignment loss and k-means cost plus experiments on multiple multi-modal clustering benchmarks across two task families.
6DKekJZxpN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that stratifying neighborhood graphs by cross-modal edge frequency is a simple, intuitive, and lightweight way to handle modality conflicts.
6DKekJZxpN.main_concern: Reviewers question the unvalidated assumption that high cross-modal edge frequency implies semantic reliability—especially under shared noise or unequal modality quality—alongside sensitivity to hard kNN cutoffs and proof issues.

d7bZVSos27.one_liner: Jointly optimizes a shared LLM policy's experience extractor and solver via RL using downstream skill-evaluation trajectories (Evolving-RL).
d7bZVSos27.problem: Self-evolving LLM agents rely on fixed system prompts or optimize solver and memory extraction separately rather than co-evolving both capabilities end to end.
d7bZVSos27.method: The authors propose Evolving-RL, which uses a single policy to extract candidate skills from past interactions and evaluate them on target tasks. Supervisory signals from these evaluation rollouts are reused to optimize both the extractor and solver via GRPO in coordinated co-evolution.
d7bZVSos27.key_idea: Co-trains a shared agent policy as both experience extractor and solver by reusing downstream task-evaluation rollouts to score candidate skills via GRPO.
d7bZVSos27.evidence: Experiments on ALFWorld, ScienceWorld, and Mind2Web (including 3B and 7B models) with objective ablations, skill-relevance tests, and cross-policy skill transfer.
d7bZVSos27.claimed_gains: Under the same skill-conditioned protocol, achieves 98.7% relative improvement over GRPO on unseen ALFWorld tasks, 35.8% overall action accuracy on Mind2Web, and a 6.3-point OOD score gain on ScienceWorld.
d7bZVSos27.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree reusing evaluation rollouts to co-optimize experience extraction and utilization is a clean, well-posed training signal.
d7bZVSos27.main_concern: Reviewers note missing baselines (Complementary RL, Skill1), OOD test-time environmental feedback leaking evaluation info, and that most ALFWorld gains come from the base policy without skills.

QE2xMXlVAP.one_liner: Generates RNA sequences across imbalanced Rfam families using a discrete flow-matching DiT with taxonomy-following nested classifier-free guidance.
QE2xMXlVAP.problem: RNA family generators either train one model per family or condition flatly on family tags, degrading badly on small and medium Rfam families.
QE2xMXlVAP.method: The authors propose RfamFlow, a Diffusion Transformer trained with conditional discrete flow matching on Rfam family tags without structural inputs. It introduces nested classifier-free guidance aligned with the Rfam taxonomic hierarchy so data-poor families borrow priors from coarser levels, while supporting masked reconstruction and zero-shot fitness prediction.
QE2xMXlVAP.key_idea: Combines discrete flow matching on a DiT with hierarchical nested classifier-free guidance along the Rfam taxonomy to share priors across imbalanced RNA families.
QE2xMXlVAP.evidence: Evaluations across 100 large, 100 medium, and 100 small Rfam families against RfamLlama and flat CFG, plus masked reconstruction and zero-shot fitness prediction benchmarks.
QE2xMXlVAP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree addressing imbalanced RNA families with a single hierarchically guided model is valuable and nested CFG improves small-family bit scores over flat CFG.
QE2xMXlVAP.main_concern: Reviewers cite missing novelty/diversity and wet-lab functional validation beyond cmsearch, unproven claims about coarser taxonomic priors, limited novelty, and dependence on known Rfam taxonomy.

5rQP6FA4Jr.one_liner: Uses a criticality world model to target failure-prone scenarios, correct collection bias via weighted resampling, and gate specialist/nominal embodied policies.
5rQP6FA4Jr.problem: Embodied policy fine-tuning plateaus because uniform scenario sampling rarely encounters remaining failure cases, while naive specialist training harms nominal performance.
5rQP6FA4Jr.method: The authors propose a recursive self-improvement loop for RL and behavior cloning: execution outcomes train a criticality world model that prioritizes high-risk scenarios for specialist fine-tuning, weighted resampling corrects collection bias, and a risk-based gate switches between the specialist and a frozen nominal policy at inference.
5rQP6FA4Jr.key_idea: Recursively trains a criticality model to sample failure-prone scenarios with inverse-proposal resampling and risk-gates between specialist and frozen nominal policies.
5rQP6FA4Jr.evidence: Sampling-bias analysis and evaluations across five embodied domains spanning RL locomotion/manipulation (Go2, ManiSkill) and BC/VLA benchmarks.
5rQP6FA4Jr.claimed_gains: Reduces failure rates by 59-67% for locomotion and manipulation and 8-25% for VLA benchmarks relative to respective baselines.
5rQP6FA4Jr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the criticality-guided loop with bias-corrected resampling and nominal gating is coherent, practically relevant, and covers diverse RL and BC/VLA domains.
5rQP6FA4Jr.main_concern: Reviewers note that the independent contributions of inverse-proposal resampling and recursive predictor updates are not ablated separately, and demonstration-curation baselines like CUPID are missing.

aMSPtOTaKt.one_liner: Refines full-atom peptide binders at test time by scoring candidates with Rosetta and sequentially re-noising only high-energy residues via Diffusion Forcing.
aMSPtOTaKt.problem: Parallel test-time sampling for peptide binder design wastes compute on poor candidates and ignores per-residue binding energy signals.
aMSPtOTaKt.method: The authors propose E-TTR, which post-trains peptide denoisers with Diffusion Forcing to support per-residue timesteps. At inference, Rosetta scores an initial pool and decomposes per-residue binding energy; subsequent rounds re-noise and denoise only high-energy residues of the best candidate within a fixed sample budget.
aMSPtOTaKt.key_idea: Post-trains peptide diffusion models with per-residue Diffusion Forcing timesteps and iteratively re-noises only Rosetta-identified high-energy residues at test time.
aMSPtOTaKt.evidence: Evaluations across three peptide-design benchmarks and two generative backbones with ablations separating Diffusion Forcing post-training and energy-guided selection.
aMSPtOTaKt.claimed_gains: Outperforms competing test-time scaling strategies in binding affinity and success rate with up to 28% lower binding energy at matched sampling budgets.
aMSPtOTaKt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree residue-level energy-guided test-time search is intuitive, clearly written, and supported by ablations isolating selection and post-training effects.
aMSPtOTaKt.main_concern: Reviewers flag circularity from using Rosetta both to guide search and to evaluate binding success without non-Rosetta metrics, alongside unreported wall-clock latency of sequential rounds and flawed diversity accounting.

aaccELMJJD.one_liner: Represents irregular time-series patches as closed-form weighted local-linear level and slope estimators inside an Adaptive Kernel Patching forecaster.
aaccELMJJD.problem: Geometry-weighted mean patch representations for irregular time series incur first-order level bias proportional to local slope under asymmetric observation timestamps.
aaccELMJJD.method: The authors replace mean patch aggregation with a closed-form weighted local-linear estimator of level and slope that preserves second-order bias. They embed it into Adaptive Kernel Patching (AKP) with sample-conditioned soft supports, support-mass-gated aggregation, and cross-variable mixing.
aaccELMJJD.key_idea: Computes each irregular time-series patch as a closed-form weighted local-linear regression of level and slope using timestamps and support weights.
aaccELMJJD.evidence: Bias theory and evaluations against 17 Optuna-tuned baselines over five runs on irregular time-series datasets (including P12, MIMIC-III, USHCN), plus backbone-swap ablations.
aaccELMJJD.claimed_gains: Lowers MSE and MAE on all eight dataset-metric pairs when swapped into PatchTST and APN; AKP achieves best mean on five of eight pairs and improves USHCN MSE/MAE by 4.0%/17.4% over the strongest competitor.
aaccELMJJD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the local-linear perspective on irregular patch representation is theoretically grounded, clearly written, and well isolated across backbones.
aaccELMJJD.main_concern: Reviewers point out that learned supports often span nearly the entire history (weakening the local-fitting interpretation), theoretical non-degeneracy conditions fail clinically, and long horizons are untested.

HjU9lEXJDa.one_liner: Estimates robot task progress without reward-model training using a VLM subagent-primary agent workflow with adaptive visual inspection and cross-agent verification.
HjU9lEXJDa.problem: Existing progress reward models for robot learning often assign spurious progress to failed attempts or wrong-object interactions.
HjU9lEXJDa.method: The authors propose the Agentic Reward System (ARS), a training-free offline inference framework using a 27B general-purpose VLM. A subagent adaptively inspects frames to propose a task-relevant event timeline, which a primary agent verifies and revises before estimating per-frame progress or auditing external reward models.
HjU9lEXJDa.key_idea: Uses two general-purpose VLM agents with adaptive frame inspection to propose, verify, and revise event timelines for training-free per-frame progress estimation.
HjU9lEXJDa.evidence: Evaluations with a 27B VLM on a controlled semantic-mismatch benchmark, LIBERO-Long simulation policy learning, ablations, and real-robot multi-screw fastening.
HjU9lEXJDa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the semantic-mismatch analysis is revealing and ARS improves downstream simulation policy learning over evaluated reward baselines without reward-model training.
HjU9lEXJDa.main_concern: Reviewers raise fairness and compute concerns comparing an expensive offline non-causal 27B VLM pipeline against single-pass online reward models, plus missing real-robot baselines and low Pi0.5 baseline numbers.

rRxWDAkJLt.one_liner: Trains LLM knowledge-graph extractors via RL using per-chunk semantic coverage and marginal-contribution compactness rewards (CoverKG).
rRxWDAkJLt.problem: Supervising graph-RAG LLM extractors solely with sparse downstream QA accuracy cannot distinguish missing semantic coverage from redundant graph extractions.
rRxWDAkJLt.method: The authors propose CoverKG, which scores each chunk's extracted graph at construction time without QA labels or gold graphs. A coverage reward aligns source sentences to extracted elements, a compactness reward scores each element's marginal contribution, and their composite drives RL policy optimization.
rRxWDAkJLt.key_idea: Optimizes LLM knowledge-graph extractors via RL using construction-time sentence-alignment coverage and leave-one-out marginal compactness rewards.
rRxWDAkJLt.evidence: Experiments across three graph-based RAG retrieval backends and multiple QA benchmarks measuring QA accuracy and index compactness.
rRxWDAkJLt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree label-free per-chunk rewards for graph-RAG extraction are practically valuable and shrink index sizes while improving QA performance.
rRxWDAkJLt.main_concern: Two reviewers construct explicit counterexamples proving the compactness reward can actually increase when redundant elements are added, and another notes the reward ignores graph relational structure.

EqBQXvE1X0.one_liner: Forecasts time series by separating scale-shared features via Product-of-Experts and minimizing pairwise mutual-information upper bounds across scales (MDN).
EqBQXvE1X0.problem: Multi-scale time-series forecasters model interactions across entangled features where non-linear cross-scale entanglement and scale-shared information interfere.
EqBQXvE1X0.method: The authors propose the Multi-scale Disentanglement Network (MDN), which infers and subtracts a scale-shared feature via a Product-of-Experts module and applies a training-only CLUB mutual-information upper-bound penalty across scale residuals. It then sequentially models intra-scale and inter-scale interactions.
EqBQXvE1X0.key_idea: Removes a Product-of-Experts scale-shared component and minimizes pairwise CLUB mutual-information upper bounds across residual scales before modeling interactions.
EqBQXvE1X0.evidence: Experiments on 7 real-world time-series datasets against 14 baselines, plus component ablations, seed-stability checks, and inference-cost analysis.
EqBQXvE1X0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree MDN is clearly specified, lightweight at inference once training-only CLUB estimators are removed, and achieves broad MAE gains across seven datasets.
EqBQXvE1X0.main_concern: Reviewers argue the semantic disentanglement claim is unsubstantiated—lacking identifiability or ground-truth factor tests—and that minimizing pairwise MI can suppress valid cross-scale dependencies.

udUQaoRekf.one_liner: Augments evolutionary LLM coding agents by mining high-level causal idea factors from scored program pairs to guide bandit-controlled exploration and exploitation.
udUQaoRekf.problem: Evolutionary LLM coding agents mutate programs via low-level surface heuristics without persistent high-level idea control.
udUQaoRekf.method: The authors propose ExpEvolve, which models program discovery via a structural causal framework and extracts high-level idea factors explaining score differences between programs. These factors guide bandit-controlled exploitation of successful ideas and exploration when discovery plateaus.
udUQaoRekf.key_idea: Extracts high-level idea factors from misranked program pairs to steer evolutionary LLM mutations with bandit-controlled exploitation and plateau exploration.
udUQaoRekf.evidence: Sample-efficiency theory and experiments on 11 open-ended math tasks, transfer to 4 additional LLMs, and 6 ML tasks from MLS-Bench.
udUQaoRekf.claimed_gains: Improves final performance and increases sample efficiency by 3.5x on average across 11 open-ended mathematical tasks.
udUQaoRekf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree formalizing evolutionary discovery with causal idea factors is an interesting, inspectable alternative to raw program reuse with consistent matched-evaluation gains.
udUQaoRekf.main_concern: Reviewers note missing component ablations (several top speedups occur during warm-up before factor extraction acts), omitted memory-extraction baselines, and unmatched token/FLOP budgets.

jCPAQnMevP.one_liner: Allocates external-state monitoring queries for stored agent intentions using learned static value scoring or DP-distilled sequential timing policies (BudgetPM).
jCPAQnMevP.problem: Long-running agents with multiple stored intentions must decide which shared external resources to query now versus reserving observation budget for later.
jCPAQnMevP.method: The authors formulate budgeted prospective-memory monitoring as query allocation and propose BudgetPM with two lightweight policies: Static learns immediate check value, while Sequential distills query timing from offline dynamic-programming schedules over complete episodes.
jCPAQnMevP.key_idea: Distills offline dynamic-programming monitoring schedules into a lightweight policy (BudgetPM) that budgets external-state checks across stored agent intentions.
jCPAQnMevP.evidence: Evaluations on PM-Bench, GoodAI, and SentinelBench-derived tasks with matched controls, budget sweeps, exact-cost decompositions, and paired bootstrap tests.
jCPAQnMevP.claimed_gains: Static preserves 99.9-100% of unconstrained Set F1 with 42-54% fewer queries; Sequential saves 9-17% of queries on PM-Bench and 5-18% on SentinelBench-derived tasks over Pacing-LB at matched performance.
jCPAQnMevP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the controlled attribution methodology is rigorous, online overhead is low, and the paper clearly delineates when future-aware allocation helps.
jCPAQnMevP.main_concern: Reviewers note limited algorithmic novelty, missing comparisons to cited budget-aware tool-use methods (e.g., When2Tool, BATS), and that scarcity results rest primarily on PM-Bench.

EhCji21y1V.one_liner: Mitigates directional cancellation in federated LoRA via local trainable magnitudes, row-wise coherence gating, and global-product angular regularization (FedCoDi).
EhCji21y1V.problem: Heterogeneous client LoRA updates point in conflicting directions and partially cancel under federated averaging, while forcing uniform directions harms personalization.
EhCji21y1V.method: The authors propose FedCoDi, which decomposes adapters into local trainable magnitudes and shared low-rank factors. Clients blend broadcast and local factors via a row-wise coherence gate and regularize angular disagreement between the local and global low-rank products while the server uses standard factor-wise averaging.
EhCji21y1V.key_idea: Keeps adapter magnitudes local while using row-wise directional coherence gating and product-level angular regularization on clients to balance global sharing and personalization.
EhCji21y1V.evidence: Directional-cancellation analysis and experiments with RoBERTa-large and Llama-3-8B on four GLUE tasks, GSM8K, and Dolly-15K against six federated LoRA baselines.
EhCji21y1V.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the directional-cancellation motivation is well grounded and FedCoDi consistently outperforms evaluated federated LoRA baselines across GLUE and GSM8K.
EhCji21y1V.main_concern: Reviewers flag unfair comparison against non-personalized or lower-parameter baselines due to local trainable magnitudes, missing fixed-ratio mixing ablations, and unresolved factor-wise server averaging mismatch.

1iMzVsYTtX.one_liner: Builds a training-free streaming action tokenizer (ActionCodec2) from optimal group-covering motion primitives compressed losslessly with Set-BPE.
1iMzVsYTtX.problem: Chunkwise VLA action tokenizers delay robot reactions until chunk boundaries, while existing streaming tokenizers use high token rates or accumulate trajectory drift.
1iMzVsYTtX.method: The authors cast minimum-rate bounded-error streaming tokenization as a group covering problem, deriving optimal fixed motion primitives (exact for translation, constant-factor tight for orientation). ActionCodec2 then compresses primitive streams losslessly with Set-BPE over unordered sets without gradient training.
1iMzVsYTtX.key_idea: Pairs provably optimal bounded-error motion primitives from group covering with lossless Set-BPE compression to form a gradient-free streaming action tokenizer.
1iMzVsYTtX.evidence: Covering-optimality proofs, fitting on 20k hours from 24 embodiments, and same-backbone VLA evaluations on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, SimplerEnv, PPO fine-tuning, and real robots.
1iMzVsYTtX.claimed_gains: Encodes 1 second of 15 Hz motion in 8.8-10.8 tokens on average and outperforms compared tokenizers on LIBERO (98.2%) and LIBERO-Plus (79.5%).
1iMzVsYTtX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the bounded-error streaming tokenization problem is well motivated and controlled multi-benchmark evaluations show consistent gains without gradient training.
1iMzVsYTtX.main_concern: Reviewers find the dense mathematical presentation hard to follow without intuitive examples, and note that streaming closed-loop reactivity benefits are weakly tested and omit streaming baselines like BEAST.

FpoWUQ1E5i.one_liner: Detects depression from EEG by learning healthy generative velocity fields and calibrating trajectory deviations against locally matched healthy references (BrainFlow).
FpoWUQ1E5i.problem: Discriminative EEG depression classifiers entangle disease signals with inter-subject and cohort variability, hurting subject-independent generalization.
FpoWUQ1E5i.method: The authors propose BrainFlow, which learns generative velocity fields over healthy EEG features as a normative reference. To handle individual residuals, Trajectory Deviation compares unseen subjects against locally matched healthy trajectories and calibrates corrected transport residuals into Flow-Energy features for supervised classification.
FpoWUQ1E5i.key_idea: Learns a healthy EEG feature velocity field and calibrates each subject's transport residuals against locally matched healthy reference trajectories into Flow-Energy descriptors.
FpoWUQ1E5i.evidence: Subject-independent EEG depression detection experiments across heterogeneous cohorts using 170 handcrafted connectivity and node-strength features.
FpoWUQ1E5i.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree reframing depression detection as locally calibrated deviation from a normative healthy reference thoughtfully addresses inter-subject EEG variability.
FpoWUQ1E5i.main_concern: Reviewers question the necessity and validation of velocity fields trained on only 472 healthy feature vectors, reliance on handcrafted EEG features, pipeline complexity, and overlap with prior relative flow-mismatch work.

ut4YjlISHu.one_liner: Unifies spatio-temporal forecasting, interpolation, extrapolation, and imputation using a two-stage latent neural field encoder and conditional residual latent diffusion (FieldDiff).
ut4YjlISHu.problem: Spatio-temporal foundation models must handle heterogeneous spatial geometries, resolutions, and multi-task uncertainty under partial observations.
ut4YjlISHu.method: The authors propose FieldDiff, a two-stage latent neural field diffusion framework. Stage one encodes values and physical coordinates into a variationally regularized latent field via globally shared and geometry-adaptive tokens; stage two treats four spatio-temporal tasks as conditional generation using residual latent diffusion.
ut4YjlISHu.key_idea: Encodes arbitrary spatio-temporal coordinates into a unified latent neural field and solves forecasting, interpolation, extrapolation, and imputation via conditional residual latent diffusion.
ut4YjlISHu.evidence: Multi-dataset spatio-temporal experiments covering forecasting, temporal interpolation, spatial extrapolation, imputation, and zero-shot/few-shot cross-domain transfer.
ut4YjlISHu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the continuous neural field formulation cleanly unifies four spatio-temporal tasks and is backed by extensive multi-dataset and transfer experiments.
ut4YjlISHu.main_concern: Reviewers flag that despite emphasizing uncertainty modeling, experiments report only point metrics (MAE/RMSE) with no probabilistic metrics or deterministic-predictor ablation, and omit closely related two-stage neural field literature.

5587Hd95Hb.one_liner: Measures min-max normalized layerwise diffusion reconstruction feature drift (architecture accent) to classify backbone lineages and analyze correction sensitivity.
5587Hd95Hb.problem: How different diffusion architectures internally organize feature discrepancies along reconstruction trajectories is poorly characterized.
5587Hd95Hb.method: The authors define feature drift as the per-layer discrepancy between a reconstruction trajectory and an independently sampled forward reference, and normalize its depth profile as the architecture accent. They evaluate ten model instances across five backbone families alongside norm-free metrics, random-initialization controls, retraining, and correction-site interventions.
5587Hd95Hb.key_idea: Profiles layerwise diffusion reconstruction drift against an independent forward reference to classify architecture-specific depth morphologies and probe correction sites.
5587Hd95Hb.evidence: Controlled registry study of ten diffusion models across five backbone families with leave-one-out classification, norm-free checks, initialization/retraining controls, and editing interventions.
5587Hd95Hb.claimed_gains: Ten model instances across five backbone families fall into two dominant classes (interior-localized and terminal-ramp) recovered in leave-one-out evaluation.
5587Hd95Hb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the measurement protocol is concrete and reproducible, with thoughtful norm-free, initialization, and exact-inversion controls.
5587Hd95Hb.main_concern: Reviewers question the diagnostic value beyond simple feature-norm schedules (which drive terminal ramps and select identical top layers), small registry size (ten models), and strawman 'not noise' framing.

XsIe9rlruK.one_liner: Upgrades BernNet for heterophilic graphs with a learnable scalar spectral warp, smooth-plus-step decomposed regularization, and a node-feature residual bypass.
XsIe9rlruK.problem: Bernstein polynomial spectral GNNs use a fixed frequency grid, apply homogeneous regularization that struggles with sharp transitions, and dilute node features at high orders.
XsIe9rlruK.method: The authors propose BernNetII, adding a single learnable spectral-warping scalar to rescale the Bernstein basis, decomposing filter coefficients into smooth and step components with separate regularizers, and adding a residual bypass. They also prove a Rademacher complexity bound and proximal-gradient convergence.
XsIe9rlruK.key_idea: Adds a scalar spectral warp, smooth-plus-step coefficient decomposition with tailored regularization, and a residual bypass to Bernstein polynomial graph filters.
XsIe9rlruK.evidence: Rademacher complexity and optimization convergence proofs plus node-classification experiments across eight benchmarks.
XsIe9rlruK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the three modifications address clear limitations of BernNet in a simple way backed by theoretical analysis.
XsIe9rlruK.main_concern: Reviewers question whether heterophilic graphs actually need step-like spectral responses, note outdated pre-2022 baselines with modest gains, and point out gaps between the full objective and theoretical analysis.

InH3V8je46.one_liner: Trains open-ended RL policies for web-app generation using human rubrics, hierarchical reasoning rewards, and failure-attributed token weights in GRPO.
InH3V8je46.problem: RL for open-ended generation lacks deterministic verifiers capable of evaluating partially successful outputs and localizing failures for policy updates.
InH3V8je46.method: The authors build an RL training environment combining human domain rubrics with model reasoning to compute hierarchical rewards and diagnose which output regions caused failures. These diagnostic attributions modulate token-level weights in the GRPO objective for interactive web application generation.
InH3V8je46.key_idea: Combines rubric-anchored hierarchical rewards with model-diagnosed failure attributions to reweight per-token updates in GRPO for open-ended web-app generation.
InH3V8je46.evidence: Evaluations on MiniAppBench and ArtifactsBench with component ablations and out-of-distribution capability-preservation checks.
InH3V8je46.claimed_gains: Achieves an average pass rate of 41.25% on MiniAppBench and 76.19% on ArtifactsBench.
InH3V8je46.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the open-ended RL problem is important and the full system delivers substantial pass-rate improvements over SFT on both web-app benchmarks.
InH3V8je46.main_concern: Reviewers note limited novelty beyond rubric-based reward pipelines, unnormalized token weights confounding localization with response-level weighting, and heavy domain-specific web-app engineering.

O4gBeCl59s.one_liner: Aligns reconstruction-free world-model latent states with image embeddings across multiple temporal window lengths using Barlow Twins (TS-Dreamer).
O4gBeCl59s.problem: Single-step latent-to-image alignment in reconstruction-free world models does not explicitly supervise multi-step motion and longer-horizon temporal dynamics.
O4gBeCl59s.method: The authors propose TS-Dreamer, which projects latent states into the image embedding space and applies Barlow Twins alignment both per step and over normalized sums across multiple temporal window lengths. It adds no trainable parameters or inference overhead relative to R2-Dreamer.
O4gBeCl59s.key_idea: Applies Barlow Twins alignment between projected latent states and image embeddings summed over multi-length temporal windows without adding model parameters.
O4gBeCl59s.evidence: Evaluations on 20 DeepMind Control Suite tasks, 26 Atari 100K games, FlappyBird, and linear physical-state and ordered-motion probing experiments.
O4gBeCl59s.claimed_gains: Default two-scale setup gets highest mean and median returns on DMC; adding a four-decision window raises Atari 100K mean human-normalized score by 10.53 percentage points over R2-Dreamer, and up to 32-decision windows yield 4.4x R2-Dreamer score on FlappyBird.
O4gBeCl59s.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the zero-parameter multi-scale alignment loss is simple, cleanly compared against R2-Dreamer, and evaluated across broad continuous and discrete benchmarks.
O4gBeCl59s.main_concern: Reviewers note marginal or inconsistent default-scale gains on DMC/Atari without paired confidence intervals, post-hoc window selection, and that window summation is permutation-invariant (ignoring temporal order).

Vnr0XKqWoY.one_liner: Reconstructs client training images passively from a single uploaded federated weighted Convolutional Tsetlin Machine by inverting memorized clause patches.
Vnr0XKqWoY.problem: Federated weighted Convolutional Tsetlin Machines appear privacy-preserving because data stay local, yet their interpretable pixel-level clauses can memorize sparse non-IID classes.
Vnr0XKqWoY.method: The authors introduce a passive server-side reconstruction attack requiring no gradients, auxiliary data, or protocol manipulation. From one uploaded model, it analyzes clause conflicts to estimate per-class sample counts, assigns clauses to samples, and spatially reassembles learned patches into original images.
Vnr0XKqWoY.key_idea: Inverts a single uploaded federated wCTM model by estimating sample counts via clause conflicts and spatially reassembling memorized pixel-level clause patches.
Vnr0XKqWoY.evidence: Multi-metric reconstruction experiments across five image benchmarks under non-IID federated heterogeneity, evaluating Matching F1, Hamming distance, and visual examples.
Vnr0XKqWoY.claimed_gains: Recovers up to 95% of heterogeneity-exposed training images (client classes with at most five samples) across five benchmarks.
Vnr0XKqWoY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper uncovers a genuine, model-specific privacy attack surface for discrete Tsetlin Machines without needing gradients or protocol tampering.
Vnr0XKqWoY.main_concern: Reviewers note narrow relevance of wCTMs to mainstream ICLR audiences, Matching F1 lacking a distance threshold to separate true fidelity from nearest-neighbor hits, and simple dataset scope.

g75TND27Jy.one_liner: Benchmarks 15 text representations across six heterogeneous text-attributed graphs and introduces label-free Text-Graph Alignment (TGA) to predict message-passing gains.
g75TND27Jy.problem: Heterogeneous text-attributed graph evaluations typically fix one text encoder, leaving unclear how stronger text features affect homogeneous versus relation-aware graph gains.
g75TND27Jy.method: The authors build MeHTAGs Bench pairing six HTAGs with 15 node representations (90 fixed-split settings) and propose Text-Graph Alignment (TGA). TGA is a label-free, training-free rank statistic comparing cosine similarities of meta-path-connected target pairs against random pairs.
g75TND27Jy.key_idea: Computes label-free Text-Graph Alignment (TGA) by contrasting meta-path-connected versus random node cosine similarities to rank residual homogeneous GNN gains.
g75TND27Jy.evidence: Controlled sweeps across 6 HTAG datasets, 15 node representations (14 text-derived plus random), multiple architectures, 5 seeds, and fixed-weight aggregation probes.
g75TND27Jy.claimed_gains: TGA achieves the strongest absolute rank correlation with residual homogeneous message-passing gains among evaluated label-free statistics on all six HTAGs.
g75TND27Jy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the controlled 90-setting benchmark is systematic and clearly written, and TGA is an interpretable, label-free diagnostic.
g75TND27Jy.main_concern: Reviewers note the findings are more descriptive than explanatory (not explaining why relation-aware gains persist), hold graph structure fixed, and compare raw percentage-point gains across different MLP baselines.

Q3ykX5Drq5.one_liner: CACRNet uses local degradation cues to route multiscale contextual codebook prompts (SCI) and gate shallow skip connections (CAGF) for JPEG restoration.
Q3ykX5Drq5.problem: Blind JPEG restoration suffers from spatially non-uniform artifacts that starve heavily degraded regions of context while leaking artifact-contaminated shallow features through skip connections.
Q3ykX5Drq5.method: CACRNet introduces a Spatial-Channel Interaction (SCI) module that uses local structural and compression-sensitive cues to retrieve prompts from a recursive multiscale Contextual Codebook Bank via factorized spatial attention, alongside a Compression-Aware Gated Fusion (CAGF) module that filters skip features before decoding.
Q3ykX5Drq5.key_idea: Coordinates local degradation cues to retrieve multiscale codebook context prompts (SCI) and gate skip-connection features (CAGF) against JPEG artifacts.
Q3ykX5Drq5.evidence: Evaluated on blind, non-blind, and aligned/misaligned double JPEG restoration benchmarks with module and loss ablations.
Q3ykX5Drq5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find adapting context and skip fusion to local degradation sensible and acknowledge consistent quantitative gains across blind, non-blind, and double JPEG benchmarks.
Q3ykX5Drq5.main_concern: Reviewers argue that experiments do not verify that SCI/CAGF actually respond to JPEG degradation rather than ordinary image structure, lack isolated CCB ablations, and omit recent double-JPEG baselines.
